levels.label: Kids · Beginners

weeks.obj: say hello and goodbye and give their name; follow 3 basic class instructions
weeks.lang: Hello. My name is... Goodbye!; stand up, sit down, look, listen
weeks.act: Hello circle with names; rehearse attention signal; make the rules poster together
weeks.hw: teach the hello song to someone at home

skills.L: Hello song and attention signal - listen and join in (Music/Songs)
skills.S: Greet the class chorally and say my name in the hello circle
skills.R: Match name cards to faces; find letters in my name (Flashcards)
skills.W: Trace and copy my name; help colour the class-rules poster

lp.wu: Name ball toss: teacher models "Hello, I am Miss/Mister X", each child catches, says their name, throws back. Slow pace, big smiles, no pressure to speak perfectly.
wuAlt: Sit in a circle; roll the ball softly to music, stop music, ball-holder says "My name is..."
Puppet introduces itself to each child; children wave and say hello to the puppet
lp.pres: Present hello/goodbye + 4 instructions (stand up, sit down, look, listen) with giant flashcards and exaggerated modelling. Teach the attention signal ("Hands on head... 1, 2, 3, eyes on me!") and rehearse it 5 times as a game.
presAlt: Puppet show: puppet does right and wrong things; class shouts Yes!/No!
Model and mirror: teacher says + does, children copy like mirrors
lp.prac: Simon Says with the 4 instructions, slow then fast. Then drill "Hello, my name is ___" around the circle with the puppet.
pracAlt: Freeze game: instructions to music, freeze when it stops
Line racing: two teams, first to correctly do the instruction wins a point
lp.ls: Listen and do: teacher calls instructions in random order while children respond; add "touch your nose/head" silliness to check listening honestly.
lp.re: Quick hello circle again — count how many children say their name with confidence; celebrate with a class cheer.
lp.prod: Make the Class Rules Poster together: children add handprints / smiley stickers and practise "We look. We listen." Display it on the wall all year.
lp.rw: Table time: trace names on pre-writing sheets (dotted letters), colour a "Hello" badge to wear home. Fast finishers trace "hello" and "goodbye".
lp.st: Hello Song (Music/Songs) with actions, sung twice; teach the Goodbye Song ready for the end of class. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line (teach it this week).
g: Soft ball, catch-say name-throw. Wrong name? Everyone helps kindly.
Only stand up / sit down / look / listen. Remove "Simon says" later weeks.
Puppet greets each child; child answers or waves — any attempt praised.
Music + instructions; freeze when music stops. Last to freeze is next caller.
Two lines; teacher calls an instruction; first whole line to do it scores.
diff: Fast finishers: write the 4 instruction words on the back of their badge.
Support: name-tracing sheets with larger dotted letters; child may whisper name to puppet first.
hw: Teach the Hello Song to someone at home (family is the audience).
Practise saying "Hello, my name is ___" in front of a mirror 3 times.
Find one English word at home or on packaging and bring it to show the class.
lp.tip: Week 1 is about safety and routine, not English volume. Learn every name before Week 2 — use the register song daily.

weeks.obj: ask How are you? and answer with 4 feeling words
weeks.lang: happy, sad, angry, tired; How are you? I am...
weeks.act: Feelings miming game; guess my emotion; feelings board check-in routine
weeks.hw: draw 4 faces and label them

skills.L: Feelings chant - listen and point to the matching face
skills.S: Mime 4 feelings; How are you? circle with flashcards
skills.R: Match feeling words to picture faces
skills.W: Trace feeling words; draw my feeling face

lp.wu: Hello Song + register song from Week 1; children answer "I am here!" with a big smile. Review names with the ball toss at speed.
wuAlt: Feelings weather report: hold up sun/cloud flashcards, children shout happy/sad
Puppet asks each child "How are you?" — puppet answers for shy children first
lp.pres: Present 4 feelings (happy, sad, angry, tired) with the emotions flashcard set: show card, make the face, children copy the face three times. Drill "How are you? — I am happy!"
presAlt: Mirror faces in pairs: one shows a feeling, partner names it
Teacher-story: tell a 30-second story with a feeling; children hold up the right card
lp.prac: Feelings miming: child mimes a feeling, class guesses in English. Then pair drill with the question around the circle.
pracAlt: Flashcard slap: two teams, slap the feeling card the teacher names
Slow reveal: hide card behind a book, slide it up slowly — first correct guess keeps the card
lp.ls: Listen and point: teacher describes ("A boy is sleepy...") children point to the correct flashcard; extend to touch-the-card races.
lp.re: Guess my emotion: teacher pulls a face, children shout the word; then children take turns being the teacher.
lp.prod: Feelings check-in routine: each child puts their name sticker on the feelings chart (happy/sad/angry/tired column) and says "I am ___." This becomes the daily opening routine.
lp.rw: Trace the 4 feeling words (dotted letters); draw and colour own face next to today's feeling. Fast finishers: copy "How are you?"
lp.st: "If You're Happy and You Know It" with all 4 feelings verses (angry = stamp feet, tired = stretch yawn) — Music/Songs. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Mime + guess in English; mime-er chooses next player.
Cards on floor, teams slap the called word. Slow calls first.
Slide card up slowly; earliest correct guesser keeps it.
Match word cards to face cards in pairs — first finished reads them aloud.
Call a feeling + count to 3; everyone makes the statue face.
diff: Fast finishers: match word cards to the flashcards on the wall.
Support: allow pointing before saying; pair a confident child with a quiet one.
hw: Draw 4 faces and label them (happy, sad, angry, tired).
Ask 2 people at home "How are you?" and report back in English words.
Play emotion statues with your family — you are the teacher.
lp.tip: Keep the feelings chart up permanently — it doubles as your daily register and an emotional check-in tool.

weeks.obj: recognize and say 5 colors and answer What color is it?
weeks.lang: red, blue, yellow, green, black; What color is it? It is...
weeks.act: Colors relay race; color chant with actions; color touch game
weeks.hw: find 3 things at home in our colors

skills.L: Colors Action Song - listen, point and sing (Music/Songs)
skills.S: What colour is it? pair pointing game
skills.R: Match colour word cards to colour splats
skills.W: Trace colour words and colour the pictures

lp.wu: Hello Song + feelings-chart check-in ("I am happy!"). Quick review of W1–2 with the paddle flashcards.
wuAlt: Colour hunt: "touch something red!" children race to touch colours in the room
I spy with my little eye... something blue (teacher models, children guess)
lp.pres: Present 5 colours (red, blue, yellow, green, black) with the Shapes-Colours flashcards: card + colour + chorus. Ask "What colour is it?" and full answer "It is red."
presAlt: Colour magic: mix paint or transparent films (blue + yellow = green!) while saying the words
Point-and-pause read of a colours picture book
lp.prac: Point-to: "Point to something red" — children find colours in the classroom. Then the Colors Action Song (listen, point, sing) twice.
pracAlt: Colour corners: assign a colour per corner, call a colour, run to the corner
Flashcard slap with colour cards
lp.ls: Listen and colour: teacher says "The apple is red" — children colour prepared fruit/shape sheets with the right crayon (checks real listening).
lp.re: Colour bingo mini-round: each child picks 3 colour cards; teacher pulls colours from a bag; winners shout Bingo!
lp.prod: Team colour collage: each team gets a big paper with their colour name; they cut/glue magazine pictures or draw items of that colour, then present: "It is blue!"
lp.rw: Trace the 5 colour words and colour the splashes correctly. Fast finishers: write the colour of 3 objects in the room.
lp.st: Colors Action Song (Music/Songs) with full-body actions; picture-book colour questions ("What colour is the bear?"). Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Colour per corner; call and run; last ones in help call next.
3 cards each, pull from a bag, full-card = Bingo.
"I spy something green..." guess classroom objects.
Teams slap the called colour; add speed rounds.
diff: Fast finishers: spell colour words aloud with a partner.
Support: keep crayons labelled with colour words for matching.
hw: Colour-by-number sheet (2 colours) with labels traced.
Find 3 red things at home and draw them.
Teach the Colors Action Song chorus to your family.
lp.tip: Insist on the full sentence "It is red" from week 3 — the pattern transfers to nearly every later topic.

weeks.obj: count 1-10 forwards and catch-count in a circle
weeks.lang: numbers 1-10; How many?
weeks.act: Counting chant with fingers; ball circle count; line-up game by number cards
weeks.hw: count the doors and windows at home

skills.L: Listen and count sounds (claps, bells); count along 1-10
skills.S: Catch-count circle; count objects aloud in pairs
skills.R: Match numeral cards to dot cards
skills.W: Trace numbers 1-10; count-and-mark sheets (Worksheets)

lp.wu: Hello Song + feelings chart. Colour review round of Flashcard Slap at speed.
wuAlt: Colour hunt relay: run, touch a called colour, run back
Bingo round with colour cards
lp.pres: Present numbers 1–10 with numeral flashcards: count chorally forwards, then count the class, chairs, pencils — real counting, not just chanting.
presAlt: Counting song with fingers (Music/Songs counting set)
Number line hop: jump along a floor number line saying numbers
lp.prac: Catch-count circle: throw the ball, count in order 1→10, restart at 1; add "How many?" with flashcard dots.
pracAlt: Human numbers: children hold numeral cards and order themselves 1–10
Clap-count: clap the number of claps you hear, then say the number
lp.ls: Listen and count: teacher drops coins/claps behind a screen; children count and hold up the numeral card. Classic, and it truly checks listening.
lp.re: Speed round: count 1–10 as fast as class can, then backwards from 5. Giggle guaranteed.
lp.prod: Counting museum: children collect exactly 5 (then 8, then 10) classroom objects and make a display on their table; partner checks by counting in English.
lp.rw: Trace numerals and number words 1–5 (1 one, 2 two...); count-and-match sheets from Worksheets. Fast finishers: 6–10.
lp.st: Read a counting picture book (10 Little... ) with pause-and-count pages; number song to finish. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Ball toss counting in order; drop = start again (kindly!).
Claps/drops behind a screen; hold up numeral card.
Floor numbers; hop and say; hop backwards = challenge.
Children order themselves with numeral cards.
Partner flashes fingers; other counts and says.
diff: Fast finishers: write 6–10 words; simple sums in English (one and one is two).
Support: numeral cards to hold before saying; count together first.
hw: Count 10 objects at home with a family member — in English.
Trace numbers 1–10 sheet and draw the right dots next to each.
Play Listen & Count with a parent clapping.
lp.tip: Halloween falls this week (Oct 26–Nov 1) — if you celebrate it in class, swap the story slot for the Seasonal Halloween pack story and keep numbers as the main lesson.

weeks.obj: combine colors and numbers in color-by-number work
weeks.lang: review: colors + 1-10; How many (red) balloons?
weeks.act:
Color-by-number worksheet; team quiz; fast-finisher extension cards
Map craft: colour the march route and say "the march goes to..."; flag colours chant.
weeks.hw: Teach someone at home 3 words from this week (Colors + numbers review) and show them the gesture.

skills.L: Listen for colour + number (three red balloons) and hold up cards
skills.S: How many red balloons? team guessing game
skills.R: Colour-by-number instructions read together
skills.W: Colour-by-number sheet; trace number words

lp.wu: Hello + feelings routine; speed count 1–10; one Colour Corners round to shake out energy.
wuAlt: Number bingo warm-up
"Point to something blue" quick commands round
lp.pres: Combine colours + numbers: "How many red balloons?" with flashcards of balloon bunches. Model answer "Three red balloons."
presAlt: Real balloons or counters in colours: count and describe together
Picture pairs: show two cards, class compares (3 blue / 2 red)
lp.prac: Color-by-number work (Worksheets): teacher calls the code ("1 is red, 2 is blue"), children colour by number — the flagship activity of this week.
pracAlt: Dice colour game: roll, count, colour that many circles in the rolled colour
"Grab 3 yellow" — teacher calls number+colour, children grab counters
lp.ls: Teacher describes a hidden picture ("I see four green frogs...") children build/draw it correctly — listening with colours + numbers combined.
lp.re: Quick quiz: teacher holds up dots of a colour, class asks "How many?" and answers as a chorus.
lp.prod: Balloon picture factory: each child draws a bunch of coloured balloons with a number label, then presents: "Five red balloons!" Display on the wall gallery.
lp.rw: Complete colour-and-number sentences: "___ red balloons" (write the number word); matching sheets from Worksheets/Print outs.
lp.st: Revisit the Colors Action Song + counting song as a medley; children choose the order — choice = engagement. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Roll dice, count, colour circles in your colour.
Call number + colour; grab counters; verify together.
Same sheet, teams; correct colouring wins.
Listen to description; draw/build it right.
Hold up dot cards; class asks and answers.
diff: Fast finishers: write the full sentence "I have three red balloons."
Support: pre-counted counters; colour-word wall chart for reference.
hw: Finish the colour-by-number picture and bring it for the gallery.
Count and colour: 3 blue things, 5 red things at home.
Teach someone the balloon sentence with your drawing.
lp.tip: This is the consolidation week — no new vocabulary. Raising accuracy and confidence on old language beats adding new.

weeks.obj: name 6 classroom objects and ask for them politely
weeks.lang: pen, pencil, book, bag, chair, table; Can I have..., please?
weeks.act: Point-and-say scavenger hunt; What is missing? tray game
weeks.hw: label 3 objects at home (with family help)

skills.L: Listen to Can I have... please requests and do as I say
skills.S: Ask for classroom objects politely in a shop-corner game
skills.R: Match object words to labelled picture cards (Flashcards)
skills.W: Label desk objects with word cards; trace object words

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; quick balloon-picture gallery tour — 3 children present their homework sentences.
wuAlt: Object hunt: "Bring me a pencil... a book!" realia round
Lucky dip: pull an object from the bag, name it if you can
lp.pres: Present 6 classroom objects (pen, pencil, book, bag, chair, table) with real objects + flashcards: touch, say, pass around the circle.
presAlt: Mystery bag: feel inside, guess the object, reveal
Label the classroom: children stick word cards on real objects
lp.prac: "Can I have the ___, please?" polite requests: model with the puppet shop; children request objects to build a tower or complete a picture.
pracAlt: Pass the parcel with an object; when music stops, holder asks for it politely
Object swap circles: two circles turn opposite ways; on stop, request partner's object
lp.ls: Listen and fetch: teacher describes ("It is on the table. It is blue. You write with it.") children race to bring the right object.
lp.re: Pencil-case inventory: pairs empty pencil cases and name everything they can in English; count objects for number review.
lp.prod: Classroom shop: half the class are shopkeepers with objects, half are buyers with polite requests; swap roles. Best manners win the "Please Cup".
lp.rw: Label-and-trace sheets: match word cards to object pictures; trace all 6 words. Fast finishers: copy "Can I have a pencil, please?"
lp.st: School objects song (Music/Songs); or "This is my pencil" pass-the-object chant. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Feel, guess, reveal; keep it if right.
Description race to bring the right object.
Stick word cards on real objects; read the room after.
Pairs name + count their pencil cases.
diff: Fast finishers: write the 6 words from memory; check with the wall labels.
Support: picture + word matching first, then tracing.
hw: Label 3 objects at home with paper labels (pen, book, bag...).
Play Mystery Bag with a family member using a pencil case.
Trace and draw the 6 classroom objects sheet.
lp.tip: Real objects beat flashcards this week — the whole lesson can run with a pencil case and a school bag.

weeks.obj: follow a simple Halloween story and say 4 themed words
weeks.lang: pumpkin, witch, ghost, candy; simple story frames
weeks.act:
Pumpkin craft; costume charades; trick-or-treat dialogue circle
Flag craft + "I am from Morocco" chant; national symbols matching game.
weeks.hw:
Note: falls close to 31 Oct
Teach someone at home the independence chant.

skills.L: Halloween story with picture prompts - listen and join in (Seasonal pack)
skills.S: Say 4 themed words; trick-or-treat chant roleplay
skills.R: Match Halloween words to pictures
skills.W: Trace themed words; colour the pumpkin mask

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; object review round (Lucky Dip from the bag).
wuAlt: Simon Says with objects ("Touch a chair! Grab a pen!")
Quick shop roleplay replay from W6
lp.pres: Halloween special: present pumpkin, witch, ghost, candy with the Seasonal pack flashcards + a simple story ("The Little Witch" style) with picture prompts and lots of pausing.
presAlt: Spooky sound box: play sounds (wind, laugh, door); guess the word
Costume show: teacher items (hat, cape) dress a volunteer as each word
lp.prac: Trick-or-treat roleplay: knock on the door (real classroom door), chant "Trick or treat!", receive a (paper) candy, say thank you. Practise the 4 words in the chant.
pracAlt: Spooky statues: witch/ghost/pumpkin poses on the drum beat
Flashcard haunted house: cards hidden around room; find and name each one
lp.ls: Halloween story listen #2: children hold up the correct card each time they hear pumpkin/witch/ghost/candy — active listening to the same story.
lp.re: Pumpkin pass: pass the pumpkin (orange ball) to music; stop = say a Halloween word + make the face/mime.
lp.prod: Make pumpkin masks or paper jack-o-lantern faces (Seasonal pack craft); parade them while chanting the trick-or-treat rhyme.
lp.rw: Trace the 4 Halloween words; colour the pumpkin mask. Fast finishers: copy "Happy Halloween!"
lp.st: Halloween song ("Knock knock, trick or treat" — Music/Songs or Seasonal pack) with the parade. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Sounds guess the word; cards as backup.
Pose per word on the beat.
Real door knocking; chant + thank you.
diff: Fast finishers: write the 4 words; add "bats" and "hat" as bonus words.
Support: mask-making first, words second — success in craft builds courage to speak.
hw: Teach the trick-or-treat chant to your family.
Colour the Halloween sheet and label the 4 words.
Find a Halloween image (book/internet) and bring one word to teach the class.
lp.tip: Culture note for the class: Halloween is "fun scary", not real scary. Keep lights on for sensitive children and check families are comfortable — offer an autumn-pumpkin framing as an alternative.

weeks.obj: recognize and say the sounds of letters A-F with 1 word each
weeks.lang: letter-sound links A-F; a is for apple...
weeks.act:
Letter hunt around the room; sound-action pairing; tracing big letters in the air
Gratitude turkey craft: one feather = one "I am thankful for..." sentence.
weeks.hw:
trace worksheet A-F (Worksheets)
Say 3 "I am thankful for..." sentences at home.

skills.L: Phonics songs A-F - listen, sing, do the actions (Music/Songs)
skills.S: Say letter sounds A-F with the a-is-for-apple chant
skills.R: Match letters A-F to first-sound pictures (Flashcards)
skills.W: Trace and write letters A-F; first-sound matching sheet

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; Halloween words echo round (say it if you remember it).
wuAlt: Alphabet march: march and chant A B C to the song beat (pre-exposure)
Quick object lucky dip
lp.pres: ABC phonics 1 (letters A–F): present each letter with its sound + anchor word (a-apple, b-ball, c-cat, d-dog, e-elephant, f-fish) using the phonics song and flashcards.
presAlt: Letter-of-the-moment show: big card, trace it in the air with your arm/foot/nose
Mystery letter bag: pull a letter, everyone shouts the sound and word
lp.prac: Air writing + table writing with fingers; then first-sound matching: apple picture → which letter? (picture cards + letter cards).
pracAlt: Letter jump: letter cards on floor; teacher says the sound; jump to it
Sound sort: sort picture cards under A–F letter headers
lp.ls: Phonics song listening: hold up the letter card when you hear its sound in the song (pre-teach: cards ready, listen, raise!).
lp.re: Quick-fire: teacher shows a letter, class makes the sound + word; reverse: teacher says the word, class finds the letter.
lp.prod: Letter detectives: find A–F letters in classroom print (posters, books, labels) with magnifying-glass fingers; tally how many of each letter they find.
lp.rw: Trace and write A–F (lower + upper case) on phonics sheets (Worksheets); draw the anchor word next to each letter.
lp.st: Phonics song (Music/Songs) again as a sing-along; start building the class Letter Wall (each week adds letters). Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Sound called, jump to the letter card.
Hunt letters in classroom print; tally.
Write letters in air with elbow/knee; partner guesses.
diff: Fast finishers: match 2 words per letter (a: apple, ant).
Support: letter cards with the anchor picture printed on them as a bridge.
hw: Find 3 things at home that start with b, c, or d (say them in English).
Trace A–F sheet; colour the anchor words.
Sing the phonics song to family; teach them one action.
lp.tip: Say sounds ("b is /b/"), never letter names yet — "bee" comes in W24's alphabet song. Keep anchors consistent all year (same apple, same cat).

weeks.obj: match letters G-M to their sounds and first-letter pictures
weeks.lang: letter-sound links G-M
weeks.act: Letter crafts; first-sound sorting game; alphabet line-up
weeks.hw: find one object per letter G-M (any 3)

skills.L: Phonics songs G-M; listen and hold up the letter card
skills.S: Sound relay - hear the sound, say the letter and word
skills.R: Match letters G-M to pictures; sort by first sound
skills.W: Trace letters G-M; write the missing first letter

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; A–F quick-fire sound round with flashcards.
wuAlt: Letter Jump replay at speed
Detective tally share: who found the most letters at home
lp.pres: ABC phonics 2 (G–M): same routine — g-goat, h-hat, i-igloo, j-jam, k-kite, l-lion, m-monkey — song, cards, actions.
presAlt: Add actions per letter (goat butts, monkey scratches); class invents the action — invented actions stick best
Letter story: one silly sentence per letter ("The goat eats jam!")
lp.prac: First-letter pictures: match picture cards to G–M letters; then mix A–M for cumulative sorting (this recycling is the point).
pracAlt: Letter Slap: two teams slap the letter whose sound is made
Pass the letter: music pass a card; stop = sound + word + action
lp.ls: Beginning-sound bingo: teacher says a word ("monkey!"); children cover the letter m on their bingo card.
lp.re: A–M speed parade: letters in order round the circle, each child one letter; restart with a shuffle — can the class do it in 13 seconds?
lp.prod: Letter Wall building: children add G–M cards + pictures to the class Letter Wall and "read the wall" chorally (a: apple... m: monkey).
lp.rw: Trace G–M sheets; missing-letter sheets ( _at → hat with picture support). Fast finishers: write 3 G–M words from the wall.
lp.st: Phonics song medley A–M with all the actions the class invented. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Sound made, team slaps the letter.
Circle order A–M against the clock.
Do the invented action; class says letter + word.
Make "goat eats jam" sentences; act them out.
diff: Fast finishers: 3-letter reading prep — blend c-a-t with you one-to-one.
Support: keep A–F cards visible during G–M work; confusion is normal at this stage.
hw: Find one object at home for g, h, or m and bring the word.
Trace G–M sheet + colour anchor words.
Teach your family the letter actions for 3 letters.
lp.tip: Cumulative review every week now: A–M mixed, not just the new seven. Five minutes of old letters beats twenty of new ones.

weeks.obj: name 5 family members and say This is my...
weeks.lang: mother, father, sister, brother, baby; This is my...
weeks.act: Family tree drawing; family song with finger play; show-and-tell photo moment
weeks.hw: draw your family tree

skills.L: Family Song - listen and point to family members (Music/Songs)
skills.S: Introduce family photos: This is my mummy
skills.R: Match family words to a family picture (Flashcards/Family)
skills.W: Trace family words; draw my family and label it

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; A–M letter parade; one Sound Sort round mixing all letters.
wuAlt: Family song chorus as a pre-listen
Letter Slap championship round
lp.pres: My family: present mother, father, sister, brother, baby with the Family flashcards + Family Song. Model "This is my mother." with family photos of teacher (real photos are gold).
presAlt: Finger family puppets: draw faces on fingers, present each member
Story book family: a picture-book family is presented; children point to members
lp.prac: Family Song with finger puppets (Music/Songs); then card drill: show card, class says "This is my sister."
pracAlt: Family photo circle: children who brought photos show and say one line
Guess who: hide a card; children guess which family member is missing
lp.ls: Listen and build: teacher describes a family ("The baby is little. The sister is tall."); children arrange family cards or draw the family correctly.
lp.re: Family chant with rhythm: clap-clap "mother!", clap-clap "father!" — speed rounds.
lp.prod: My family drawing: children draw their family and rehearse one line per person ("This is my father.") in pairs; volunteers present to the class.
lp.rw: Trace family words; label the family drawing (mummy, daddy...). Fast finishers: copy "This is my family."
lp.st: Family Song full sing-along + a family-themed picture book read-aloud. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Draw faces on fingers; song drives the drill.
Cards face down; remove one; guess in English.
Show photo, say one line, pass on.
diff: Fast finishers: add grandfather/grandmother as bonus words.
Support: sentence frame card "This is my ___" stays on the board all lesson.
hw: Finish the family drawing and label 3 people in English.
Sing the Family Song at home and point to family members.
Ask a parent to write one English family word to learn together.
lp.tip: Families are diverse — offer "This is my ___" flexibly (grandma raising a child is "my grandmother" and equally celebrated). Never force nuclear-family frames.

weeks.obj: name 5 toys and ask for them: Can I have the..., please?
weeks.lang: ball, doll, car, teddy, puzzle; I have got a...
weeks.act: Toy shop corner roleplay; I have got guessing game; toy graph on the board
weeks.hw: choose a toy and present one sentence

skills.L: Listen to toy descriptions and point to the right toy (Flashcards/Toys)
skills.S: Ask for toys politely: Can I have the ball, please?
skills.R: Match toy words to toy pictures
skills.W: Trace toy words; complete I have got a ___

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; family words echo round; 2 children present their family drawings.
wuAlt: Family Song chorus with finger puppets
A–M letter quick-fire
lp.pres: Toys: present ball, doll, car, teddy, puzzle with the Toys flashcards + real toys from the mystery bag. Model "I have got a ball." and "Can I have the car, please?"
presAlt: Toy shop video/photo talk: describe what you see
Toy pass-around: each toy goes round with its word chanted
lp.prac: Toys TPR: "Roll the ball! Hug the teddy! Drive the car!" — do the action with (imaginary) toys; then flashcard drill with "I have got a ___".
pracAlt: Toy charades: mime playing with a toy, guess in English
Slap game with toy cards
lp.ls: Listen and match: teacher describes a toy ("It is soft. You sleep with it.") children point/grab the right one; extend to colour + toy combos ("a red car").
lp.re: Toy survey: everyone "has" one toy card; mingle and ask "Teddy?" — find your twin with the same toy, stand together.
lp.prod: Toy shop roleplay: shopkeeper + buyer with polite requests (recycles W6); buyers must say "Can I have the red ball, please?" — colour + toy together.
lp.rw: Trace toy words; draw "my favourite toy" and label it. Fast finishers: write "I have got a ___" sentence.
lp.st: Toys song or chant (Music/Songs); "My teddy bear" lullaby-style wind-down before goodbye. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Feel, guess, reveal, keep on desk.
Mime the play action; guess the word.
Simon Says variant with toy actions.

skills.L: Phonics songs N-T; listen and find the sound
skills.S: Build 3-letter words aloud (cat, pen) in pairs
skills.R: Match N-T letters to pictures; read word cards
skills.W: Trace letters and write first letters; word-building sheet (Worksheets)

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; weather report; A–M + G–M letter speed round (letters fade fast — revive them!).
wuAlt: Letter parade A–M against the clock
Letter Slap championship
lp.pres: ABC phonics 3 (N–T): n-nose, o-orange, p-pen, q-queen, r-rain, s-sun, t-table — same routine: song, cards, actions; anchor words recycle known topics where possible.
presAlt: Letter story: one silly sentence per letter ("The queen has a pen... on her nose!")
Children invent actions for N–T (they remember their own best)
lp.prac: Sound sort A–T mixed; word building start: make c-a-t and p-e-n with letter cards — first blending moments, celebrate hugely.
pracAlt: Letter jump N–T
Beginning-sound bingo A–T
lp.ls: Phonics song listening with A–T cards: raise the letter when its sound is sung; then listen-for-the-word: teacher says words, children stand if it starts with s.
lp.re: Blending buddy time: pairs build 3-letter words from letter cards (cat, pen, sun) and "read" them to another pair.
lp.prod: Word factory: teams draw a picture card (cat, sun, pen, top), build the word with letter cards, write it on the factory chart, read it to the class.
lp.rw: Trace N–T; first word-writing sheets (cat, pen, sun — copy below dotted models). Fast finishers: write 2 more from the word bank.
lp.st: Phonics song A–T medley with all invented actions; Letter Wall gains N–T. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Pairs build + read to another pair.
Word called; stand if it starts with s.
diff: Fast finishers: build 4-letter words (top→stop).
Support: Elkonin boxes (one box per sound) with counters before letters.
hw: Build 2 words at home from letter cards/paper squares; draw the picture.
Trace N–T + the 3 first words.
Sound hunt: find 2 things at home starting with n or s.
lp.tip: Blending is the hardest leap of the year — keep words to 3 letters, celebrate every success like a goal, and slow down if more than half the class struggles.

weeks.obj: complete the alphabet with sounds U-Z; sing the alphabet song
weeks.lang: letter-sound links U-Z; alphabetical order
weeks.act: Alphabet arc games; missing letter activity; alphabet song performance
weeks.hw: Teach someone at home 3 words from this week (ABC phonics 4 (U-Z) + alphabet song) and show them the gesture.

skills.L: ABC song - listen and point along the alphabet line
skills.S: Chant the alphabet; I-know-a-word-for... game
skills.R: Order letter cards U-Z and match to pictures
skills.W: Trace U-Z; complete my ABC chart

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; weather; alphabet march with the ABC Song chorus.
wuAlt: Letter parade A–T
Word factory gallery: read 3 words from last week's chart
lp.pres: ABC phonics 4 (U–Z): u-umbrella, v-van, w-water, x-fox (x in fox!), y-yo-yo, z-zebra. The alphabet is COMPLETE — celebrate: "We know A to Z!"
presAlt: Alphabet party reveal: giant A–Z line on the floor, walk it while singing
Missing letters: alphabet line with gaps; children fix it with cards
lp.prac: ABC Song (letter NAMES now: "ay, bee, see") + alphabetical order games: order letter cards A–Z in teams on the floor.
pracAlt: Alphabet relay: run, pick the next letter, place it
First-letter dictionary skill: find words in a picture dictionary page by first letter
lp.ls: Alphabet listening: teacher says a letter name; children write it in the air then find it on the wall frieze; speed rounds.
lp.re: A–Z freeze: music plays ABC song; stop = teacher shows picture (apple), children shout first letter ("A!") and do its action.
lp.prod: Class picture dictionary: each child makes one dictionary page (letter + picture + word) — bind into the class book; W30 will read it as their final product.
lp.rw: Trace U–Z; alphabetical order worksheet (order 5 letters). Fast finishers: write the alphabet in lower case from memory.
lp.st: ABC Song full and proud; alphabet picture book read-aloud with letter hunts. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Picture shown; shout the first letter.
Make one page of the class dictionary.
diff: Fast finishers: write 2 words for their dictionary letter.
Support: alphabet frieze stays visible; x is "fox" (ends with the sound) — keep it simple.
hw: Finish your class dictionary page (letter + 2 pictures + words).
Sing the ABC song with letter names at home.
Put 5 toy names in alphabetical order.
lp.tip: Letter names vs sounds confusion is normal — say "its name is A, its sound is /a/" explicitly, with the two chants. It clicks by repetition.

weeks.obj: review colors, numbers, animals through seasonal games
weeks.lang: review weeks 16-24 language
weeks.act: Spring garden craft; egg-and-spoon vocabulary review; team quiz
weeks.hw: Teach someone at home 3 words from this week (Easter/spring review special) and show them the gesture.

skills.L: Listen to a spring story and join the seasonal songs
skills.S: Seasonal games with speaking turns: colours, numbers, animals
skills.R: Match spring and Easter words to pictures
skills.W: Trace and copy review words; colour an egg pattern

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; weather; alphabet quick-fire round (names now).
wuAlt: Spring song chorus
Easter egg word hunt preview: hide eggs with letters on them
lp.pres: Easter/spring special: spring words (flower, egg, chick, bunny, butterfly) + There is / There are with a big spring picture ("There is a bunny. There are three eggs.").
presAlt: Spring walk story: picture walk with counting + spring words
Egg reveal: plastic eggs open to spring word cards
lp.prac: Spring picture counting game: children find and count hidden items in a big poster ("How many eggs? Three!") — numbers + spring words combined.
pracAlt: Egg-and-spoon word relay: carry the egg to the word card, say it
Spring bingo
lp.ls: Listen and stick: teacher describes the spring scene; children place picture stickers in the right spots — checks There is/are comprehension.
lp.re: Review medley part 1: colours + numbers + letters stations (3-minute rounds, favourite games only).
lp.prod: Easter egg hunt (words!): eggs hidden with pictures/words inside; finders read the word to keep the egg — reading as treasure.
lp.rw: Trace spring words; complete "There is a ___ / There are ___ ___" with the poster. Fast finishers: write one full spring sentence.
lp.st: Spring/Easter song; spring picture book; compare in one sentence: "In Morocco we... " (teacher scribes their words — first shared writing!). Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Count hidden eggs/flowers in the poster.
Carry egg to card; say the word.
Words + pictures; read back to win.
diff: Fast finishers: write 2 There is/are sentences about the poster.
Support: word eggs contain pictures + words; either "counts".
hw: Draw a spring picture with 3 eggs and label them.
Play Word Egg Hunt at home (paper eggs with 4 words).
Count flowers/plants at home in English.
lp.tip: Cultural framing: Easter as "spring celebration" parallels (not replaces) local spring traditions — children compare, all celebrations respected.

weeks.obj: name 4 rooms and say where simple things are
weeks.lang: house, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom; Where is mummy? She is in the...
weeks.act: House poster craft; room sorting game; Where is the teddy? guessing
weeks.hw: tell someone 3 rooms in English

skills.L: Listen to room riddles: Where is mummy? She is in the...
skills.S: Name the rooms in a house-building game
skills.R: Match room words to the house picture (Flashcards/Rooms)
skills.W: Trace room words; draw my house and label

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; weather; spring words echo; one There-is round with the poster.
wuAlt: House song chorus pre-load
Alphabet freeze round
lp.pres: My house: house, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom (+ living room bonus) with Rooms flashcards + a doll house or big paper house. Model "Where is mummy? She is in the kitchen."
presAlt: House tour video/photos: "Which room is this?"
Family-in-rooms story: family flashcards move around rooms
lp.prac: Rooms drill + family positioning: children place family cards in rooms and say "Daddy is in the bedroom" — combines two old topics into new sentences.
pracAlt: Room corners: call a room, run to its poster corner
Rooms slap game
lp.ls: Listen and place: teacher says where everyone is ("The baby is in the bathroom!"); children place cards on the house map — real comprehension check.
lp.re: Rooms counting: "How many beds? How many chairs?" — rooms + numbers (the spiral keeps spiralling).
lp.prod: My house design: children draw/scribble their house rooms and walk a partner through: "Kitchen! Bedroom!" or full "This is my kitchen." — museum walk at the end.
lp.rw: Trace room words; label a house picture. Fast finishers: write "Mummy is in the ___" sentence.
lp.st: House/home song; "The Three Little..."-style house story with room vocabulary. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Place + say where family cards are.
Run to the room poster called.
Count furniture per room in English.
diff: Fast finishers: add garage, garden.
Support: room icons on the house map (bed in bedroom) as scaffolds.
hw: Draw your home and label 3 rooms.
Play Listen & Place: family says a room, you run to it.
Count the rooms in your home in English.
lp.tip: Homes differ (apartments, houses, shared rooms) — "my home" not "my house"; celebrate every kind of home in the museum walk.

weeks.obj: describe where things are using in, on, under
weeks.lang: table, chair, bed, box; in, on, under
weeks.act: Teddy hiding game; draw the scene dictation; prepositions with real objects
weeks.hw: Teach someone at home 3 words from this week (Furniture and in / on / under) and show them the gesture.

skills.L: Listen and place the toy in, on or under the box
skills.S: Say where the toy is: in, on, under
skills.R: Match preposition words to position pictures (Flashcards)
skills.W: Trace in / on / under; circle-and-match sheet

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; weather; rooms echo; house-map quick round.
wuAlt: Furniture flashcard lucky dip
Where-is-the-teddy quick game (hide a toy, guess the room)
lp.pres: Furniture + prepositions: table, chair, bed, box + in, on, under. Use a real box + teddy: put teddy IN/ON/UNDER the box — the clearest demo in ELT.
presAlt: Hide the teddy (visible!): class describes where it is
Draw-along: teacher dictates a room scene ("The cat is on the chair") — children draw it
lp.prac: Teddy position drill: children command in pairs ("Put it under the box!") with a box + object each; swap roles.
pracAlt: Preposition statues: pose as "on" (standing on a chair-side pose — safe!), "in", "under"
Slap game with position picture cards
lp.ls: Draw-what-I-say (classic picture dictation): teacher dictates 4-position scene; compare drawings — laughter guaranteed, listening verified.
lp.re: Quick positions round with classroom objects: "Put your pencil under your book!" — whole-class listen-and-do at speed.
lp.prod: Room rearrange challenge: pairs get a furniture picture set + a room mat; one is the "architect" (gives 3 commands), one arranges: "The bed is under the window!" Swap.
lp.rw: Trace in/on/under + furniture words; complete position sentences with word bank. Fast finishers: write one full command sentence.
lp.st: Position song/chant; hide-and-seek story book with preposition pages. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Real teddy positions; say each one.
Pencil under book! Whole class speed.
diff: Fast finishers: add next to, behind.
Support: position gesture cues (hand in fist = in) stay standardised all year.
hw: Play Teddy in the Box at home with a toy + box.
Draw the dictation scene again from memory; label 2 positions.
Put 3 objects in/on/under things and tell family in English.
lp.tip: The box-and-teddy demo is the lesson — do it before any flashcard. Physical first, pictorial second, written third (Concrete→Pictorial→Abstract).

weeks.obj: sequence 5 morning actions with English words
weeks.lang: wake up, wash, brush my teeth, eat, go to school
weeks.act: Routine cards sequencing; brush-my-teeth song; mime the morning chain
weeks.hw: do the morning routine chant at home

skills.L: Brush-my-teeth song; listen and order the routine
skills.S: Mime morning actions and say the words
skills.R: Order the 5 routine picture cards (Flashcards/Daily Routine)
skills.W: Trace routine words; sequence-and-draw sheet

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; weather; prepositions quick round (pencil under book).
wuAlt: Routine song chorus to pre-load vocabulary
Clock-mime game: mime the daily action, guess
lp.pres: Morning routine: wake up, wash, brush my teeth, eat, go to school with Daily Routine flashcards + the Brush My Teeth song. Model sequencing: "First I wake up. Then I eat."
presAlt: Routine story of a child's morning (with the clock ticking!)
Teacher mimes their own morning; children order the cards
lp.prac: Routine card sequence: pairs order the 5 cards and chant the sequence; add actions per verb (wake-up stretch, teeth brush...).
pracAlt: Routine bingo
Musical routine: music stops = do + say the routine card shown
lp.ls: Listen and sequence: teacher tells a mixed-up morning ("First I eat. Then I wake up?!") — children catch the silly order and fix it with their cards.
lp.re: Time preview with clock flashcards: o'clock only ("I wake up at 7 o'clock" — choral, no mastery expected; it seeds next levels).
lp.prod: My morning timeline: children draw their 5-step morning with times (approximate) and present: "First I wake up. Then I wash..." — their first long turn in English; rehearse in pairs first.
lp.rw: Trace routine verbs; order-and-write worksheet (number the pictures 1–5, copy two verbs). Fast finishers: write "I wake up at ___".
lp.st: Brush My Teeth song + routine song medley; morning-routine picture book. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
diff: Fast finishers: add get dressed, go to bed (evening preview).
Support: numbered sequence mat 1–5; first/then arrows on the wall.
hw: Finish the morning timeline; tell family in order.
Do + say your routine tomorrow morning (wake up! wash!).
Play Silly Order Fix with a parent.
lp.tip: First/Then language is the real outcome — sequencing beats verb perfection at Pre-A1.

weeks.obj: show confidence across the year's topics in station games
weeks.lang: all year outcomes
weeks.act:
6 stations: colors/numbers, animals, food, family, body, weather; station passports stamped
Recycle-sort game in English; plant-a-seed craft with "First... then..." instructions.
weeks.hw:
Complete observation checklist pre-fill
Find 3 things at home to recycle and name them in English.

skills.L: Listen-and-do stations mixing songs and instructions
skills.S: Station games - say, ask and answer across the year's topics
skills.R: Word-and-picture station races
skills.W: Tracing and labelling station sheets

lp.wu: Hello + feelings; weather; routine chant with actions.
wuAlt: Game spinner: class picks warm-up games from the whole year
Wall-gallery walk: name 5 things you can see
lp.pres: Big Review Carousel framing: 6 stations of the year's greatest hits. Quick re-teach of any game half the class has forgotten; teams formed with team names in English!
presAlt: Quiz-show framing with team buzzers (clap patterns)
Detective badge making (paper badges) for the review week
lp.prac: Stations 1–2: Alphabet A–Z order race + Blending word factory (letters + reading); Station 3: Colours-and-numers quiz show (buzz to answer in full sentences).
pracAlt: Swap in any game bank favourites — station signs list the skill, teacher picks the game
lp.ls: Station 4: Listen & Draw mega-dictation (house scene with positions, weather + clothes — one drawing uses HALF the year's language!).
lp.re: Station 5: Like-survey speed mingle (food + pets graphs, read the class graph from W19 if kept!) — old artifacts as reading texts.
lp.prod: Station 6: Roleplay theatre: shop + market + weather forecast mash-up scenes in threes — children choose their scene; performances at the end.
lp.rw: Rainbow writing: write 5 words you are proudest of (any topic) in your best letters; add to your portfolio for parents' day.
lp.st: Year medley sing-along: children vote the top 3 songs of the year; sing them out. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: One drawing, half a year of language.
diff: All: mixed-level teams; stronger children read word cards, newer ones name pictures — everyone contributes.
Teacher floats; assistant (if any) anchors the rowdiest station.
hw: Teach your family ONE game from this year (your choice).
Practise your portfolio words for the celebration.
Choose your favourite English word of the year — bring it Friday.
lp.tip: Photo/video the station carousel: it is the single best artifact of the year for parents and for your own CPD file.

weeks.obj: complete game-based final assessment; celebrate the year
weeks.lang: all year outcomes
weeks.act:
Assessment games in pairs; mini ceremony rehearsal; goodbye circle with stamps
Jobs guessing game (What does a ... do?); thank-you cards for workers we know.
weeks.hw:
Final report cards sent; certificates at ceremony
Draw one job you love and write 3 sentences about it.

skills.L: Listen-and-do assessment games (Tests)
skills.S: Mini speaking chat through game tasks, then celebrate
skills.R: Word-picture matching assessment sheet
skills.W: Name, numbers and topic-word writing check

lp.wu: Welcome celebration framing: "Today we show EVERYTHING" — final carousel warm-up with the 3 voted songs.
wuAlt: Portfolio gallery walk: read each other's rainbow words
Team parade with team chants
lp.pres: Final assessment as Game Day II: same 6-station format as W15 but harder cards (blending words, full sentences to say, dictation to draw, timeline to sequence). Observation checklist part 2.
presAlt: TV-show framing: "The Big English Show" with applause cards
Passport control framing: stamp each completed station in an English Passport
lp.prac: Stations 1–2: Reading corner (word factory words + class picture dictionary — each child reads 3 words aloud) and Writing corner (name + best sentence copying).
pracAlt: One-to-one pull-out stations while the class plays — the quiet corner works best for checklists
lp.ls: Listening station: final mega-dictation + listen-and-do sequence (3-step commands — W17 chains, now longer).
lp.re: Speaking circuit: teacher + puppet interview each child (name, age, likes, pet, weather today) — 60 warm seconds each, others play word games with the assistant/peer leader.
lp.prod: The Big Show: pairs perform their chosen scene from W29 theatre; class picture dictionary is "published" and read; certificates ceremony with families if possible.
lp.rw: Final portfolio page: "I can..." star chart — child colours stars for what they can do (say hello, count to ten, name colours, read cat...). Self-assessment as celebration.
lp.st: Top-3 songs sing-along finale; goodbye tradition: each child says their favourite English word into the microphone; group photo with certificates. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Read 3 words from the class dictionary.
One word each into the mic.
diff: All: stations let every child show their best somewhere — speaking shy? Show the reading star. Reading hard? Show the speaking star.
Celebrate growth, not level: each certificate names two "wow moments" from the checklists.
hw: Summer mission card: 5 star activities (one song a week, teach a game, find 10 English words, read the dictionary page, watch one cartoon in English).
Keep the portfolio and dictionary at home — read it in September with pride.
Write (or trace) one letter to next year's class: "English is fun!"
lp.tip: End on identity: "You are English speakers now." Certificates + photos + the mission card turn June momentum into September readiness.
checklist: Says name and greets (Hello, I am...)
Follows classroom instructions
Names colours + counts 1–10 (and beyond)
Names key topic vocabulary (animals/food/clothes...)
Reads 3-letter words (cat, pen)
Writes name + words from memory
Produces phrases (It is... / I like... / Can I have...?)

levels.desc: A first English class for children aged 6–9 with no previous English. Thirty weeks build the routines, vocabulary, and confidence to greet, count, name, and talk about the everyday world — colours, numbers, family, animals, food, and the alphabet — through songs, games, and play.

levels.label: Kids · Intermediate

weeks.obj: Greet a partner and introduce a friend; say hello and goodbye and give their name; follow 3 basic class instructions
weeks.lang: Hello. My name is... Goodbye!; stand up, sit down, look, listen + be questions review; What's your name? he/she
weeks.res: Music/Songs (hello song); Flashcards/Class rules; Worksheets/Print outs
weeks.act: Mini-survey: ask 3 friends about classroom routines and report back
weeks.hw: teach the classroom routines words to someone at home

skills.L: Hello song plus a listen-and-do for 3 class instructions; be-questions chant
skills.S: Greet a partner and introduce a friend in pairs
skills.R: Read simple class-rule phrases and match to pictures (Worksheets)
skills.W: Write my name and age; copy 3 rule phrases

lp.wu: Hello Ball Toss: Students stand in a circle, toss a soft ball, and say 'Hello, my name is...' when they catch it. Teacher models first, then students introduce themselves.
wuAlt: Hello Puppet Show: Teacher uses a puppet to greet students, who respond with 'Hello, my name is...'.
Name Chain: First student says 'Hello, I am [name]', next student repeats and adds their own name.
lp.pres: Teacher uses flashcards of 'stand up', 'sit down', 'look', 'listen' to demonstrate actions with exaggerated movements. Models 'Stand up!' and students repeat and stand. Checks understanding with 'What do I say?' and gestures.
presAlt: Classroom Rules Story: Teacher draws a simple story on the board of a student following rules, saying 'Look, listen, sit down.'
TPR Command Game: Teacher performs actions and says commands, then asks students to copy and say the words.
lp.prac: Simon Says: Teacher says 'Simon says stand up/sit down/look/listen'. Students only move when 'Simon says' is included. Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation.
pracAlt: Command Relay: Teams line up, first student runs to board, points to a command flashcard, and says it. Team earns points for correct actions.
Action Charades: Student draws a command flashcard, acts it out without speaking, and classmates guess the word.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher says 'Stand up and look at the board' or 'Sit down and listen to me'. Students draw simple pictures to show they understood the sequence of 3 instructions.
lp.re: Freeze Dance: Play music, students dance on 'stand up', freeze on 'sit down'. Teacher calls commands randomly to reactivate vocabulary.
lp.prod: Mini-Survey: Students walk around with a paper asking 'What is your name?' and 'Can you stand up/sit down?'. They write 3 friends' names and report back: 'Ali can stand up.'
lp.rw: Trace and Copy: Students trace dotted words 'stand up', 'sit down', 'look' on a worksheet, then copy them neatly. Teacher checks for correct spelling and formation.
lp.st: Goodbye Song: Sing 'Goodbye, Goodbye' with actions (wave, clap, stomp). End with a sticker chart where students put a sticker next to their name, then line up for high-fives.
g: Toss ball and say 'Hello, my name is...' to a partner.
Teacher says commands, students only move when 'Simon says' is included.
Teams race to point to flashcards and say commands correctly.
Dance on 'stand up', freeze on 'sit down' when music stops.
Ask 3 friends their name and if they can do actions, then report.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a short sentence 'My name is __. I can stand up.' with a drawing.
Support: Use picture flashcards alongside command words for visual cues.
hw: Teach 'stand up', 'sit down', 'look' to a family member and show them the actions.
Draw a picture of yourself following one classroom rule and write the word.
Practice the 'Hello' song with a sibling and perform it for the class next week.
lp.tip: Use exaggerated gestures and facial expressions for TPR commands to ensure comprehension, especially for shy learners in a large group.

weeks.obj: Ask How are you? and answer with 6 feeling words; ask How are you? and answer with 4 feeling words
weeks.lang: happy, sad, angry, tired; How are you? I am... + happy/sad/tired/hungry adjectives; I'm not...
weeks.res: Flashcards (emotions set); Games/Game ideas; Worksheets/Print outs
weeks.act: Make a mini-book about how are you? Feelings and read it to a partner
weeks.hw: find and label 5 pictures of how are you? Feelings from magazines

skills.L: Listen to feelings mini-dialogues and match to emotion cards
skills.S: How are you? I am happy/sad pair chain with 6 words
skills.R: Read feeling words and match to faces
skills.W: Write feeling words; complete I am ___ today

lp.wu: Simon Says feelings: Teacher says 'Simon says show me happy' and students smile, 'Simon says show me sad' and students frown. After 3 rounds, teacher asks 'How are you?' and students shout 'I am happy/sad!'
wuAlt: Flashcard drill: Teacher holds up happy/sad/angry/tired cards, students say the word and make the face
Mime game: Teacher mimes feeling, students guess 'You are tired!'
lp.pres: Teacher shows a puppet, says 'Hello, I am Sam. How are you?' Puppet replies 'I am happy!' Then 'How are you?' 'I am sad!' Teacher points to mouth when speaking, gestures to students to repeat. Checks by asking 'Show me happy?'
presAlt: Storybook: Read 'The Feelings Monster' where monster changes expressions, ask 'How is the monster?' after each page
Realia: Show a banana and say 'I am hungry!', ask students to bring food and say 'I am hungry!'
lp.prac: Pair chain: Students stand in pairs, A asks 'How are you?' B answers 'I am happy!' then asks 'How are you?' A answers 'I am sad!' and so on, switching after 4 turns. Teacher circulates to help pronunciation.
pracAlt: Board race: Two teams race to write 'I am ___' under happy/sad/angry/tired flashcards on the board
Ball toss: Teacher throws a ball, asks 'How are you?', student catches and answers, then throws back
lp.ls: Listen and match: Teacher plays 4 short dialogues ('How are you? I am happy!', etc.), students point to matching emotion flashcards on their desks. Check by holding up each card and asking 'Is this happy?'
lp.re: Feelings charades: After break, teacher acts out tired (yawns), angry (stomps), happy (jumps), students shout the word and copy the action
lp.prod: Mini-book making: Students fold paper into 4 pages, draw a face on each page (happy/sad/angry/tired), write 'I am ___' under each. Then walk around and read to 3 partners: 'This is me. I am happy!'
lp.rw: Trace and copy: Students trace 'happy' 'sad' 'angry' 'tired' in dotted letters, then copy them 3 times. Then write 'I am ___ today' and fill in one word with a drawing
lp.st: Song: Sing 'If You're Happy and You Know It' with clapping/stomping, then goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line
g: Students cross out happy/sad/angry/tired as teacher calls them
Match feeling cards with face cards
Run to board and write 'I am ___' under correct flashcard
Roll a die with feelings, say 'I am ___'
Act out feeling for team to guess
diff: Fast finishers: Draw a 5th feeling (hungry) and write a sentence
Support: Use word bank with pictures to copy from
hw: Cut out 5 feeling pictures from magazines, glue and label them
Draw 4 feeling faces and write 'I am ___' under each
Ask 3 family members 'How are you?' and write their answers
lp.tip: Use the puppet for shy students – they’ll talk to the puppet instead of you. Link feelings to local context: 'After Eid, we are happy!'

weeks.obj: Spell the colour words and ask What colour is it?; recognize and say 5 colors and answer What color is it?
weeks.lang: red, blue, yellow, green, black; What color is it? It is... + What colour is/are...?; plurals with colours
weeks.res: Flashcards/Shapes-Colours; Music/Songs (Colors Action Song); Worksheets/Print outs
weeks.act: Guessing game: teams ask questions about colors
weeks.hw: play the matching game in the colors library folder with a family member

skills.L: Colors Action Song; listen for colour words in a chant
skills.S: What colour is it? spelling relay in teams
skills.R: Read and match colour words; find them in a word search
skills.W: Write colour words; colour-by-word sheet

lp.wu: Color Ball Toss: Teacher throws a ball to a student and says 'What color is it?' Student catches it and says 'It is red.' Student throws to another student and asks 'What color is it?' and so on.
wuAlt: Color Jump: Students jump on colored mats. Teacher says 'Jump on red!' and students jump. Then students say 'Jump on blue!' and teacher jumps.
Color Flashcard Slap: Teacher shows flashcards quickly. Students slap the card and say the color word.
lp.pres: Teacher holds up red, blue, yellow, green, black flashcards and says each word clearly. Students repeat. Teacher models 'What color is it?' and answers 'It is red.' Teacher holds up a red apple and asks 'What color is it?' Students answer 'It is red.'
presAlt: Color Story: Teacher reads a story about a bird with red feathers, blue wings, etc. Students point to the colors in the book.
Color Magic: Teacher has a bag of colored objects. Students reach in without looking, feel the object, and guess the color.
lp.prac: Spelling Relay: Teams line up. Teacher says 'Spell red!' First student runs to the board, writes R-E-D, runs back. Team does this for all 5 colors. Teacher checks spelling.
pracAlt: Color Bingo: Teacher calls out colors. Students cover the matching picture on their bingo card. First to get a line wins.
Color Chain: Students sit in a circle. Student 1 says 'I see something red.' Student 2 says 'I see something red and blue.' and so on, adding one color each time.
lp.ls: Listen and Color: Teacher says 'Color the apple red.' 'Color the sky blue.' Students color a picture of an apple and sky. Teacher checks if they colored correctly.
lp.re: Color Hopscotch: Draw a hopscotch grid with colored squares. Students jump and say the color of the square they land on. 'Blue! Green! Yellow!'
lp.prod: What's in the Box? Teacher puts a colored object in a box. Students ask 'What color is it?' by taking turns. Student guesses 'It is red!' Teacher opens the box to see if correct.
lp.rw: Color-by-Word: Students have a sheet with shapes. Each shape has a color word. They read 'red' and color the shape red. 'blue' and color blue, etc. Then they trace the color words.
lp.st: Teacher sings 'I Can Sing a Rainbow' with actions. Students join in. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teams take turns. A student thinks of a colored object. Team asks 'What color is it?' until they guess correctly.
Students take turns turning over two cards. If they match, they say the color word and keep the cards.
Teacher says 'I spy with my little eye something red.' Students guess 'Is it a pen?'
Teams race to sort colored objects into red, blue, yellow, green, black piles.
Student acts out an object. Other students ask 'What color is it?' and guess.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a sentence about their favorite color: 'My favorite color is red.'
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank with the 5 color words to copy from.
hw: Play the matching game in the colors library folder with a family member.
Draw 5 objects, each a different color, and write the color word under each one.
Ask your family 'What is your favorite color?' and write down their answers.
lp.tip: Use realia like Moroccan fruits (red apples, yellow bananas) to connect colors to local culture and make learning more relevant.

weeks.obj: Count to 20 and ask How many...?; count 1-10 forwards and catch-count in a circle
weeks.lang: numbers 1-10; How many? + numbers 11-20; How many ... can you see?
weeks.act:
Cut-and-stick poster with numbers 1-10 labels
Craft: paper pumpkins while saying "This is my pumpkin. It is big/scary!"; costume word game.
weeks.hw:
read your numbers 1-10 mini-book to someone at home
Draw your costume and label it in English.

skills.L: Listen and count to 20; number bingo listening
skills.S: How many ... can you see? pair counting games
skills.R: Read number words one-ten and match to numerals
skills.W: Write numerals and number words 1-10

lp.wu: Warm-up: Halloween Count Circle. Children stand in a circle, pass a plastic pumpkin, and count 1-10 forwards. Teacher says 'One', child passes to next and says 'Two', etc. If a child hesitates, they do a spooky action like 'Boo!'
wuAlt: Alternative 1: Number Flashcard Jump. Teacher shows number flashcards 1-10, children jump the number of times shown.
Alternative 2: Spooky Whisper. Children whisper 'One ghost, two cats...' while passing a toy around the circle.
lp.pres: Presentation: Big Halloween Poster. Teacher shows a large poster with 10 Halloween items (bats, pumpkins, ghosts). Models 'How many pumpkins? One, two, three.' Children repeat. Teacher points and asks 'How many bats?' Children respond with numbers. Checks with thumbs up/down.
presAlt: Alternative 1: Mystery Bag. Teacher puts 10 plastic spiders in a bag, children guess 'How many?' before counting.
Alternative 2: Halloween Storybook. Read 'Ten Spooky Spiders', counting each page aloud.
lp.prac: Guided Practice: Cut-and-Stick Poster. Children receive a poster with 10 unlabelled Halloween items and number stickers 1-10. They work in pairs to match numbers to items, saying 'One pumpkin, two bats...' as they stick. Teacher circulates to help.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: Number Bingo. Teacher calls numbers 1-10, children cover the corresponding pictures on their bingo cards.
Alternative 2: Halloween Memory Game. Children turn over number cards and Halloween picture cards, saying 'Two ghosts' when they match.
lp.ls: Listening Slot: How Many? Game. Teacher plays a recording of spooky sounds (e.g., one howl, two bangs). Children hold up the correct number of fingers. Teacher asks 'How many sounds?' Children say the number. Checks with number flashcards.
lp.re: Reactivation Game: Monster Count Freeze. Children dance to Halloween music. When music stops, teacher shouts a number (e.g., 'Four!'), children freeze in groups of four and say 'Four monsters!'
lp.prod: Production Task: My Pumpkin Craft. Children draw and decorate a paper pumpkin. They present it to the class saying 'This is my pumpkin. It is big/scary!' Classmates ask 'How many eyes?' and the child answers.
lp.rw: Reading/Writing Slot: Number Mini-Book. Children trace and copy number words 1-10 in a mini-book with Halloween pictures (e.g., 'One bat'). They read the book to a partner, pointing to each word.
lp.st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Sing 'Five Little Pumpkins' song with actions. Read a short Halloween story about counting. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Children cover pictures on their bingo cards as teacher calls numbers 1-10.
Children roll a die, say the number, and draw that many pumpkin seeds on their paper.
Teacher says a costume word (e.g., 'witch'), children jump the number of letters.
Children count 1-10 while tossing a soft pumpkin.
Children hide paper ghosts around the room, then ask 'How many?' and count them.
diff: Fast finishers: Draw a spooky scene with 10 items, label them in English.
Support: Use number lines or trace dotted numbers for the craft.
hw: Homework 1: Read your numbers 1-10 mini-book to someone at home.
Homework 2: Draw your costume and label it in English (e.g., 'My mask is red').
Homework 3: Count 10 things in your house and tell your family in English.
lp.tip: Use local Halloween-like traditions (like 'Aicha's wedding' sweets) to make the theme relatable. Pair strong and weak learners during craft activities to encourage peer support.

weeks.obj: Use colours and numbers together in a counting game; combine colors and numbers in color-by-number work
weeks.lang: review: colors + 1-10; How many (red) balloons? + There is/There are + numbers
weeks.res: Worksheets/Print outs; Games/Printable games; Worksheets/Print outs
weeks.act:
Circle game: pass the ball and answer a question about colors and numbers
Map craft: colour the march route and say "the march goes to..."; flag colours chant.
weeks.hw:
write the colors and numbers words twice in your notebook, once in rainbow colours
Draw the Moroccan flag and write its colours in English.

skills.L: Listen to There is / There are sentences and choose the picture
skills.S: Run a colours-and-numbers quiz in teams
skills.R: Read How many? questions and answer with cards
skills.W: Complete counting sentences: There are ___

lp.wu: Ball Pass Count: Students stand in a circle. Teacher passes a soft ball to a student, who says 'One red balloon' and passes it to the next, who says 'Two blue balloons', continuing to ten. Teacher helps with pronunciation.
wuAlt: Flashcard Jump: Teacher holds up a color flashcard; students jump and say the color number (e.g., 'Three green!').
Color Hunt: Teacher calls 'Find something blue!'; students point and say 'I see one blue book!'
lp.pres: Teacher shows a large map of Morocco with the Green March route marked. 'This is the Green March. The march goes to... Agadir!' Students repeat. Teacher models 'The march goes to...' with different cities, using a pointer. Teacher asks 'How many red flags?' and holds up a flashcard to check 'There are three red flags.'
presAlt: Storytime: Teacher reads a simple story about a boy counting colored flags during the Green March, pausing to ask 'How many yellow flags?'
Flag Craft Demo: Teacher draws a simple Moroccan flag on the board, colors it red and green, and says 'The flag is red and green.'
lp.prac: Team Counting Race: Two teams race to count colored balloons on flashcards. Teacher asks 'How many (blue) balloons?' Team members answer 'There are five blue balloons!' and get a point. Teacher helps with full sentences.
pracAlt: Color-by-Number Worksheet: Students trace and color a simple map of the Green March route using numbers 1-5 (1=red, 2=green). They say 'The march goes to... number 1!'
Flag Chant: Students stand and chant 'Red, green, red, green! The Moroccan flag!' with claps.
lp.ls: Listen and Point: Teacher plays an audio saying 'There are four red balloons.' Students point to the correct picture on a worksheet with three options (e.g., 3 blue, 4 red, 5 green). Teacher checks answers together.
lp.re: Simon Says Colors: After break, teacher plays 'Simon says touch something green!' Students touch green objects and say 'Green!' to reactivate vocabulary quickly.
lp.prod: March Route Project: In pairs, students get a blank map. They draw the Green March route with numbered stops (1-5). They take turns saying 'The march goes to... number one! It is red.' Teacher walks to support.
lp.rw: Flag Writing: Students trace the words 'red' and 'green' in their notebooks. Then, they copy the sentence 'The flag is red and green.' Teacher checks spelling and handwriting.
lp.st: Goodbye Song: Teacher leads 'Goodbye, Goodbye, See You Next Time!' with gestures. Students line up for a high-five and get a sticker for their chart.
g: Pass a ball and count colored objects (1-10).
Race to answer 'How many balloons?' for points.
Chant and clap 'Red, green, red, green!'
Touch and name colors on command.
diff: Fast finishers: Draw 10 balloons and write the color word for each.
Support: Use a word bank with colors and numbers to help with writing.
hw: Write 'red' and 'green' twice in rainbow colors.
Draw the Moroccan flag and write 'red' and 'green' under it.
Count 10 objects at home and say 'There are... (number) (color) (objects).'
lp.tip: Use the Green March theme to connect language learning to local history, making colors and numbers more meaningful and memorable for students.

weeks.obj: Name classroom objects and ask for them politely; name 6 classroom objects and ask for them politely
weeks.lang: pen, pencil, book, bag, chair, table; Can I have..., please? + this/that/these/those; Can I have ..., please?
weeks.act: Show-and-tell: two sentences about classroom objects
weeks.hw: write 3 sentences about classroom objects and draw a picture

skills.L: Listen to polite requests and do classroom-object tasks
skills.S: Ask for objects politely; this/that pair practice
skills.R: Read object words and match to labelled photos
skills.W: Label desk objects; copy Can I have..., please?

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'Simon Says' with classroom objects. Teacher says 'Simon says touch your pencil' or 'Simon says show me your book'. Students touch or show the object. If they move without 'Simon says', they sit down. Teacher asks 'What is it?' and students say 'It is a pencil/book'.
wuAlt: Alternative warm-up 1: 'Mystery Bag'. Teacher puts a classroom object in a bag. Students feel it and guess 'Is it a pen?'. Teacher says 'Yes, it is' or 'No, it isn't'.
Alternative warm-up 2: 'Flashcard Race'. Two lines of students. Teacher shows a flashcard. First student to say the word (e.g., 'bag') gets a point for their team.
lp.pres: Presentation: Teacher uses real classroom objects (pen, pencil, book, bag, chair, table). Holds up each object and says 'This is a pen.' Students repeat. Then models the question 'Can I have the pen, please?' and gives the object to a student. Students practice asking and receiving.
presAlt: Alternative presentation 1: 'Story Time'. Teacher tells a short story about a character who needs classroom objects. 'Ali needs a pen. Can I have the pen, please?' Students repeat the requests.
Alternative presentation 2: 'Flashcard Dialogue'. Teacher shows flashcards of objects and models the dialogue: 'What is it?' 'It is a book.' 'Can I have the book, please?'
lp.prac: Guided practice: 'Pass the Object'. Students sit in a circle. Teacher gives an object to one student and says 'Can I have the pencil, please?'. The student passes it to the next student, who must say the full request. Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation.
pracAlt: Alternative practice 1: 'Find the Object'. Teacher says 'Can I have the book, please?'. Students point to the book on their desks. First to point correctly gets a sticker.
Alternative practice 2: 'Pair Dialogue'. Students work in pairs. Student A holds an object. Student B says 'Can I have the __, please?'. Student A gives it and says 'Here you are.'
lp.ls: Listening slot: 'Listen and Draw'. Teacher describes a scene: 'Draw a table. On the table, draw a book and a pen. Next to the table, draw a chair.' Students follow instructions and draw. Teacher checks drawings to confirm comprehension of object names and prepositions.
lp.re: Reactivation game: 'Musical Objects'. Play music. Students walk around the classroom. When music stops, teacher calls out an object (e.g., 'bag!'). Students must find and touch a bag. Last one to touch is 'out' but becomes the next caller.
lp.prod: Production task: 'Classroom Shop'. Set up a 'shop' with classroom objects. Students take turns being the shopkeeper and customers. Customers must say 'Can I have the __, please?' to request an object. Shopkeeper says 'Here you are.' Students use 'this/that' (e.g., 'Can I have that pen, please?').
lp.rw: Reading and writing slot: 'Label and Trace'. Students look at a worksheet with pictures of classroom objects but no words. They trace the words 'pen', 'pencil', 'book', 'bag', 'chair', 'table' below the pictures. Then, they copy the words into their notebooks next to the correct picture.
lp.st: Story / song + goodbye: Read 'The Day I Lost My Pencil' story, focusing on repeated object words. Sing the 'Hello Goodbye Song'. End with the goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teacher calls out object words. Students cover the matching picture on their bingo card. First to get a line shouts 'Bingo!'
Teacher places 3 objects on a table. Students close eyes. Teacher removes one. Students open eyes and say 'The pen is missing! Can I have the pen, please?'
Two teams race to bring a requested object to the teacher. Teacher says 'Can I have the book, please?'. First student to bring the book gets a point.
Teacher says 'I spy with my little eye something beginning with b'. Students guess 'Is it a book?'. Teacher says 'Yes, it is.'
Students match flashcards of objects to word cards on the board. Say the word aloud when making a match.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a short sentence about their favourite classroom object and draw a picture of it using 'This is my __.'
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank with picture clues to label the objects on their worksheet.
hw: Homework option 1: Draw a picture of your desk and label 3 objects (e.g., 'This is my book.')
Homework option 2: Ask your family for objects using 'Can I have the __, please?' and write down what they said
Homework option 3: Make flashcards for 6 classroom objects and practice saying the words with a family member
lp.tip: Use the local context of American Space Oujda by connecting the lesson to 'What objects do you use in the library?' to reinforce real-world use of the language.

weeks.obj: Talk about Halloween characters with have got; follow a simple Halloween story and say 4 themed words
weeks.lang: pumpkin, witch, ghost, candy; simple story frames + have got (I/you/we/they); witch, ghost, pumpkin
weeks.act:
Matching race with Halloween word and picture cards
Flag craft + "I am from Morocco" chant; national symbols matching game.
weeks.hw:
teach the Halloween words to someone at home
Teach someone at home the independence chant.

skills.L: Halloween story with have got - listen and sequence the pictures
skills.S: Describe Halloween characters: It has got...
skills.R: Read simple themed sentences and match to characters (Worksheets)
skills.W: Write 2 Halloween sentences with have got

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'Simon Says' with Halloween commands. Teacher says 'Simon says touch your nose,' 'Simon says say boo,' 'Simon says pretend to be a witch.' Students react physically and repeat the words.
wuAlt: Warm-up: 'What's Missing?' with 3 Halloween flashcards (pumpkin, witch, ghost) on the board. Students close eyes, teacher removes one, they guess which is missing.
Warm-up: 'Action Chant' - Teacher chants 'Pumpkin, pumpkin, round and orange!' with gestures, students repeat and copy gestures.
lp.pres: Presentation: Show large flashcards of pumpkin, witch, ghost. Say 'It is a pumpkin. It has got a big face.' Repeat for witch and ghost. Point to features (hat, broom, sheet) and ask 'What has it got?' Students answer 'It has got a hat.'
presAlt: Presentation: Use a Halloween storybook with big pictures. Read 'Look! A ghost. It has got a white sheet.' Point to the sheet, ask students to repeat.
Presentation: Teacher wears a witch hat and says 'I am a witch. I have got a hat.' Pass the hat to students, each says 'I am a witch. I have got a hat.'
lp.prac: Guided practice: 'Matching Race' - Two teams race to match word cards (pumpkin, witch, ghost) with picture cards. Teacher says 'Find the witch!' Students grab the correct pair. Winners get high-fives.
pracAlt: Guided practice: 'Have Got Drill' - Teacher shows a ghost flashcard, asks 'What has it got?' Students say 'It has got a sheet.' Repeat with witch and pumpkin.
Guided practice: 'Pair Work' - Student A holds a flashcard, Student B asks 'What has it got?' Student A answers 'It has got a [feature].' Swap roles.
lp.ls: Listening slot: Listen to a simple story about a ghost, witch, and pumpkin. Story: 'The ghost has got a sheet. The witch has got a hat. The pumpkin has got a face.' Students listen and sequence 3 picture cards in the correct order.
lp.re: Reactivation game: 'Halloween Freeze Dance' - Play spooky music, students dance when music plays. Teacher pauses music and shouts 'Ghost!' Students freeze and say 'It has got a sheet!'
lp.prod: Production task: 'Create a Halloween Character' - Students draw a witch, ghost, or pumpkin. They present their drawing to the class, saying 'This is a witch. It has got a hat and a broom.'
lp.rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read 3 simple sentences on a worksheet: 'The pumpkin has got a face.' 'The ghost has got a sheet.' 'The witch has got a hat.' They match each sentence to the correct character picture. Then, they trace the sentences and copy them once.
lp.st: Story / song + goodbye: Read a short Halloween story with repetition. End with 'Goodbye Song' where students sing 'Goodbye, goodbye, see you next time!' Teacher gives stickers and students line up for high-fives.
g: Teams race to match word cards with picture cards.
Teacher gives commands with Halloween words, students react.
Teacher removes a flashcard, students guess which one is missing.
Students dance and freeze when music stops, saying a character's feature.
Students draw a character and present it using 'It has got...'
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Draw two characters and write two sentences about each.
Support / weaker learners: Use sentence starters like 'It has got a...' to complete the worksheet.
hw: Homework option 1: Teach the words pumpkin, witch, ghost, and 'It has got...' to a family member and draw a picture.
Homework option 2: Practice the 'I am from Morocco' chant with a family member.
Homework option 3: Color a Halloween picture and label it with the words.
lp.tip: Tip: Use TPR (Total Physical Response) for vocabulary retention—students remember words better when paired with gestures. For the American Space Oujda context, connect Halloween to local celebrations like Eid by comparing festive foods or costumes.

weeks.obj: Read and write ch/sh words; recognize and say the sounds of letters A-F with 1 word each
weeks.lang: letter-sound links A-F; a is for apple... + digraphs ch, sh; fish, chair, shop
weeks.act:
Pair picture dictation with this week's words
