Gratitude turkey craft: one feather = one "I am thankful for..." sentence.
weeks.hw:
find and label 5 pictures of phonics from magazines
Say 3 "I am thankful for..." sentences at home.

skills.L: Phonics songs; listen for the ch and sh sounds in words
skills.S: Sound-spell ch/sh words aloud in pairs
skills.R: Read ch/sh words and sort the word cards
skills.W: Write ch/sh words; complete the word sort

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'Phonics Jump' — Teacher says a letter sound (e.g., 'a'), students jump and say a word (e.g., 'apple'). Repeat for A-F sounds.
wuAlt: Warm-up: 'Sound Bingo' — Students have bingo cards with A-F pictures; teacher calls sounds, students mark matches.
Warm-up: 'Pass the Sound' — Students pass a ball and say a word for the called sound (e.g., 'b' for 'ball').
lp.pres: Presentation: Use flashcards for A-F (apple, ball, cat, dog, egg, fish) and ch/sh (chair, shop). Model 'a is for apple', 'ch is for chair'. Students repeat and point.
presAlt: Presentation: 'Phonics Story' — Show a short story with A-F and ch/sh words; teacher reads, students repeat sounds.
Presentation: 'Realia Show' — Bring real objects (apple, ball, chair, shop toy); name them, emphasize sounds.
lp.prac: Guided Practice: 'Pair Picture Dictation' — Student A says a word (e.g., 'fish'), Student B draws it. Swap roles. Teacher monitors for correct sounds.
pracAlt: Guided Practice: 'Word Sort' — Students sort ch/sh word cards into two columns; teacher checks pronunciation.
Guided Practice: 'Sound Hopscotch' — Draw hopscotch with A-F sounds; students jump and say a word for each sound.
lp.ls: Listening Slot: 'Sound Hunt' — Teacher plays a recording with ch/sh words (e.g., 'shop', 'chair'). Students raise hands when they hear the sound and say the word.
lp.re: Reactivation Game: 'Turkey Tag' — One student is 'it' (turkey), others run. If tagged, they say 'I am thankful for...'.
lp.prod: Production Task: 'Gratitude Turkey Craft' — Students make a turkey with paper feathers. Each feather has a sentence: 'I am thankful for...'. Share in groups.
lp.rw: Reading/Writing Slot: 'Trace and Write' — Students trace ch/sh words (fish, chair, shop) from the board, then copy them into notebooks.
lp.st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Sing 'The Thanksgiving Turkey' song with actions. End with 'Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.'
g: Jump and say a word for the called sound.
Draw words said by a partner.
Tagged students say 'I am thankful for...'.
Sort ch/sh word cards into columns.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 extra 'thankful' sentences.
Support: Trace words with dotted lines.
hw: Find and label 5 pictures of A-F and ch/sh words from magazines.
Say 3 'I am thankful for...' sentences at home to your family.
Draw a picture of your favorite ch/sh word and write it below.
lp.tip: Use real objects (like a toy shop or chair) to make phonics tangible; connect gratitude to local values like family and community.

weeks.obj: Read long-vowel words (magic e); match letters G-M to their sounds and first-letter pictures
weeks.lang: letter-sound links G-M + CVCe pattern: cake, bike, home
weeks.act: Mini-survey: ask 3 friends about phonics and report back
weeks.hw: play the matching game in the phonics library folder with a family member

skills.L: Listen to magic-e word pairs (tap/tape) and choose the one I hear
skills.S: Read long-vowel words aloud in a quick-fire relay
skills.R: Read CVCe words and match to pictures (Games)
skills.W: Write long-vowel words; add the magic e

lp.wu: Flashcard Relay: Students line up in two teams. Teacher shows a G-M flashcard (e.g., 'goat'). First student runs, says the sound /g/, and tags the next. Team with all students fastest wins.
wuAlt: Phonics Bingo: Teacher calls out a sound (e.g., /m/), students cover the matching letter on their bingo card.
Sound Jump: Students jump when they hear the sound of their letter (G-M) called out.
lp.pres: Teacher uses a story about 'Magic E' who changes short vowels to long vowels. Shows flashcards for 'tap' vs 'tape', 'kit' vs 'kite'. Models: 'This is tap. This is tape. Magic E makes the vowel say its name.' Students repeat.
presAlt: Realia Show: Teacher shows a real cap and a cape, contrasting /æ/ vs /eɪ/ sounds. Models: 'Cap. Cape.'
Video Clip: Short cartoon showing Magic E changing words like 'mad' to 'made'.
lp.prac: CVCe Matching Game: Students work in pairs. Each pair gets a set of CVCe word cards (cake, bike, home) and picture cards. They match words to pictures and say them aloud. Teacher monitors and helps with pronunciation.
pracAlt: Whiteboard Relay: Teams take turns writing CVCe words from dictation (e.g., 'write home').
Phonics Hopscotch: Draw hopscotch with G-M letters. Students hop and say the sound of the letter they land on.
lp.ls: Listen and Circle: Teacher plays a recording with pairs of words (e.g., 'tap/tape', 'kit/kite'). Students circle the word they hear on their worksheet. Checks if they can distinguish long vs short vowels.
lp.re: Phonics Tag: Teacher calls out a sound (e.g., /b/). Students with 'b' cards run around. When teacher calls 'Magic E!', they freeze and say the long vowel sound (e.g., /baɪ/).
lp.prod: Mini-Survey: Students ask 3 friends, 'What is your favorite CVCe word?' Friends answer, 'My favorite is __.' Students report back to the class, e.g., 'Fatima likes home.'
lp.rw: Trace and Write: Students trace CVCe words (cake, bike, home) on a worksheet, then copy them 3 times each. Teacher checks for correct letter formation and magic e placement.
lp.st: Story: Read 'The Magic E Adventure' book, pointing to CVCe words. End with 'Goodbye Song' (e.g., 'Bye Bye, Goodbye') and students line up for a high-five as they get a sticker.
g: Students jump when they hear the sound of their letter (G-M) called out.
Students flip over word/picture cards and match CVCe words to pictures.
Students roll a die, move, and say a CVCe word for the space they land on.
Teacher says, 'I spy with my little eye something with /eɪ/.' Students guess 'cake' or 'cape'.
Students hop on G-M letters and say the sound, then add 'Magic E' and say the long vowel sound.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a sentence with a CVCe word, e.g., 'I see a bike.'
Support: Use word/pairing cards with pictures to help match CVCe words.
hw: Play the matching game in the phonics library folder with a family member. Show them 3 CVCe words.
Draw a picture of your favorite CVCe word (e.g., home) and write the word underneath.
Ask your family: 'What is your favorite CVCe word?' and write it down.
lp.tip: Use hand gestures for Magic E (e.g., a magic wand) to make the concept visual and memorable. Connect to local culture by using CVCe words related to Moroccan life, like 'home' or 'bike'.

weeks.obj: Describe a family tree with possessive 's; name 5 family members and say This is my...
weeks.lang: mother, father, sister, brother, baby; This is my... + possessive 's; This is my sister's...
weeks.act: Make a mini-book about my family and read it to a partner
weeks.hw: read your my family mini-book to someone at home

skills.L: Family Song plus listen to family descriptions
skills.S: Present my family tree with possessive s
skills.R: Read family sentences and complete the tree
skills.W: Write 2 sentences about my family

lp.wu: Play 'Simon Says' with family vocabulary: 'Simon says touch your mother', 'Simon says show me your sister', 'Simon says point to your brother'.
wuAlt: Play 'Pass the Parcel' with family flashcards; child says 'This is my...' when music stops
Play 'Flashcard Jump' - kids jump to flashcard of mother/father/sister/baby and name it
lp.pres: Use a large family tree poster; point to each person and say 'This is my mother', 'This is my father'; then add 'This is my mother's book' with a small book prop; check understanding by asking 'Who is this?' and 'Whose book is this?'
presAlt: Use a puppet family; puppet introduces each member and says 'This is my...'; kids repeat
Show a family photo album; teacher says 'This is my sister's doll' as kids look at photos
lp.prac: Pair drill with mini family trees; Student A points to a person and says 'This is my...', Student B says 'This is my... too' or 'This is my father's car' with a car prop; teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation
pracAlt: Play 'Family Bingo' with pictures; kids cover 'mother' when teacher says 'This is my mother'
Play 'Chain Game' - first kid says 'This is my mother', next says 'This is my mother and this is my father'
lp.ls: Play 'Listen and Draw' - teacher describes a family tree ('This is my father. This is my mother's cat. This is my brother's ball') and kids draw what they hear; check drawings in pairs
lp.re: Play 'Family Statues' - teacher calls 'Mother!' kids pose as mothers, 'Father!' kids pose as fathers, etc.; fastest movers get stickers
lp.prod: Make a mini-book with 4 pages; kids draw their family and write 'This is my mother', 'This is my father', etc.; read their book to a partner using 'This is my...'
lp.rw: Trace family words (mother, father, sister, brother) with dotted lines, then copy them 3 times; write one sentence like 'This is my mother' in their notebooks
lp.st: Sing 'The Family Song' with actions (hands on hips for mother, big muscles for father, etc.); end with Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line
g: Match family member cards with their objects (e.g., father's car)
One child describes a family member (e.g., 'This is my sister's doll') and others guess
Teams race to place flashcards in correct family tree positions
Teacher removes a family member from the poster and kids say 'This is my mother's...?'
Pass a family flashcard and say 'This is my...' when music stops
diff: Fast finishers: Draw an extra family member and write 'This is my...'
Support: Trace dotted words and use word bank for writing
hw: Read your mini-book to your family
Draw a picture of your family and label 3 members
Ask your family 'Who is this?' and write down 3 names
lp.tip: Use Moroccan family photos (e.g., with grandparents, cousins) to make the theme relatable; praise kids for using full sentences even if pronunciation isn't perfect.

weeks.obj: Describe toys with two adjectives; name 5 toys and ask for them: Can I have the..., please?
weeks.lang: ball, doll, car, teddy, puzzle; I have got a... + his/her + adjective + noun word order
weeks.act: Guessing game: teams ask questions about toys
weeks.hw: write the toys words twice in your notebook, once in rainbow colours

skills.L: Listen to toy descriptions with two adjectives
skills.S: Describe my toy: It is a big red car
skills.R: Read toy descriptions and match to the toys
skills.W: Write two-adjective toy sentences

lp.wu: Toy Charades: Teacher acts out a toy (e.g., bouncing a ball), students guess 'Is it a ball?', teacher replies 'Yes, it is!' or 'No, it isn't!'.
wuAlt: Toy Flashcard Race: Two teams race to match toy flashcards to pictures on the board.
Toy Sound Game: Teacher makes toy sounds (car vroom, doll giggle), students name the toy.
lp.pres: Show toy flashcards (ball, doll, car, teddy, puzzle) with adjectives (big, small, red, blue, green). Model sentences: 'It is a big red car.' Students repeat chorally. Ask 'What is it?' and elicit full sentences.
presAlt: Toy Storybook: Read a simple story like 'The Big Red Ball', highlighting adjectives. Point to toys and ask 'What is it?'
Realia Show: Bring real toys to class, describe them, pass them around for students to feel and describe.
lp.prac: Guessing Game: Teams take turns. One student describes a toy (e.g., 'It is a small blue doll.'), team guesses 'Is it a doll?'. Teacher monitors for correct word order and adjectives.
pracAlt: Toy Description Relay: Teams line up, first student runs to flashcards, picks one, describes it, next student continues.
Adjective Match: Students match toy flashcards to adjective cards (e.g., 'car' + 'red' = 'red car').
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher says 'Draw a big green teddy', students draw. Check drawings to confirm comprehension of two-adjective descriptions.
lp.re: Toy TPR: Teacher shouts 'Be a big car!' students move arms like wheels, 'Be a small doll!' students tiptoe and giggle.
lp.prod: Toy Shop Roleplay: One student is shopkeeper, others are customers. Customers say 'Can I have the small blue puzzle, please?', shopkeeper hands it over. Swap roles.
lp.rw: Trace and Copy: Students trace toy words (ball, doll, car, teddy, puzzle) and copy them twice. Then write sentences: 'I have got a big red ball.'
lp.st: Read 'The Toy Box' story with repeated toy descriptions. Sing 'The Teddy Bear Song' (to the tune of 'Twinkle Twinkle'). Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teacher removes a toy from a line, students say 'The big red ball is missing!'
Students sit in a circle, each adds a toy with an adjective: 'I have a big ball, a small doll...'
Students mark toy flashcards as teacher calls them out with adjectives
Students sort toy flashcards into 'big' and 'small' piles
First student asks 'Do you have a doll?', next answers and asks another student
diff: Fast finishers: Draw their own toy and write three sentences about it.
Support: Use word banks with toy names and adjectives for writing tasks.
hw: Write the toys words twice in your notebook, once in rainbow colours.
Draw your favourite toy and write one sentence: 'It is a ____ ____ ____.'
Ask your family: 'What is your favourite toy?' and tell the class next week.
lp.tip: Use local Moroccan toys like 'taqcha nqaqa' (wooden tops) to connect the theme to students' lives, making vocabulary more meaningful and culturally relevant.

weeks.obj: Say what farm animals can and can't do; name 6 farm animals and make their sounds in English
weeks.lang: cow, horse, sheep, duck, chicken, pig; It is a... + can/can't for ability; A cow can...
weeks.act:
Cut-and-stick poster with farm animals labels
Party week: Christmas vocab stations, carols with actions, "Santa Says".
weeks.hw:
write 3 sentences about farm animals and draw a picture
Teach the carol to someone at home.

skills.L: Old MacDonald plus listen for can/can't sentences
skills.S: Say what farm animals can and can't do
skills.R: Read animal fact sentences and match to animals
skills.W: Write A cow can / can't ___ sentences

lp.wu: Mime the animal: Teacher mimes an animal (e.g., flapping arms like a duck), kids guess 'What is it?' and say the name and sound, e.g., 'It is a duck! Quack quack!'
wuAlt: Animal sound bingo: Teacher calls out animal sounds, kids cover the matching picture on their bingo cards
Flashcard jump: Lay flashcards on the floor, kids jump to the correct card when teacher says 'Jump to the cow!'
lp.pres: Show flashcards of cow, horse, sheep, duck, chicken, pig; ask 'What is it?' and model 'It is a cow'; then ask 'What can a cow do?' and model 'A cow can eat grass'; ask 'Can a cow fly?' and model 'A cow can't fly'
presAlt: Farm animal story: Read a simple story like 'Dear Zoo' with farm animals, pause to ask 'What can it do?'
TPR actions: Teacher does actions (eat, run, fly) and asks 'Can a cow fly?' kids respond 'No, it can't'
lp.prac: Cut-and-stick poster: Kids cut out animal pictures and labels, stick them on a farm poster, then say 'It is a sheep' and 'A sheep can eat grass'
pracAlt: Animal can/can't pelmanism: Match picture cards with sentence cards like 'A duck can swim'
Find the animal: Kids search for hidden animal cards, when found say 'It is a pig' and 'A pig can roll in mud'
lp.ls: Listen and draw: Teacher says sentences like 'Draw a cow. A cow can eat grass. A cow can't swim', kids draw and check
lp.re: Santa Says: Teacher says 'Santa says hop like a horse' or 'Santa says quack like a duck', kids do the action only if 'Santa says' is included
lp.prod: Farm animal survey: Kids walk around and ask three friends 'Can a horse fly?' and 'Can a horse run?', tally answers and report back
lp.rw: Read and match: Kids read simple sentences like 'A duck can swim' and match them to the correct animal picture, then write 'A duck can swim' on their paper
lp.st: Sing 'Old MacDonald' with actions for each animal, then do goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line
g: One child mimes an animal, others guess 'What is it?' and say what it can do
Teams race to complete sentences like 'A pig can ___' on the board
Kids draw an animal and others guess what it can do
Teacher says an animal sound and action, kids do both
Kids match baby animals to mothers and say what they can do
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 sentences about what farm animals can and can't do
Support learners: Trace the sentences 'A cow can eat grass' and match to pictures
hw: Write 3 sentences about farm animals and draw a picture
Teach 'Old MacDonald' to someone at home with actions
Make a list of 3 animals you can see in Morocco and what they can do
lp.tip: Use TPR (total physical response) to reinforce can/can't by doing actions for 'can' (thumbs up) and 'can't' (crossed arms), making abstract grammar concrete for young learners.

weeks.obj: Match wild animals to their homes and say a fact; name 4 wild animals; answer What is it? in a guessing game
weeks.lang: lion, elephant, monkey, snake; It is big/small... + has got; live in the jungle/forest
weeks.act:
Circle game: pass the ball and answer a question about wild animals and
"My wish for 2027" craft + Happy New Year song; months-of-the-year line-up game.
weeks.hw:
teach the wild animals and words to someone at home
Write your wish on the class poster template.

skills.L: Listen to animal-homes riddles
skills.S: Match and say: animals and homes with has got
skills.R: Read animal facts and complete the fact sheet
skills.W: Write one animal fact with has got

lp.wu: Circle Game: Pass the soft ball around the circle. When the music stops, the child holding the ball answers 'What animal is it?' and the class guesses.
wuAlt: Flashcard Jump: Lay animal flashcards on the floor. Children jump on the card you name and say the word.
Simon Says: Play Simon Says with actions like 'Simon says be a big lion!'
lp.pres: Show flashcards of lion, elephant, monkey, snake. Model 'It is a lion. It is big. It has got a mane. It lives in the jungle.' Ask 'Where does it live?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Story Time: Read 'Walking Through the Jungle' and stop to ask about each animal's home.
Puppet Show: Use animal puppets to ask 'What is it? It is a __.' and 'Where does it live?'
lp.prac: Pair Work: Match animal flashcards to home flashcards (jungle/forest) with the sentence 'It is a __. It lives in the __.' Support with sentence strips.
pracAlt: Board Game: Roll a dice and move. Land on a square, say the animal and its home.
Find Your Partner: Children wear animal pictures and find their home partner by saying 'I live in the __.'
lp.ls: Listen to animal-homes riddles: 'I am big and grey. I have a long nose. I live in the jungle. What am I?' Children point to the correct animal flashcard.
lp.re: Jungle Run: When you call an animal, children run to the 'jungle' corner. When you call 'snake!', they freeze. Checks listening and movement.
lp.prod: Craft: Decorate a 'My Wish for 2027' star. Write 'I wish for __.' and draw a picture. Share wishes with a partner.
lp.rw: Animal Fact Sheet: Trace and copy sentences like 'The lion has got a big mane.' Then write one original fact with 'has got'.
lp.st: Sing 'Happy New Year' with actions. End with the Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Child describes an animal with 'It is big/small. It has got __.' Class guesses.
Children line up in order of months when called, saying 'January, February...'
Pass a wrapped parcel; when music stops, name an animal and its home.
Child acts an animal, others guess 'Is it a lion?'
Teams race to match animal flashcards to home flashcards.
diff: Fast finishers: Draw a new animal and write two facts with 'has got'.
Support: Use word banks with animal and home words for the fact sheet.
hw: Teach the 4 wild animals and their homes to a family member.
Write your wish on the class poster template at home.
Draw a picture of your favorite wild animal and label it.
lp.tip: Use TTPR (Total Physical Response) for animal actions to engage kinesthetic learners and reinforce vocabulary retention.

weeks.obj: Ask for Christmas presents politely; follow the Christmas story frames; join 2 carols; review S1 topics
weeks.lang: Christmas vocabulary; review week 1-13 + I want / I would like; please/thank you routines
weeks.act: Show-and-tell: two sentences about christmas
weeks.hw: find and label 5 pictures of christmas from magazines

skills.L: Carols plus listen to the Christmas story
skills.S: I would like ___ - polite present requests roleplay
skills.R: Read the story frames and follow the party plan
skills.W: Write my Christmas present list with I would like

lp.wu: Christmas Pictionary: Teacher draws 3 Christmas words (tree, star, gift), students shout the English words. Then students draw 1 word each in pairs, guessing 'What is it? It is a __.'
wuAlt: Christmas Bingo: Students mark Christmas vocabulary pictures on their bingo cards as teacher calls words.
Christmas Memory: Students flip over flashcards to match pairs, saying 'I see a __.'
lp.pres: Teacher shows a Santa flashcard and models 'I would like a bike, please.' Students repeat. Then teacher holds a 'present' box and asks 'What would you like?' Students practice 'I would like __, please.' Teacher nods for correct requests.
presAlt: Santa's Sack: Teacher pulls out toys from a sack, asking 'What is it?' Students answer 'It is a __.'
Polite Requests Poster: Teacher writes 'I would like ___' on the board with a 'please' bubble, students fill in blanks with toy words.
lp.prac: Santa's Workshop: Students sit in groups with toy flashcards. They take turns being Santa and saying 'What would you like?' The shopper replies 'I would like a __, please.' Teacher monitors for polite language.
pracAlt: Pass the Present: Students pass a wrapped box while music plays. When it stops, they open it and say 'I would like a __, please.'
Christmas Roleplay Cards: Students draw cards with roles (child/Santa) and act out polite requests.
lp.ls: Listen and Color: Teacher describes a Christmas picture ( 'Color the star yellow. Draw a gift under the tree.') Students color their pictures, checking comprehension by raising hands for each instruction.
lp.re: Reindeer Hop: Students hop like reindeer while teacher calls 'Red reindeer!' or 'Green reindeer!' Students touch the correct colored paper on the floor.
lp.prod: Show-and-Tell Christmas: Students bring a small toy or draw a picture. They stand up and say two sentences: 'This is a __. I would like a __ for Christmas.' Teacher gives stickers for full sentences.
lp.rw: Christmas List Writing: Students trace 'I would like ___' on a worksheet, then copy 3 sentences with their desired presents (e.g., 'I would like a ball. I would like a book.'). Fast finishers draw their presents.
lp.st: Teacher reads a short Christmas story with picture frames, pausing for students to repeat key phrases like 'Merry Christmas!' Then the class sings 'Jingle Bells' with actions. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teams race to match word cards to picture cards on the board.
Students feel inside a stocking and guess 'Is it a __?' using 'Yes/No' answers.
Blindfolded students stick a red nose on a Rudolph poster, saying 'Merry Christmas!'
Students act out Christmas words (tree, gift, star) for classmates to guess.
Students roll a dice and say a Christmas word or phrase matching the number (1=tree, 2=star, etc.).
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write 5 sentences about what they would like for Christmas and why.
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank with picture clues to fill in 'I would like a __.'
hw: Find and label 5 Christmas pictures from magazines (e.g., tree, star, gift).
Draw 3 presents you would like and write 'I would like a __.' under each.
Ask your family 'What would you like for Christmas?' and draw their answers.
lp.tip: Use Moroccan Christmas context: Compare Christmas with Eid gift-giving traditions to build cultural bridges. Emphasize 'please/thank you' as universal polite routines.

weeks.obj: Show what I know in games and a short quiz; show learning through game-based observation tasks
weeks.lang: all S1 outcomes; game-based assessment + semester 1 review
weeks.act: Mixed-skills revision circuit in teams
weeks.hw: revise your notes for the assessment week

skills.L: Listen-and-circle quiz across S1 topics (Tests)
skills.S: Pair picture chat plus game-based observation
skills.R: Read-and-match quiz and word search
skills.W: Short guided writing: my favourite ___ (2 sentences)

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'Simon Says' with S1 vocabulary. Teacher says 'Simon says touch your nose', 'Simon says point to the door'. Students perform actions and repeat the phrases. Teacher praises correct responses.
wuAlt: Alternative warm-up 1: 'I spy with my little eye' using S1 objects in the classroom. Students guess 'Is it a book?'
Alternative warm-up 2: 'Quick quiz' with 3 S1 questions like 'What colour is the pen?'
lp.pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of S1 topics (animals, food, colours). Ask 'What is it?' and model 'It is a __.' Then ask 'Can you __?' (e.g. 'Can you fly?') and model 'Yes, I can.' Check understanding by asking students to repeat and answer.
presAlt: Alternative presentation 1: Use a storybook with S1 words, point to pictures and ask questions
Alternative presentation 2: Bring real objects (apple, ball) and have students name them and answer 'Can you __?'
lp.prac: Guided practice: 'Find the Match' game. Students work in pairs with picture and word cards. They take turns saying 'What is it?' and 'It is a __.' Teacher monitors and helps with pronunciation.
pracAlt: Alternative practice 1: 'Action Drill' - students stand up and perform actions (jump, run) while saying 'I can jump'
Alternative practice 2: 'Chain Game' - students say 'I like __' and the next student repeats and adds one more
lp.ls: Listening slot: 'Listen and Circle' quiz. Teacher plays audio with S1 sentences (e.g. 'Point to the red apple'). Students circle the correct picture on their worksheet. Checks listening comprehension of key vocabulary.
lp.re: Reactivation game: 'Musical Statues'. Play music, students dance. When music stops, teacher calls out an S1 word (e.g. 'book') and students freeze in the shape of that object. Says 'What is it?' and students respond.
lp.prod: Production task: 'Pair Picture Chat'. Students work in pairs with a picture scene. They take turns asking 'What is it?' and answering 'It is a __.' and 'Can you __?' Teacher listens and assesses speaking skills.
lp.rw: Reading and writing slot: 'Read and Match' quiz. Students match S1 words to pictures. Then 'My favourite ___' writing: students trace, then copy, then write two sentences like 'My favourite animal is a cat. It is big.'
lp.st: Story / song + goodbye: Read a short S1 story about a day. Then sing 'Goodbye Song' with actions. End with sticker chart and high-five line. Teacher says 'Good job today!'
g: Students have S1 pictures on cards. Teacher calls words, students mark and shout 'Bingo!' when complete
Teams race to grab the right flashcard when teacher says a word
Student mimes an S1 word, others guess 'Is it a __?'
Students turn over cards to find matching picture-word pairs
Teams answer S1 questions for points
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write 3 sentences about their favourite S1 topic
Support / weaker learners: Trace words and match to pictures with a word bank
hw: Homework option 1: Draw 3 S1 things and write the words
Homework option 2: Play 'I spy' with family at home
Homework option 3: Practice 'What is it?' with a family member
lp.tip: Use the sticker chart to reward effort, not just accuracy, to build confidence. For Moroccan learners, include local words like 'tagine' or ' couscous' where appropriate.
checklist: I can say 'What is it?' and answer 'It is a __.'
I can ask 'Can you __?' and answer 'Yes, I can.'
I can understand and circle S1 words in a listening quiz
I can read and match S1 words to pictures
I can write 2 sentences about my favourite thing
I can play a game using S1 words
I can take part in a pair chat

weeks.obj: Name body parts and say what hurts; name 8 body parts and touch them on command
weeks.lang: head, shoulders, knees, arms, hands, feet, eyes, ears + have got + body; My ... hurts
weeks.act: Pair picture dictation with this week's words
weeks.hw: read your my body mini-book to someone at home

skills.L: Head, Shoulders song plus listen for the body part that hurts
skills.S: Name body parts; say what hurts: My ___ hurts
skills.R: Read body words and label the monster poster
skills.W: Write 4 body words; complete My ___ hurts frames

lp.wu: Simon Says: Teacher calls out 'Simon says touch your head/shoulders/knees/arms/hands/feet/eyes/ears'. Students touch the correct body part. Teacher says 'My head hurts' and pretends to hold it, students repeat.
wuAlt: Body Part Bingo: Teacher shows flashcards, students shout 'Bingo!' when they have 3 in a row on their grid.
Action Charades: Student mimes a body part, others guess 'It is your ___!'.
lp.pres: Teacher holds flashcards of body parts, says 'This is my head' and points to own head, students repeat. Teacher draws a sad face on the board, points to head, says 'My head hurts', students repeat. Teacher asks 'What is it? It is a ___.' for each flashcard.
presAlt: Storytime: Read 'My Body' book, point to each body part and say the word. Students repeat.
TPR Drill: Teacher does actions (touch head, clap hands) and says the word, students copy.
lp.prac: Picture Dictation: Student A has a picture of a monster, Student B has a blank paper. Student A says 'Draw a big head', Student B draws. They swap roles using target body parts.
pracAlt: Memory Game: Flashcards are face down. Students take turns turning two over, saying 'It is a ___' if they match.
Body Part Relay: Teams race to touch body parts on flashcards pinned to the wall.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher says 'Draw a circle for the head. Draw two circles for the eyes. Draw a circle for the stomach.' Students draw and label. Teacher checks each drawing.
lp.re: Musical Body Parts: Play music, students dance. When music stops, teacher shouts a body part, students must touch it. Last one out is 'it'.
lp.prod: Doctor Roleplay: Students work in pairs. One is the doctor, one is the patient. Patient says 'My ___ hurts', Doctor says 'Touch your ___'. They swap roles.
lp.rw: Label the Monster: Students trace body part words (head, shoulders, etc.) from the board onto a monster poster. Then they copy 4 words into their notebook.
lp.st: Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes song: Sing slowly, then faster. End with 'Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line'.
g: Teacher calls out body parts, students touch them if 'Simon says'.
Students mark off body parts on their bingo cards as teacher calls them.
Students touch body parts when music stops.
Patient says 'My ___ hurts', Doctor says 'Touch your ___'.
Students trace and copy body words onto a poster.
diff: Fast finishers: Draw a monster with 8 body parts and label them all.
Support: Use word bank with pictures for labeling activity.
hw: Read your 'My Body' mini-book to someone at home and point to the body parts.
Ask 3 family members 'What is your favourite body part?' and write their answers.
Play 'Simon Says' with a brother or sister.
lp.tip: Use exaggerated facial expressions when demonstrating 'My ___ hurts' to convey meaning without translation. Connect to local culture by discussing how to say 'I have a headache' in Darija.

weeks.obj: Mime and guess action verbs; understand and produce 8 action verbs with TPR
weeks.lang: clap, jump, run, walk, swim, fly, eat, sleep + can/can't + action verbs; jump, clap, swim
weeks.act: Mini-survey: ask 3 friends about actions and movement and report back
weeks.hw: write the actions and movement words twice in your notebook, once in rainbow colours

skills.L: Listen to can/can't ability sentences about actions
skills.S: Mime and guess actions; report with the verb
skills.R: Read action sentences and match to the mimes
skills.W: Write can/can't sentences about 3 actions

lp.wu: Simon Says: Teacher says 'Simon says clap' and students clap; 'Simon says jump' and students jump; 'Simon says swim' and students swim; 'Simon says fly' and students pretend to fly; 'Simon says sleep' and students pretend to sleep.
wuAlt: Action Charades: Teacher mimes an action (e.g., run) and students guess 'You run!'
Flashcard Race: Show flashcards of actions quickly, students say the word.
lp.pres: Use flashcards of the 8 action verbs (clap, jump, run, walk, swim, fly, eat, sleep); teacher mimes each action and says the word; students repeat; ask 'Can you swim?' and students respond 'Yes, I can' or 'No, I can't'; check understanding with thumbs up/down.
presAlt: TPR Story: Tell a story about a boy who can run, jump, and swim, using flashcards to illustrate each action
Video Clip: Show a short video of animals doing actions, pause and ask 'What is it? It is a __.'
lp.prac: Mime and Guess: Students work in pairs, one student mimes an action, the other guesses 'You __!' (e.g., 'You jump!'); teacher circulates to correct pronunciation; play 'Action Charades' with the whole class.
pracAlt: Action Bingo: Students draw a 3x3 grid and write 6 action verbs; teacher calls out actions, students cross them off; first to get a line wins
Action Relay: Divide class into teams, one student runs to the board, writes an action verb, runs back, next student mimes it.
lp.ls: Listen and Match: Teacher says sentences like 'I can swim' or 'I can't fly'; students hold up the correct flashcard; check comprehension by asking 'Can you fly?' and students respond with thumbs up/down.
lp.re: Action Dance: Play a short song with actions (e.g., 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes'), students stand up and do the actions; after the break, do the dance again to re-energize.
lp.prod: Mini-Survey: Students ask 3 friends 'Can you __?' (e.g., 'Can you jump?'); friends respond 'Yes, I can' or 'No, I can't'; students report back to the class 'Ali can jump, but Sara can't swim.'
lp.rw: Trace and Copy: Students trace the 8 action verbs in their notebook; then copy them once in rainbow colours; write 3 sentences like 'I can clap' or 'I can't fly'.
lp.st: Read 'The Hungry Caterpillar' story focusing on actions like 'eat' and 'sleep'; sing the 'Hello Song' and 'Goodbye Song'; end with sticker chart and high-five line.
g: Teacher gives commands with 'Simon says' and students follow; if no 'Simon says', they don't move
Student mimes an action, others guess the verb
Students cross off verbs as teacher calls them
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 sentences about what they can and can't do
Support: Use word bank with pictures to help write sentences
hw: Write the 8 action verbs twice in rainbow colours
Draw a picture of yourself doing 3 actions and write the words
Ask your family members 'Can you __?' and write down their answers
lp.tip: Use local context: reference Moroccan festivals like Green March by asking 'Can you march?' to connect the theme to students' culture.

weeks.obj: Say which fruit I like and don't like; name 6 fruits; answer Do you like...? with yes/no
weeks.lang: apple, banana, orange, grapes, strawberry, lemon + I like / I don't like + fruit; Do you like...?
weeks.act: Make a mini-book about fruit and read it to a partner
weeks.hw: write 3 sentences about fruit and draw a picture

skills.L: Apples and Bananas plus fruit listening bingo
skills.S: Fruit likes survey - ask 3 friends and report back
skills.R: Read fruit words and match to the basket
skills.W: Write likes: I like ___; I don't like ___

lp.wu: Fruit Charades: Teacher acts out a fruit (e.g., peeling a banana), students guess 'Is it a banana?' and the class responds 'Yes, it is!' or 'No, it isn!'
wuAlt: Fruit Memory Game: Students match picture and word flashcards for fruits, saying 'Apple' when they find a pair
Fruit I Spy: Teacher says 'I spy with my little eye something red and round', students guess 'Is it an apple?'
lp.pres: Teacher shows real fruits or large flashcards of apple, banana, orange, grapes, strawberry, lemon, saying 'This is an apple. I like apples.' Students repeat. Teacher asks 'Do you like apples?' and models 'Yes, I do' or 'No, I don't'. Students point to thumbs up/down to show understanding.
presAlt: Fruit Story: Teacher reads a simple story about a monkey who likes bananas but not lemons, using target language
Fruit Bingo Prep: Teacher calls out fruits, students mark them on a bingo grid, saying 'I like grapes' when they mark
lp.prac: Fruit Likes Survey: Students walk around with a paper asking 'Do you like apples?' to 3 friends, tick yes/no, and report back to teacher 'Ali likes apples. Fatima doesn't like lemons.' Teacher provides sentence frames on the board.
pracAlt: Fruit Dominoes: Students match picture cards to word cards, saying 'Apple' when they place a card
Fruit Board Game: Students roll a dice, move a counter, and say 'I like/ don't like [fruit]' when they land on a square
lp.ls: Fruit Listening Bingo: Teacher calls out 'I like strawberries' or 'I don't like lemons', students cover the corresponding picture on their bingo card. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
lp.re: Fruit Relay: Two lines of students race to the board, draw a fruit, and run back. Team with most correct drawings in 2 minutes wins.
lp.prod: Make a Mini-Book: Students fold 3 sheets of paper into a book, draw 6 fruits on each page, write 'I like ___' or 'I don't like ___' under each, and read it to a partner using a pointer.
lp.rw: Trace and Copy: Students trace fruit words from a worksheet, then copy them into sentences. Advanced learners write 'I like apples. I don't like lemons.' with a drawing.
lp.st: Read 'The Very Hungry Caterpillar' focusing on fruit pages, then sing 'Apples and Bananas' song replacing vowels. End with Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students act out fruits for others to guess
Students match picture and word cards for fruits
Teacher calls out likes/dislikes, students cover pictures
Teams race to draw fruits on the board
Ask friends about likes and report back
diff: Fast finishers: Write a short story about a fruit monster who likes all fruits
Support: Use word banks with pictures for writing sentences
hw: Draw 3 fruits and write 'I like ___' or 'I don't like ___' under each
Make a fruit collage and label each fruit
Interview your family about fruit likes and write down 3 answers
lp.tip: Use real fruits when possible to engage tactile learners and build vocabulary retention through multisensory input.

weeks.theme: Food 2: I like / I don't like
weeks.obj: Ask a friend about food they like; talk about food likes and dislikes in simple sentences
weeks.lang: I like... / I do not like...; yum! yuck! + Does he/she like...? Yes, he does / No, he doesn't
weeks.act:
Guessing game: teams ask questions about food
Ramadan routines vocab (suhoor, iftar, mosque); days-of-the-week fasting chart craft.
weeks.hw:
teach the food words to someone at home
Draw your iftar table and label 5 foods in English.

skills.L: Listen to Does he/she like...? mini-dialogues
skills.S: Ask about a friend's food likes and report to class
skills.R: Read third-person like sentences and match
skills.W: Write about a friend: He likes... She does not like...

lp.wu: Food Charades: Teacher shows flashcards of food, mimes eating it, kids shout 'yum!' or 'yuck!' and guess 'Is it [food]?'
wuAlt: Pass the Plate: Play music, pass a paper plate, stop and child says 'I like [food]' or 'I do not like [food]'.
Flashcard Race: Two teams race to match 'yum!' and 'yuck!' flashcards to food pictures.
lp.pres: Teacher holds up a Ramadan plate with dates, milk, harira, msemen; models 'I like dates. Yum!' and 'I do not like cucumber. Yuck!'; kids repeat, then ask 'Do you like [food]?' to teacher.
presAlt: Storytime: Read 'Samira's Ramadan' book, point to food pictures and ask 'Does Samira like [food]?' kids say 'Yes/No'.
Realia: Bring in suhoor items (bread, cheese) and iftar items (dates, juice), kids touch and say 'I like...'.
lp.prac: Guess the Food: Teams take turns, one child thinks of a food, others ask 'Does he/she like [food]?'; guesser says 'Yes, he does' or 'No, he doesn't' until correct.
pracAlt: Food Survey: Kids walk around with a paper asking 3 friends 'Do you like [food]?' and tally answers with ticks.
Memory Game: Place food cards face down, kids turn two over and say 'I like...' or 'I do not like...' for each.
lp.ls: Listen and Tick: Play a dialogue of two kids talking about food ('Do you like milk?' 'Yes, I do!'); kids listen and tick 'yum' or 'yuck' on their worksheet.
lp.re: Food Relay: Two lines, teacher calls a food, first kid runs to touch the flashcard and shouts 'I like [food]!' or 'I do not like [food]!'.
lp.prod: Iftar Table Craft: Kids draw their family's iftar table, label 5 foods in English, then present to partner 'This is my iftar table. I like... She does not like...'.
lp.rw: Trace and Write: Kids trace 'He likes milk' and 'She does not like bread' sentences, then copy them 3 times; read a short text about Ramadan meals and match foods to 'yum'/'yuck'.
lp.st: Goodbye Song: 'If You're Happy and You Know It' with food verses ('If you like apples, clap your hands!'); sticker chart for participation, high-five line as they exit.
g: Teacher calls 'I like pizza!', kids cover the pizza picture on their bingo card.
Kids find someone who likes a food and say 'Do you like [food]?' then high-five.
Teams race to put food cards in 'yum' or 'yuck' baskets.
Teacher removes a food from a tray, kids guess 'Is it [food]?' with 'Yes/No'.
Child mimes eating and others guess 'Does he/she like [food]?'
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 more sentences about their family's food likes.
Support: Use word banks with food pictures and 'yum'/'yuck' labels for the craft.
hw: Teach 5 food words to your family and draw their reactions.
Draw your suhoor plate and label 3 foods in English.
Ask your parents about their favorite Ramadan food and write 'He likes...' or 'She likes...'.
lp.tip: Use Ramadan as a bridge to connect the food theme with local culture; praise kids for using full sentences, even if imperfect.

weeks.obj: Describe what someone is wearing; name 6 clothing items; say I am wearing...
weeks.lang: t-shirt, trousers, dress, shoes, hat, jacket + present continuous (he/she is wearing)
weeks.act: Cut-and-stick poster with clothes labels
weeks.hw: find and label 5 pictures of clothes from magazines

skills.L: Clothing Song plus present-continuous listening
skills.S: Describe what someone is wearing (guess who)
skills.R: Read clothing sentences and dress the paper doll
skills.W: Write He/She is wearing ___ sentences

lp.wu: Flashcard Race: Students stand in two lines. Teacher shows a clothing flashcard (e.g., 'hat'). The first student in each line runs to the board, draws the item, and says 'It is a hat.'
wuAlt: TPR Simon Says: Teacher says 'Simon says touch your shoes' and students touch the correct clothing item on their bodies.
Memory Game: Students sit in a circle. Teacher says 'I am wearing a jacket' and each student adds one item, e.g., 'I am wearing a jacket and shoes.'
lp.pres: Teacher wears a funny outfit (e.g., over-sized hat, mismatched shoes). Points to each item and says 'I am wearing a hat.' 'He is wearing a jacket.' Uses flashcards to drill 6 clothing items. Checks understanding by asking 'What am I wearing?' and students point.
presAlt: Storybook: Read 'The Mixed-Up Chameleon' but replace animals with clothing items. Teacher says 'He is wearing a dress.'
Realia Show: Teacher brings a bag of clothes. Students pull one out and say 'It is a __.'
lp.prac: Pairwork: Students get a worksheet with 3 people. They take turns saying 'He is wearing trousers.' 'She is wearing a dress.' Teacher monitors and helps with pronunciation.
pracAlt: Bingo: Teacher calls out clothing items. Students cover the picture on their bingo card. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Flashcard Guess: Student picks a flashcard without showing. Others ask 'Is it a hat?' and they answer 'Yes/No.'
lp.ls: Clothing Song: Students listen to 'What Are You Wearing?' and point to their own clothes. Then listen again and draw 3 items they hear in a notebook.
lp.re: Clothing Relay: Students line up. Teacher whispers 'Run to the board and draw shoes.' First student draws and says 'Shoes!'
lp.prod: Guess Who: Students take turns describing a classmate's outfit. 'He is wearing a blue jacket and a hat.' Others guess who it is.
lp.rw: Paper Doll Dress-Up: Students get a paper doll and 6 clothing stickers. They dress the doll and write sentences like 'She is wearing a dress.'
lp.st: Story: Read 'Elmer's New Clothes' by David McKee. Sing 'Goodbye Song' and give stickers. Line up for high-fives.
g: Teacher calls a clothing item. Students jump to the flashcard on the floor.
Student mimes wearing an item. Others guess 'He is wearing a jacket.'
Teacher says 'Find someone wearing shoes.' Students link arms.
Teacher says 'Draw a boy wearing a hat.' Students draw and check.
Teacher shows 3 flashcards. Students close eyes. Teacher removes one. Students say 'The hat is missing.'
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 sentences about what their family member is wearing.
Support: Trace the words 'shoes', 'hat', 'dress' in their notebook.
hw: Cut out 5 clothes pictures from a magazine and stick them in a notebook. Write the word under each.
Draw a picture of yourself. Label 3 things you are wearing.
Ask your family 'What are you wearing?' and write 2 sentences.
lp.tip: Use local context: Bring in a djellaba or gandora to compare with 'jacket' and 'dress'. Link to Green March or Independence Day by describing traditional festival clothes.

weeks.obj: Talk about today's weather and what I wear; recognize 4 weather words and report today's weather
weeks.lang: sunny, rainy, windy, cloudy; What is the weather like? + It's raining/sunny; wear + clothes
weeks.act: Circle game: pass the ball and answer a question about weather and seasons
weeks.hw: play the matching game in the weather and seasons library folder with a family member

skills.L: Weather listening - match reports to pictures
skills.S: Talk about today's weather and what I wear
skills.R: Read weather words and complete the weather chart
skills.W: Write Today it is ___; complete the chart

lp.wu: Weather Ball Toss: Students stand in a circle, pass a soft ball, and say 'Today it is sunny/rainy/windy/cloudy' when they catch it. Teacher models first, then students repeat.
wuAlt: Weather Charades: Teacher acts out a weather type (e.g., pretending to shiver for cold), students guess 'Is it rainy? Is it windy?'
Flashcard Quick Review: Show weather flashcards rapidly, students call out the word.
lp.pres: Teacher shows a storybook about a boy checking the weather each day, using flashcards for 'sunny, rainy, windy, cloudy'. Model 'What is the weather like? It's sunny.' Students repeat chorally. Check with thumbs-up/down: 'Is it sunny?'
presAlt: Realia Weather Box: Teacher pulls out sunglasses (sunny), umbrella (rainy), scarf (windy), cloud (cloudy) and asks 'What is the weather like?'
Weather Song Video: Play a short, simple weather song with gestures, students repeat the words and actions.
lp.prac: Weather Bingo: Students get bingo cards with weather pictures. Teacher calls out 'It's rainy!' students cover the picture. Support: Teacher gestures while calling.
pracAlt: Pair Weather Dialogue: Students A/B ask 'What is the weather like?' and answer 'It's sunny/windy/etc.' using flashcards for support.
Weather Dice Game: Roll a die with weather pictures, students say the sentence and mime the action (e.g., 'It's windy' + blowing).
lp.ls: Listen and Match: Teacher plays 4 short audio clips (e.g., 'rain sounds', 'wind sounds', 'sunshine sounds', 'cloud sounds'). Students match the clip to the correct picture on their worksheet.
lp.re: Weather Action Relay: In two teams, students race to the board to draw a weather picture (sun, rain, wind, cloud) when called out. 'Draw sunny! Go!'
lp.prod: My Weather Report: Students draw today's weather and write 'Today it is ___.' in their notebooks. Then, in pairs, they present their report to each other: 'Today it is sunny. I wear a T-shirt.'
lp.rw: Weather Chart: Students read a simple chart with weather words and icons (e.g., 'Sun = sunny', 'Cloud = cloudy'). They trace the words, then copy them into their own chart.
lp.st: Story: 'The Weather Monster' by Annie Rose (or similar). Students guess the weather as the story progresses. End with 'Goodbye Song' + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Pass the ball and say a weather sentence
Draw weather pictures on the board
Act out weather for others to guess
diff: Fast finishers: Draw and write about their favourite weather.
Support: Trace weather words with dotted lines.
hw: Play the matching game in the weather library folder with a family member.
Draw the weather for 3 days and write the word.
Ask family 'What is the weather like?' and write their answers.
lp.tip: Use gestures and TPR heavily for weather words (e.g., arms up for sunny, hands down for rainy) to reinforce meaning and cater to kinesthetic learners.

weeks.obj: Describe my pet with have got and can; say I have got a (pet) and ask And you?
weeks.lang: cat, dog, bird, fish; I have got... Have you got...? + have got + body parts; It can...
weeks.act: Show-and-tell: two sentences about pets and I have got
weeks.hw: read your pets and I have got mini-book to someone at home

skills.L: Listen to pet descriptions with have got and can
skills.S: Pet show-and-tell: describe my pet in 2 sentences
skills.R: Read pet facts and match to animals
skills.W: Write about a pet with have got + can

lp.wu: Flashcard Jump: Students jump when they see a pet flashcard and say 'I have got a cat/dog/bird/fish!' Teacher holds up flashcards one by one.
wuAlt: Pet Charades: Students act out a pet and classmates guess 'Have you got a dog?'
Pet Memory Game: Students match pet flashcards and say 'I have got a fish!' when they find a pair.
lp.pres: Teacher shows a stuffed dog and says 'I have got a dog. It can run!' Then points to a cat and asks 'Have you got a cat?' Students practice asking each other with flashcards.
presAlt: Story 'My Pet': Teacher reads a simple story about pets with 'I have got...' and 'It can...' sentences, using flashcards to illustrate.
TPR Pet Actions: Teacher says 'It can fly!' and flaps arms for bird, 'It can swim!' for fish, students copy and repeat.
lp.prac: Find My Pet Game: Students hide pet flashcards around the room. Teacher says 'Find the dog!' and students bring it back saying 'I have got a dog!'
pracAlt: Pet Survey: Students walk around asking 'Have you got a dog?' and tally answers on a simple chart.
Match the Cards: Students match pet pictures to sentences like 'I have got a bird. It can fly.'
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes pets ('I have got a cat. It can climb.') and students draw the correct pet, then hold up their drawings.
lp.re: Pet Relay: Teams race to place flashcards on the board when teacher calls out 'I have got a dog!' or 'It can swim!'
lp.prod: Show-and-Tell: Each student brings a toy or drawing of a pet and says two sentences: 'I have got a __. It can __.'
lp.rw: Trace and Copy: Students trace sentences like 'I have got a dog.' from the board, then copy them into their notebooks with a drawing.
lp.st: Story 'The Pet Show': Teacher reads a story with repeated 'I have got...' and 'It can...' lines. End with 'Goodbye Song' and sticker chart.
g: Students cover pictures on bingo cards when teacher says 'I have got a cat!'
Student describes a pet with 'It can...' and classmates guess
Students play shopkeeper and customer: 'Have you got a dog?'
Students match pet cards and say 'I have got a fish!'
Students act out pet actions when teacher says 'It can swim!'
diff: Fast finishers: Write three sentences about their dream pet.
Support: Use sentence frames with pictures to help them talk.
hw: Read your 'Pets and I have got' mini-book to a family member.
Draw a pet and write 'I have got a __. It can __.'
Ask five family members 'Have you got a pet?' and tell the class next week.
lp.tip: Use local pets like goats or birds to connect with students' lives; praise effort with stickers to build confidence.

weeks.obj: Read and write N-T words with blends; link letters N-T to sounds and build 3-letter words
weeks.lang: letter-sound links N-T; word building: cat, pen... + blends st, sp, sn; stop, spin, snake
weeks.act:
Matching race with phonics word and picture cards
Eid greetings roleplay "Eid Mubarak!"; gift-and-cookie counting game.
weeks.hw:
write the phonics words twice in your notebook, once in rainbow colours
Write the Eid greeting card we started in class.

skills.L: Phonics songs; listen for the st, sp, sn blends
skills.S: Build and say blend words in pairs
skills.R: Read blend words and sort them by blend
skills.W: Write N-T words with blends (Worksheets)

lp.wu: Phonics Pictionary: Teacher draws a picture of a cat on the board, kids shout 'cat!' and spell it. Teacher draws a pen, kids shout 'pen!' and spell it. Teacher draws a snake, kids shout 'snake!' and spell it.
wuAlt: Phonics Bingo: Kids have bingo cards with pictures of cat, pen, snake. Teacher calls out 'C-A-T!', kids cover the cat picture.
Action Phonics: Teacher says 'Show me a cat!' kids act like a cat. 'Show me a pen!' kids pretend to write. 'Show me a snake!' kids slither.
lp.pres: Teacher shows flashcards for 'stop', 'spin', 'snake'. Teacher models the sounds /st/, /sp/, /sn/. Kids repeat the sounds after the teacher. Teacher points to the letters in each word and says 'S-T-stop', 'S-P-spin', 'S-N-snake'. Kids repeat the letter-sound links.
presAlt: Story Time: Teacher reads a short story about a snake that spins and stops. Teacher points to the words 'snake', 'spin', 'stop' as she reads them.
Realia: Teacher shows a toy snake, a spinning top, and a stop sign. Teacher says 'This is a snake. S-N-snake. This is a spin. S-P-spin. This is a stop. S-T-stop.'
lp.prac: Matching Race: Kids are in two teams. Each team gets a set of phonics word cards (stop, spin, snake) and picture cards. On 'Go!', the first kid from each team runs to the board, matches a word card to a picture card, and says the word. The team that matches all cards first wins.
pracAlt: Phonics Hopscotch: Draw a hopscotch grid with letters S, T, P, N. Teacher calls out a word like 'stop'. Kids jump on S, then T, then P, and say the word.
Build-a-Word: Kids get letter tiles. Teacher calls out a word like 'spin'. Kids build the word with their tiles and say it.
lp.ls: Listen and Circle: Teacher plays a recording of words: 'cat', 'pen', 'stop', 'spin', 'snake', 'dog'. Kids listen and circle the words on their worksheet that have the N-T sounds or st, sp, sn blends.
lp.re: Freeze Dance: Play music. Kids dance. When the music stops, the teacher calls out a word like 'stop'. Kids must freeze and say 'stop!'. If they move, they sit down.
lp.prod: Eid Greetings Roleplay: Kids work in pairs. One kid is giving a gift. The other kid is receiving it. The giver says 'Eid Mubarak! This is for you.' The receiver says 'Thank you! Eid Mubarak!' They practice the dialogue twice, then swap roles.
lp.rw: Worksheet: Kids trace the words 'stop', 'spin', 'snake' in their notebook. Then they copy the words once. Finally, they write the words once on their own. For fast finishers, they draw a picture next to each word.
lp.st: Story Time: Teacher reads a short story about a snake celebrating Eid. The snake spins and stops to eat cookies. After the story, the class sings the 'Goodbye Song'. Teacher gives out stickers for good work. Kids line up for a high-five.
g: Kids flip over word cards and picture cards. They take turns flipping two cards to find a match.
Teams race to write a blend word (stop, spin, snake) on the board.
Kids count cookies on a worksheet and say 'I have 3 cookies.'
Teacher says 'I spy with my little eye something that starts with /sp/.' Kids guess 'spin!'
Kids match pictures of gifts to the words 'gift' and 'cookie'.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a sentence using one of the phonics words, e.g., 'The snake can spin.'
Support / weaker learners: Trace the letters with their finger on a flashcard while saying the sound.
hw: Write the phonics words 'stop', 'spin', 'snake' twice in your notebook, once in rainbow colours.
Finish the Eid greeting card we started in class. Draw a picture of a gift and write 'Eid Mubarak!'
Ask your family 'What is your favourite cookie?' and tell me the answer in class.
lp.tip: Use the Eid theme to make phonics practice culturally relevant. Kids are more motivated to learn words like 'gift' and 'cookie' when connected to a celebration they know.

weeks.obj: Put U-Z words in alphabetical order; complete the alphabet with sounds U-Z; sing the alphabet song
weeks.lang: letter-sound links U-Z; alphabetical order + alphabet order; first/last letter
weeks.act: Pair picture dictation with this week's words
weeks.hw: write 3 sentences about phonics and draw a picture

skills.L: ABC song; listen for alphabetical neighbours
skills.S: Alphabetical-order team race with speaking turns
skills.R: Order U-Z words alphabetically on cards
skills.W: Write words in ABC order; complete my chart

lp.wu: Alphabet Relay: Students line up in two teams. Teacher calls out a letter (U-Z), first student runs to the board, writes it, runs back, tags next player. Team with all letters wins. They shout 'U, V, W, we are the best!'
wuAlt: Letter Jump: Teacher holds flashcards U-Z, students jump when they hear their letter's sound
Alphabet Chain: One student says 'U', next says 'V', continue until Z
lp.pres: Teacher displays flashcards umbrella, violin, window, xylophone, yellow, zebra. Models 'U is for umbrella /ʌ/, V is for violin /v/' etc. Students repeat. Teacher asks 'What is it? It is a __.' Students answer. Checks understanding by holding up random cards.
presAlt: Storytime: Read 'The Umbrella and the Zebra' with U-Z words, point to letters as they appear
Mystery Box: Students reach in, pull out object (toy violin), say letter and sound
lp.prac: Pair Picture Dictation: Student A has U-Z pictures, Student B has alphabet chart. A says 'Write umbrella under U', B writes word under correct letter. Swap roles. Teacher monitors and helps with spelling.
pracAlt: Alphabet Order Race: Teams get shuffled U-Z word cards, first to line them up alphabetically wins
Sound Match: Students match U-Z picture cards to sound cards on the board
lp.ls: Alphabet Neighbors Game: Teacher plays a recording of mixed U-Z letter sounds. Students hold up two cards when they hear neighbors (e.g., V and W). Teacher checks pairs.
lp.re: Alphabet Jump Rope: Students jump while chanting 'U, V, W, X, Y, Z', stop when teacher claps. Last one out does a silly dance.
lp.prod: My Alphabet Chart: Students trace U-Z letters in a chart, then write 3 words under each (from flashcards). They share with partner 'This is umbrella, U-U-Umbrella!'
lp.rw: Write in Order: Students write 5 U-Z words on slips, mix them, then reorder alphabetically. Copy sentences: 'Umbrella starts with U. Zebra starts with Z.'
lp.st: Sing the Alphabet Song with actions (U: open arms like umbrella, Z: roar like zebra). Story: 'The Zebra's Umbrella' with U-Z focus. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students cover pictures when teacher calls out U-Z sounds
Teacher says 'Line up from U to Z!', students race to order themselves
Jump on correct letter when teacher says sound
Find U-Z words hidden in classroom, say letter and sound
Students say 'I spy with my little eye, something beginning with U'
diff: Fast finishers: Write a sentence with 2 U-Z words and draw a picture
Support: Trace letters with dotted lines, use word bank for spelling
hw: Write 3 sentences: 'U is for umbrella. V is for violin. Z is for zebra.' Draw pictures
Make flashcards for U-Z words with pictures and sounds
Practice the alphabet song with family, teach them the actions
lp.tip: Use Moroccan context: show pictures of 'umbrella' for sun protection, 'violin' in local music. Link to Green March by saying 'Z is for zero, like the start of our march!'

weeks.obj: Talk about an Easter story and spring words; review colors, numbers, animals through seasonal games
weeks.lang: review weeks 16-24 language + Easter words; There is/are with spring pictures
weeks.act: Mixed-skills revision circuit in teams
weeks.hw: revise your notes for the assessment week

skills.L: Listen to an Easter story and sequence the pictures
skills.S: Talk about Easter words; There is/There are games
skills.R: Read spring sentences and match to pictures
skills.W: Write 2 spring sentences with There is / There are

lp.wu: Easter Egg Hunt: Hide 10 plastic eggs with spring pictures inside. Kids search, find, and say 'I found a __!' with the picture (e.g., 'I found a butterfly!').
wuAlt: Spring Bingo: Call out spring words; kids cover the matching pictures on their bingo cards.
TPR Spring Actions: Kids jump like bunnies, flap like butterflies, and hop like lambs as the teacher says the words.
lp.pres: Show a picture story of 'The Easter Bunny' with flashcards. Model sentences: 'The Easter bunny has eggs.' 'There is a carrot.' Kids repeat and point to the pictures. Ask 'What is it?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Realia Show: Bring a basket with plastic eggs, a bunny toy, and flowers. Say 'There is a __' for each item, kids repeat.
Spring Song: Sing 'Spring is Here' with gestures, pause and ask kids to fill in the words (e.g., 'Spring is here, the __ are green').
lp.prac: Picture Pair Game: Kids work in pairs. Each pair gets a spring picture. They ask 'What is there?' and answer 'There is a __.' Teacher monitors and helps with pronunciation.
pracAlt: Easter Egg Pass: Pass a plastic egg around the circle. Kids say a spring word when they hold it (e.g., 'flower', 'sun').
There is/Are Board Game: Roll a dice, move, and make a sentence about the space they land on (e.g., 'There is a bee').
lp.ls: Listen to a short audio story about a spring day. Kids have picture cards and sequence them in order as they hear the story (e.g., 'First, there is a sun. Then, there are flowers.')
lp.re: Spring Charades: Kids act out spring words (e.g., 'planting', 'flying a kite') while others guess 'Are you a __?'
lp.prod: Spring Poster Project: Kids draw a spring scene and label 3 things with 'There is a __' or 'There are __.' They present their posters to the class.
lp.rw: Read and Match: Kids read simple sentences like 'There is a yellow chick.' and match them to the correct pictures. Then, they trace 2 sentences and copy them into their notebooks.
lp.st: Read 'The Happy Easter Bunny' storybook with repetitive phrases. Sing 'Goodbye, Goodbye' song and do the sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teams race to carry an egg on a spoon and say a spring word at the end.
Match picture cards with word cards (e.g., 'butterfly' + picture).
Teacher removes 1 item from a spring display; kids say 'There is no __.'
Roll a dice with spring pictures; say a sentence about the picture.
Kids say 'I spy with my little eye, something __' (e.g., 'yellow').
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 more sentences about their spring poster.
Support: Trace dotted words for their sentences.
hw: Draw your favorite spring thing and write 'There is a __.'
Ask 3 family members 'What is your favorite spring word?' and write them down.
Play 'Spring I Spy' with a family member.
lp.tip: Use local spring imagery (e.g., blooming almond trees) to connect with Moroccan learners and make the theme relatable.

weeks.obj: Say what rooms there are in my house; name 4 rooms and say where simple things are
weeks.lang: house, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom; Where is mummy? She is in the... + there is/there are + rooms
weeks.act: Make a mini-book about my house and read it to a partner
weeks.hw: find and label 5 pictures of my house from magazines

skills.L: Listen to a house tour and point to the right room
skills.S: Say what rooms my house has: There is / There are
skills.R: Read room sentences and match to the house plan
skills.W: Write There is / There are about my house

lp.wu: Simon Says with house parts: 'Simon says touch the kitchen!' 'Simon says point to the bedroom!' Students jump and say the room name when correct.
wuAlt: Flashcard Race: Show room flashcards, students race to touch the whiteboard and say the name.
Find the Room: Call out a room, students find the matching picture card on their table.
lp.pres: Use a big house poster to show rooms. Teacher says: 'This is a house. A house has rooms. This is the kitchen. This is the bedroom. This is the bathroom.' Ask: 'Where is mummy?' Students point and say: 'She is in the kitchen.'
presAlt: Storytime: Read 'My House' story, point to rooms. Ask: 'Where is the cat?' Students answer: 'In the bedroom.'
TPR Tour: Walk around the room, pretend to cook in 'kitchen', sleep in 'bedroom', wash in 'bathroom', say sentences.
lp.prac: Make a mini-book: Students fold paper into 4 sections. Draw kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, living room. Write 'There is a kitchen' etc. Read to partner: 'This is my house. There is a kitchen.'
pracAlt: House Plan Match: Give house plan with rooms blank. Students listen: 'There is a bedroom' and draw it in the right place.
Find and Stick: Students have room stickers. Teacher says: 'Put the kitchen in the house.' Students stick and say: 'There is a kitchen.'
lp.ls: Listen to a house tour audio: 'Look! This is the kitchen. Mummy is in the kitchen.' Students point to the kitchen on their house poster. Check if they point correctly.
lp.re: Room Jump: Call out a room, students jump to the flashcard on the floor. Say: 'I jump to the bedroom!'
lp.prod: My House Show and Tell: Students use their mini-book. Stand up, point to a room, say: 'This is my house. There is a bedroom. Mummy is in the bedroom.'
lp.rw: Trace and Write: Students trace sentences: 'There is a kitchen.' 'There is a bedroom.' Then copy them. Draw a picture next to each sentence.
lp.st: Sing 'The House Song' with actions. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students have bingo cards with room pictures. Teacher calls out a room, students cover it.
Hide a teddy in a room. Students ask: 'Where is Teddy?' Teacher answers: 'He is in the kitchen.'
Students match room pictures and words. Say: 'Kitchen, kitchen.'
Students put house puzzle together. Say: 'This is the bedroom.'
Teacher acts cooking, students guess: 'It is the kitchen!'
diff: Fast finishers: Draw an extra room (e.g. garden) and write: 'There is a garden.'
Support: Use word bank with room names to copy from.
hw: Find 5 house pictures in magazines, cut them out, stick on paper, label: 'kitchen', 'bedroom' etc.
Draw your house, write 3 sentences: 'There is a kitchen.' 'There is a bedroom.'
Ask family: 'Where is Daddy?' Write: 'He is in the living room.'
lp.tip: Use TPR to reinforce prepositions (in, on) with room objects, e.g. 'Put the spoon in the kitchen.'

weeks.obj: Say where things are in a room; describe where things are using in, on, under
weeks.lang: table, chair, bed, box; in, on, under + in/on/under/behind/next to + furniture
weeks.act: Guessing game: teams ask questions about furniture
weeks.hw: play the matching game in the furniture library folder with a family member

skills.L: Listen and place objects in, on, under or behind
skills.S: Say where things are in the room picture
skills.R: Read preposition sentences and match to pictures
skills.W: Write The cat is ___ sentences

lp.wu: Simon Says with furniture: teacher says 'Simon says touch the table', students touch flashcards or point to real classroom furniture; they repeat 'It is a table' and 'I touch the table'
wuAlt: Flashcard drill: show furniture flashcards, students say 'It is a ___' and make a sentence 'The table is big'
TPR game: teacher mimes sitting, students say 'Sit on the chair' and mime
lp.pres: Use a felt board with a bedroom scene; place a small box on the bed, under the chair, and next to the table; model 'The box is on the bed', 'The box is under the chair', 'The box is next to the table'; ask students 'Where is the box?' to check understanding
presAlt: Storytime: read 'Where is my cat?' with a cat hiding in/on/under furniture; pause to ask 'Where is the cat?'
Realia hunt: hide a small toy in/on/under classroom furniture; students find it and say 'It is in the box'
lp.prac: Preposition pairs: students get furniture flashcards and preposition cards; they make sentences like 'The book is on the table' in pairs; teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation
pracAlt: Furniture bingo: call out 'in the box', students cover the picture of a box in a box; first to shout 'Bingo!' wins
Draw and describe: students draw a room and label furniture, then tell partner 'The bed is under the window'
lp.ls: Listen and draw: teacher describes a room ('The ball is on the table. The cat is under the bed'), students draw; check drawings against teacher's picture
lp.re: Furniture relay: teams race to place flashcards in/on/under a drawn room on the board; first team to place all correctly wins
lp.prod: Find and tell: students search the classroom for small objects (pen, eraser), place them in/on/under furniture, and tell the class 'The pen is on the chair'
lp.rw: Trace and copy: students trace pre-written sentences like 'The cat is in the box', then copy them independently; draw a picture to match
lp.st: Read 'Brown Bear, Brown Bear' with furniture substitutions ('I see a table looking at me'); sing 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' with 'table, chair, bed, box'; goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line
g: Draw a grid with 'in', 'on', 'under'; students toss a beanbag and say a sentence with the preposition
Student mimes sitting on a chair; others guess 'Are you on the chair?'
Teacher hides a toy; students ask 'Is it in the box?' until found
Match picture cards (e.g., cat under bed) with sentence cards
Student draws a table; others guess 'Is it a table?'
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: write 3 sentences about their own room using the prepositions
Support / weaker learners: use word banks with furniture and preposition words to copy
hw: Play the matching game in the furniture library folder with a family member
Draw your bedroom and label 3 pieces of furniture with 'in', 'on', 'under'
Ask your family 'Where is the remote?' and answer in English
lp.tip: Use Moroccan home contexts (e.g., 'Where is the teapot?') to make the theme relatable; praise effort over accuracy to build confidence.

weeks.obj: Describe my morning routine in order; sequence 5 morning actions with English words
weeks.lang: wake up, wash, brush my teeth, eat, go to school + first, then, next; get up, wash, eat
weeks.res: Flashcards/Daily Routine; Music/Songs (brush my teeth); Tests/General
weeks.act: Cut-and-stick poster with morning routines labels
weeks.hw: read your morning routines mini-book to someone at home

skills.L: Listen to a morning routine and order the events
skills.S: Describe my morning with first, then, next
skills.R: Read routine sentences and order the cards
skills.W: Write my morning routine in 3 steps

lp.wu: Students play 'Simon Says' with morning actions: 'Simon says wake up!', 'Simon says brush your teeth!', 'Simon says wash your face!', 'Simon says eat breakfast!', 'Simon says go to school!'. They perform the actions and shout the verbs.
wuAlt: Students do a 'Morning Routine Relay' in teams: run to the board, point to a flashcard of 'wake up', run back, high-five next student who points to 'wash', etc.
Students play 'What's Missing?': I show 5 flashcards (wake up, wash, brush teeth, eat, go to school), they close eyes, I remove one, they guess 'What is missing? It is __.'
lp.pres: I show a big poster of a boy's morning routine with 5 pictures in random order. I model: 'First, I wake up. Then, I wash my face. Next, I brush my teeth. Then, I eat breakfast. Finally, I go to school.' I ask 'What is first?' and students point to the picture. I check understanding with 'What do I do after wake up?'
presAlt: I use a storybook 'My Busy Morning' with repeating sentences: 'I wake up. I wash. I eat. I go to school.' I pause and ask 'What is next?'
I act out the routine with props: a pillow (wake up), a towel (wash), a toothbrush (brush teeth), a banana (eat), a bag (go to school). Students say the verbs as I act.
lp.prac: Students work in pairs with a cut-and-stick worksheet of 5 morning actions. They cut out the pictures and glue them in order on a timeline strip. They practice saying: 'First, I __. Then, I __. Next, I __.' I help with pronunciation and sentence structure.
pracAlt: Students play 'Routine Order Race' in teams: I give each group a set of 5 picture cards. They race to put them in order and say the sequence correctly.
Students play 'Teacher Says': I say a sequence like 'First, wake up. Then, wash.' and students mime it in order.
lp.ls: Students listen to an audio of a girl describing her morning routine. They have 5 picture cards and put them in the order they hear. I play the audio twice: 'I wake up at 7. Then, I wash my face. Next, I brush my teeth. Then, I eat bread. Finally, I go to school.'
lp.re: Students play 'Morning Routine Freeze Dance': I play music, they dance/mime morning actions. When I pause, they freeze and I ask 'What are you doing?' They answer 'I am __.' (e.g., 'I am brushing my teeth.')
lp.prod: Students draw their own morning routine in 3 steps on a paper strip. They present to a partner: 'First, I __. Then, I __. Next, I __.' I encourage them to use the sequence words and add details like 'I eat bread' or 'I drink milk'.
lp.rw: Students trace 3 simple sentences: 'I wake up. I wash. I eat.' Then they copy the sentences under the pictures. For fast finishers, they write their own 3-step routine: 'First, __. Then, __. Next, __.'
lp.st: We sing the 'Good Morning Song' with actions: 'Good morning, good morning, wake up! Good morning, good morning, wash your face! Good morning, good morning, eat your bread! Good morning, good morning, go to school!' Then we do the goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students have bingo cards with morning actions. I call out 'Wake up!' and they cover the picture. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Teams race to put 5 picture cards in order on the board and say the sequence correctly.
I show 3 picture cards in order. Students close eyes, I swap two, they guess what changed.
Students mime a morning action, others guess 'Are you __?' (e.g., 'Are you brushing your teeth?')
Students sit in a circle. Student 1 says 'First, I wake up.' Student 2 says 'First, I wake up. Then, I wash.' and so on.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: They write a 4-step morning routine and draw a picture for each step.
Support / weaker learners: They use a sentence frame with picture cues: 'First, I __. Then, I __. Next, I __.'
hw: Read your morning routines mini-book to someone at home. Point to the pictures and say the sentences.
Draw your family's morning routine and label 3 actions in English.
Play 'Teacher Says' with your family using morning actions.
lp.tip: Use the local context: ask students what they eat for breakfast (e.g., 'Do you eat bread and milk?') to make the routine personal and relevant to Moroccan culture.

weeks.obj: Play review games for all semester 2 topics; show confidence across the year's topics in station games
weeks.lang: all year outcomes + semester 2 review
weeks.act:
Mixed-skills revision circuit in teams
Recycle-sort game in English; plant-a-seed craft with "First... then..." instructions.
weeks.hw:
revise your notes for the assessment week
Find 3 things at home to recycle and name them in English.

skills.L: Listening stations across S2 topics
skills.S: Speaking carousel - games with Q and A turns
skills.R: Reading-and-matching station races
skills.W: Short writing station: sentence completions

lp.wu: Warm-up: Recycle Relay! Teams race to sort picture cards into bins labeled 'Paper', 'Plastic', 'Glass'. Students shout 'This is paper!' or 'This is plastic!' as they sort.
wuAlt: Alternative warm-up 1: Earth Day Pictionary—draw a recycling symbol, a tree, or a litter bin for teammates to guess in English.
Alternative warm-up 2: 'I Spy with my little eye something you can recycle'—students guess objects in the classroom.
lp.pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of recyclable items (bottle, can, newspaper) and trash (banana peel, plastic bag). Model 'What is it? It is a bottle.' and 'Can you recycle it? Yes, I can.' Check understanding with thumbs up/down.
presAlt: Alternative presentation 1: Use a story about a child cleaning up a park—point to items and ask 'Recycle or trash?'
Alternative presentation 2: Demonstrate with realia—hold up a bottle and ask 'Can you recycle this?' students answer.
lp.prac: Guided practice: Pair work—students take turns asking 'What is it?' and 'Can you recycle it?' using flashcards. Monitor and correct pronunciation, especially 'can' and 'recycle'.
pracAlt: Alternative practice 1: 'Recycle Sort' game—teams race to sort word cards into correct bins, shouting the category.
Alternative practice 2: 'First, then...' drill—'First, I find a bottle. Then, I put it in the bin.'
lp.ls: Listening slot: Play a recording of a teacher saying 'I can recycle a can. I cannot recycle a banana peel.' Students hold up the correct picture card. Checks if they distinguish recyclable from non-recyclable.
lp.re: Reactivation game: 'Litter Tag'—one student is 'litter' (holds a trash card), others chase them to tag and say 'Put it in the bin!' to make them 'recycle'.
lp.prod: Production task: Plant-a-seed craft—students follow 'First, put soil in the pot. Then, put a seed in.' in pairs. They take turns giving instructions, using target language.
lp.rw: Reading and writing slot: Trace and copy sentences like 'I can recycle a bottle.' and 'This is paper.' Then complete sentence starters like 'I can recycle ____.' with words from a word bank.
lp.st: Story/Song + goodbye: Read 'The Earth Day Helpers' story with repetitive phrases. End with 'Goodbye Song' (tune of 'Twinkle Twinkle')—'Goodbye friends, goodbye friends, see you next time, goodbye!' followed by sticker chart and high-five line.
g: Teams race to sort picture cards into bins labeled 'Paper', 'Plastic', 'Glass'.
Draw a recycling symbol, tree, or litter bin for teammates to guess in English.
Students take turns giving instructions like 'First, find a bottle. Then, recycle it.'
One student is 'litter', others tag them and say 'Put it in the bin!'
Follow 'First, put soil in the pot. Then, put a seed in.' in pairs.
diff: Fast finishers: Draw 3 more things to recycle and write sentences.
Support: Trace the sentences with dotted lines and match to pictures.
hw: Homework 1: Find 3 things at home to recycle and name them in English.
Homework 2: Draw a picture of you recycling and write one sentence about it.
Homework 3: Teach a family member how to sort recycling in English.
lp.tip: Use Moroccan context—relate recycling to local cleanliness drives or the Green March spirit of community action. Celebrate with stickers for effort, not just accuracy.

weeks.obj: Show everything I can do in the final quiz; complete game-based final assessment; celebrate the year
weeks.lang: all year outcomes + full-year review
weeks.act:
Mixed-skills revision circuit in teams
Jobs guessing game (What does a ... do?); thank-you cards for workers we know.
weeks.hw:
revise your notes for the assessment week
