Draw one job you love and write 3 sentences about it.

skills.L: Listen-and-circle final quiz (Tests)
skills.S: Picture-chat assessment in pairs
skills.R: Read-and-match final sheet
skills.W: Guided short writing: all about me (3 sentences)

lp.wu: Review Relay Race: Teams race to write 10 jobs on the board. Teacher shouts 'Teacher! Doctor! Farmer!' and students run to write them. Winners get 2 points, others 1.
wuAlt: Job Charades: Students act out jobs like 'bake bread' or 'drive a bus' while others guess.
Flashcard Speed: Show job flashcards fast; teams shout the job name.
lp.pres: Teacher shows realia (doctor's coat, chef's hat) and asks 'What is it? It is a __.' Then models 'What does a doctor do? They help people.' Students repeat in pairs with flashcards.
presAlt: Job Poster: Point to a poster of jobs and ask 'What does a farmer do? They grow food.' Students answer in full sentences.
Storytime: Read 'Jobs Around Us' story, stopping to ask 'What does the baker do?'
lp.prac: Jobs Guessing Game: Team A thinks of a job, Team B asks 'Does it wear a hat? Do they work outside?' until they guess. Teacher monitors for full sentences like 'Yes, they do.'
pracAlt: Job Match-Up: Students match picture cards to job description cards ('They teach students.') in pairs.
TPR Job Actions: Teacher says 'Be a farmer!' and students pretend to plant seeds; 'Be a doctor!' and they pretend to check a patient.
lp.ls: Listen and Circle: Students listen to audio of 5 jobs (e.g., 'A firefighter puts out fires.') and circle the correct picture on their worksheet. Teacher checks answers together.
lp.re: Job Action Freeze: Play music; students dance to a job action (e.g., 'sweep like a cleaner'). When music stops, they freeze. Last one out sits down.
lp.prod: Thank-You Cards: Students draw a worker they know (e.g., 'My father is a mechanic.') and write 'Thank you for working hard!' with crayons. They share with the class.
lp.rw: Read and Match: Students read 3 simple sentences ('A teacher works at school.') and match them to the correct job picture. Then they trace 3 sentences about their dream job.
lp.st: Read 'The Little Worker' story about a child helping at home. Sing 'What Do You Do?' song with actions. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teams take turns running to write a job on the board; no duplicates allowed.
Teacher describes a job ('I wear a uniform and drive a bus.'); students guess.
Students draw a job for their team to guess.
Students act out jobs while others guess the name.
Students mark off jobs called by the teacher.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 sentences about what jobs they want to do when they grow up.
Support: Trace the job names and match to pictures with sentence starters.
hw: Draw one job you love and write 3 sentences about it (e.g., 'I love teachers. They help students. They are smart.')
Ask your family about their jobs and write them down.
Play the Jobs Guessing Game with your family.
lp.tip: Use Moroccan context: highlight local jobs like 'artisan' or 'fisherman' to connect Labour Day to students' lives. Praise effort, not just correctness, during assessment.
checklist: I can name 10 jobs in English
I can ask 'What does a ___ do?'
I can answer 'They ___.'
I can listen and circle the correct job
I can read and match jobs to sentences
I can write 3 sentences about a job
I can say thank you to workers

levels.desc: For children aged 8–10 who can already greet and name the basics. The year revisits the Beginners themes at A1 depth — full sentences, short dialogues, first simple reading of three-word sentences — and adds new topics (daily routine, weather, house, furniture) with pair work and Cambridge YLE Starters/Movers task types.

levels.label: Kids · Advanced

weeks.obj: Run a classroom routine and greet guests in English; say hello and goodbye and give their name; follow 3 basic class instructions
weeks.lang: Hello. My name is... Goodbye!; stand up, sit down, look, listen + review be + questions; classroom language upgrade
weeks.res: Music/Songs (hello song); Flashcards/Class rules; Worksheets/Print outs
weeks.act: Mini-project: make a poster about classroom routines and present it
weeks.hw: prepare 2 facts about classroom routines to tell the class

skills.L: Listen to classroom-role audio and spot the routines; be-question quiz
skills.S: Run a classroom routine and greet guests in English
skills.R: Read class-rule texts and match to situations
skills.W: Write our class rules (3 rules) on the poster

lp.wu: Stand Up Sit Down Game: Teacher calls out 'stand up' or 'sit down', children jump up or down quickly. Teacher speeds up to make it fun. Children shout 'Yes!' when they do it right.
wuAlt: Simon Says: Teacher says 'Simon says stand up', children obey; if no 'Simon says', they freeze. Children laugh when tricked.
Hello Circle: Children stand in a circle, pass a ball, say 'Hello, my name is [name]' when they get the ball.
lp.pres: Use flashcards showing 'stand up', 'sit down', 'look', 'listen'. Teacher models each action with clear commands: 'Stand up! Now sit down.' Children repeat the words and actions. Teacher asks 'What do I do?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Puppet Show: A puppet gives wrong commands (e.g., 'Sit down!' while standing), children correct it by saying the right action. Puppet says 'Oh, sorry!'.
Realia Demo: Teacher uses a doll to show 'look' at the doll, 'listen' to a bell, children copy and say the words.
lp.prac: Command Relay: Teams line up, teacher whispers a command to the first child, they run to the board, draw it, next child says the command. Teacher helps with spelling if needed. Teams cheer when they get it right.
pracAlt: Classroom Routine Bingo: Children have bingo cards with pictures of actions (stand, sit, look, listen). Teacher calls out commands, children mark the picture. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Action Charades: One child mimes an action, others guess and say the command. Mimes 'stand up' if correct.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw Audio: Play a short audio of a teacher giving 3 commands (e.g., 'Stand up. Look at the board. Sit down.'). Children draw the actions in order. Teacher checks drawings to see if they followed correctly.
lp.re: Freeze Dance: Play music, children dance; when music stops, teacher shouts a command (e.g., 'sit down'), children freeze in that position. Laugh if someone moves too soon.
lp.prod: Classroom Rules Poster: Groups of 3 draw 3 rules (e.g., 'Stand up when the teacher comes in', 'Listen when the teacher speaks') on a poster. Each group presents their poster, saying the rules clearly.
lp.rw: Read and Match: Children read short sentences ('When the teacher claps, sit down.') and match them to picture cards of classroom situations. Teacher helps with unknown words.
lp.st: Goodbye Song: Sing 'Goodbye, goodbye, see you next time!' with waving motions. Children line up for a high-five and get a sticker for the sticker chart. Teacher says 'Goodbye, [name]!' to each child.
g: Teacher says 'Simon says [action]', children obey; if no 'Simon says', they freeze.
Teams race to draw or act out commands first.
Dance until music stops, then freeze when a command is called.
Mark pictures of actions as commands are called.
Mime actions for others to guess the command.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 4th rule for the poster with a drawing.
Support: Trace the words 'stand up', 'sit down' on the poster.
hw: Draw a picture of your favorite classroom routine and write 1 sentence about it.
Ask your family 3 classroom rules in English and tell the class next week.
Make a list of 3 greetings (hello, goodbye) and practice saying them in a mirror.
lp.tip: Use the American Space Oujda poster to model greetings; connect to local culture by saying 'Salam alaikum' as a hello, then teach 'Hello' as the English version.

weeks.obj: Say how I feel and why with because; ask How are you? and answer with 4 feeling words
weeks.lang: happy, sad, angry, tired; How are you? I am... + feelings + because; Why...? Because...
weeks.res: Flashcards (emotions set); Games/Game ideas; Worksheets/Print outs
weeks.act: Roleplay with props: a situation about how are you? Feelings, in pairs
weeks.hw: read the how are you? Feelings page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words

skills.L: Listen to why-sentences and match feelings to reasons
skills.S: Say how I feel and why with because
skills.R: Read feeling + reason sentences and match the halves
skills.W: Write I am ___ because ___ sentences

lp.wu: Feelings Charades: Students pick a feeling flashcard, act it out without speaking, and classmates guess 'Are you happy/sad/angry/tired?'
wuAlt: Feelings Bingo: Teacher calls out feelings, students mark them on bingo cards; first to shout 'Bingo!' wins
Feelings Chain: One student says 'I am happy', next says 'He is happy, I am sad', continuing the chain
lp.pres: Teacher shows a story about a boy named Ahmed who feels tired because he played football, sad because his friend left, happy because he ate cake, and angry because his brother broke his toy. Model sentences: 'How are you?' 'I am tired because I played football.' Check understanding with thumbs up/down for each feeling-reason pair.
presAlt: Realia Feelings: Teacher holds up objects (ball, toy, cake, photo) and says 'I am happy because I have a cake', students repeat
Puppet Show: Two puppets ask 'How are you?' and answer with feelings + because, students echo
lp.prac: Feelings Dominoes: Students get dominoes with feelings on one half and reasons on the other; they match them and say the full sentence 'I am [feeling] because [reason]'. Teacher circulates to correct pronunciation.
pracAlt: Feelings Memory Game: Cards with feelings and reasons face down; students flip two, match, and say the sentence; if no match, turn back
Feelings Dice: Roll a feelings die and a reason die, then make a sentence
lp.ls: Listen and Match: Teacher reads sentences like 'I am angry because my book is lost' and students point to the matching picture on their worksheet with 4 feelings and 4 reasons.
lp.re: Feelings Relay: Students line up; teacher calls a feeling, first student runs to the board, writes it, runs back, next student writes a reason; team with fastest correct pair wins.
lp.prod: Feelings Doctor Roleplay: In pairs, one is a doctor, one is a patient. Doctor asks 'How are you?', patient answers with feeling + because, then asks 'Why?', doctor guesses. Props: toy stethoscope, bandages.
lp.rw: Read and Complete: Students read a short paragraph like 'Lila is happy because it is Eid. She is not sad.' Then write 2 sentences: 'I am ___ because ___' and 'I am not ___ because ___'.
lp.st: Story: 'The Feelings Monster' where a monster changes feelings; students act out the feelings. End with 'Goodbye Song' (to the tune of 'Twinkle Twinkle') and high-five line.
g: Students act out feelings, classmates guess
Match feeling cards to reason cards and say sentences
Race to write feeling-reason pairs on the board
Ask and answer about feelings with props
Mark called-out feelings on bingo cards
diff: Fast finishers: Draw a picture of themselves with a feeling and write 3 sentences
Support learners: Use sentence frames 'I am ___ because ___' with word banks
hw: Read the 'How are you?' page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words
Draw 4 faces (happy, sad, angry, tired) and write a sentence for each
Ask 3 family members 'How are you?' and write their answers
lp.tip: Use local context like Eid or Independence Day to make feelings relevant—e.g., 'I am happy because it is Eid'.

weeks.obj: Describe and compare two colour pictures; recognize and say 5 colors and answer What color is it?
weeks.lang: red, blue, yellow, green, black; What color is it? It is... + adjective order: a big red ball; looks + adjective
weeks.res: Flashcards/Shapes-Colours; Music/Songs (Colors Action Song); Worksheets/Print outs
weeks.act: Quiz show in teams about colors
weeks.hw: draw a comic strip about colors with speech bubbles

skills.L: Listen to colour descriptions and spot the adjective order
skills.S: Describe and compare two colour pictures
skills.R: Read picture descriptions and find the right one
skills.W: Write a 2-sentence colour description with adjectives

lp.wu: Color Relay: Students line up in two teams. Teacher holds up a flashcard (e.g., red), and the first student runs to the board, draws a red object, and says 'It is a big red ball'. The team with the correct drawing and sentence gets a point.
wuAlt: Color Bingo: Students have bingo cards with color words. Teacher calls out 'Find something blue in the classroom', and students mark the word if they see blue.
Color Chain: One student says 'I see something red', the next says 'I see something red and blue', and so on, building the chain.
lp.pres: Teacher uses a story about a Moroccan market (souk) with colorful items. Flashcards show a 'big yellow lemon', 'small green mint', and 'long red pepper'. Model sentences: 'What color is it? It is a big yellow lemon'. Check understanding by asking 'What color is the mint?'
presAlt: Realia Show: Teacher brings real fruits (lemon, apple, banana) and asks 'What color is it?' Students answer 'It is a yellow banana'.
Color Song: Sing 'I See Something Blue' with gestures, then pause and ask 'What color is the pen?'
lp.prac: Team Quiz Show: Two teams compete to describe pictures. For example, Team A gets a picture of a 'small black cat' and must say 'It is a small black cat'. Teacher gives sentence starters: 'It is a...'.
pracAlt: Picture Match: Students get two sets of cards—color words and adjective+color phrases (e.g., 'big red'). They match them.
Describe and Compare: In pairs, Student A describes a picture (e.g., 'It is a big blue car'), Student B finds the matching picture from two options.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes a picture: 'It is a big green ball and a small yellow ball'. Students draw and compare. Checks if they can spot adjective order.
lp.re: Color Jump: Students stand in a circle. Teacher calls out 'Jump to red!', and students jump to the red flashcard. After the break, this reactivates movement and color words.
lp.prod: Comic Strip Project: In groups, students draw a 2-frame comic strip with two colorful objects (e.g., a big red kite and a small blue kite). They add speech bubbles: 'What color is it?' and 'It is a big red kite'.
lp.rw: Read and Match: Students read short sentences like 'It is a long green snake' and match them to the correct picture. Then they write their own 2-sentence description: 'It is a big yellow sun. It is hot.'
lp.st: Story: 'The Rainbow Over the Atlas Mountains' (a short story about colors in nature). End with the goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students run to board to draw/color objects when teacher calls a color
Teams describe pictures to earn points
Match color words to adjective+color phrases
Teacher describes, students draw to check listening
Groups draw and write speech bubbles about colors
diff: Fast finishers: Add more details to their comic strip (e.g., 'It is a big, shiny red kite').
Support: Use word banks with color words and adjectives (big, small, long, short).
hw: Draw a comic strip with 2 frames about colors and add speech bubbles (e.g., 'What color is the flag? It is red and green').
Write 3 sentences about colors in your room (e.g., 'My bed is blue. My pillow is white.')
Find 5 colorful objects at home and write their colors (e.g., 'The door is brown. The carpet is red.')
lp.tip: Use local context like the Moroccan flag (red and green) to make colors relevant. For the American Space, connect to US holidays like Independence Day (red, white, blue) to build cultural bridges.

weeks.obj: Do simple maths in English up to 100; count 1-10 forwards and catch-count in a circle
weeks.lang: numbers 1-10; How many? + numbers to 100; plus, minus, equals
weeks.act:
Story chain: add a sentence about numbers 1-10 in turns
Craft: paper pumpkins while saying "This is my pumpkin. It is big/scary!"; costume word game.
weeks.hw:
interview a family member about numbers 1-10 and note 2 answers
Draw your costume and label it in English.

skills.L: Listen to maths problems in English and solve them
skills.S: Do plus/minus maths aloud in pair races
skills.R: Read number words to 100 and write the numerals
skills.W: Write number problems for a partner to solve

lp.wu: Count and Catch: Students stand in a circle and throw a soft pumpkin. They count from 1 to 10 in order, each student saying one number. If a student drops the pumpkin or says the wrong number, they sit down. The last student standing wins.
wuAlt: Number Bingo: Teacher calls out numbers 1-10 in English, students cover the corresponding number on their bingo card. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Halloween Count: Teacher shows flashcards of Halloween items (e.g., 3 bats, 5 ghosts), students shout the number in English.
lp.pres: Teacher uses a big storybook about a pumpkin patch. Pointing to pumpkins, models 'This is my pumpkin. It is big/scary!' and 'How many pumpkins?' Students repeat chorally. Teacher writes numbers 1-10 on the board and says 'plus, minus, equals' with simple sums (e.g., 2 + 1 = 3). Students hold up fingers to show answers.
presAlt: Number Hopscotch: Draw a hopscotch grid with numbers 1-10. Students jump and say the number they land on. Teacher calls out 'Jump to 5!' or 'Jump to 8!'.
Pumpkin Craft Demo: Teacher shows a paper pumpkin craft, saying 'I need 1 orange paper. I need 2 eyes. I need 1 mouth.' Students repeat the sentences.
lp.prac: Pair Race: Students work in pairs. Each pair gets a set of number cards 1-10. Teacher calls out a sum (e.g., '3 plus 2!'). The first pair to find the answer card (5) and hold it up wins a point. Teacher models 'Three plus two equals five!'
pracAlt: Pumpkin Counting Game: Students get a bowl of plastic spiders. Teacher says 'Put 4 spiders on your pumpkin!' Students do it and say 'Four spiders!'.
Number Chain Story: Students sit in a circle. Each student adds one sentence to a story using a number, e.g., 'I see 1 bat. I see 2 cats...'. Teacher starts the story.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher reads a short Halloween story with numbers, e.g., 'There are 3 pumpkins. 2 pumpkins are big. 1 pumpkin is small.' Students draw the pumpkins as they listen. Teacher checks drawings for correct numbers and sizes.
lp.re: Zombie Tag: One student is 'it' (zombie) and chases others. When tagged, students freeze and say a number 1-10. Another student can 'unfreeze' them by saying the next number. Game continues until all are frozen.
lp.prod: Pumpkin Costume Project: Students design their own Halloween costume on paper. They label parts in English, e.g., 'This is my mask. It is scary. I have a cape.' They present their costume to the class, saying 'This is my costume. It is [adjective]. I have [item].'
lp.rw: Number Problem Writing: Students write 2 simple maths problems for a partner, e.g., '5 plus 3 equals?' and '10 minus 4 equals?'. They swap papers and solve the problems, writing the answers numerals.
lp.st: Teacher reads a short Halloween counting story, e.g., 'Ten Little Pumpkins'. Students count along with the story. End with the 'Goodbye Song' and a sticker chart. Students line up for high-fives as they leave.
g: Teacher calls out numbers 1-10. Students cover the number on their bingo card. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Students take turns rolling a dice and putting that many plastic spiders on their paper pumpkin. First to 10 spiders wins.
Teacher writes a sum on the board. Students race to write the answer on their mini-whiteboard. First correct wins.
Teacher shows a flashcard of a costume (e.g., 'witch'). Students say 'This is a witch. It is scary.'
Students throw a ball and count how many times they catch it without dropping it.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 more maths problems for a friend.
Support learners: Use number lines or fingers to solve sums.
hw: Interview a family member: 'What is your favourite number? Why?' Write 2 answers.
Draw your dream Halloween costume and label 3 parts in English.
Count 10 things in your house and write them in a list, e.g., '1 table, 2 chairs...'.
lp.tip: Use Moroccan cultural references, like comparing Halloween to local festivals, to make the theme relatable. For example, 'Halloween is like a fun party where we dress up, just like during the Green March!'

weeks.obj: Run a colours-and-numbers quiz show in teams; combine colors and numbers in color-by-number work
weeks.lang: review: colors + 1-10; How many (red) balloons? + Which one? The ... one; review colours + numbers
weeks.res: Worksheets/Print outs; Games/Printable games; Worksheets/Print outs
weeks.act:
Survey and simple bar graph about colors and numbers
Map craft: colour the march route and say "the march goes to..."; flag colours chant.
weeks.hw:
find a colors and numbers worksheet in the library folder and bring it done
Draw the Moroccan flag and write its colours in English.

skills.L: Listen to quiz questions and buzz in with the answers
skills.S: Run a colours-and-numbers quiz show in teams
skills.R: Read quiz questions and check the rules sheet
skills.W: Write 2 quiz questions with answer keys

lp.wu: Balloon Pop Review: Teacher holds 10 numbered balloons in different colors. Students take turns popping a balloon, saying its color and number (e.g., 'Blue, number 5!').
wuAlt: Color Hunt: Teacher calls out a color and number (e.g., '3 red balloons!'), students find matching flashcards and bring them to the front.
Number Jump: Students jump the number of times the teacher says, wearing a color hat (e.g., 'Jump 5 times if you have blue!').
lp.pres: Teacher shows a map of Morocco with the Green March route. Models: 'The march goes to... (city name). It's (color). Students repeat. Teacher holds up numbered flashcards and asks 'How many (red) flags?' Students answer 'Five red flags!'
presAlt: Flag Flashcards: Teacher shows Moroccan flag colors, says 'This is red and green.' Students repeat and point to colors on their mini-flags.
March Story: Teacher tells a short story about the Green March using a picture book, pointing to colors and numbers in the illustrations.
lp.prac: Team Quiz Show: Two teams compete. Teacher asks 'How many (blue) balloons? Which one? The (big) one?' Teams buzz in, answer, and get points. Teacher supports with flashcards and gestures.
pracAlt: Color-by-Number: Students color a map of the Green March route using a worksheet with numbers (1=red, 2=green, etc.), saying 'The march goes to... (city name). It's (color).'
Survey: Students ask classmates 'What's your favorite color? How many?' and tally answers on a simple bar graph.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes a scene: 'There are 3 green flags and 2 red balloons. Draw them!' Students listen and draw, then check with a partner.
lp.re: Color Relay: After break, students line up. Teacher calls 'Run to the (blue) circle!' Students race to touch the correct color, saying 'Blue! Number 4!'
lp.prod: Map Craft: Students color a large map of the Green March route. In groups, they present: 'The march goes to... (city name). It's (color). We see (number) flags!'
lp.rw: Flag Writing: Students draw the Moroccan flag and write: 'The flag is red and green. There is a star.' Teacher helps with spelling and sentence structure.
lp.st: Goodbye Song: 'Goodbye, Goodbye' with color and number actions (e.g., wave 3 times for 'green'). Sticker chart for participation, high-five line.
g: Teams buzz in to answer 'How many (color)? Which one?' questions for points.
Students color a map using number codes, saying 'The march goes to... (city name).'
Students ask 'What's your favorite color? How many?' and make a bar graph.
Students race to touch the correct color when called, saying 'Color! Number!'
Groups present their colored map, saying 'The march goes to... (city name). It's (color).'
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 quiz questions for a friend to answer.
Support: Use color/number word bank for writing and speaking tasks.
hw: Draw the Moroccan flag and write its colors in English.
Find a colors and numbers worksheet in the library folder and bring it done.
Ask your family 'What's your favorite color? How many?' and tell the class next week.
lp.tip: Use the Green March theme to connect language learning to local history, making vocabulary memorable through cultural context.

weeks.obj: Describe classroom objects and set class rules; name 6 classroom objects and ask for them politely
weeks.lang: pen, pencil, book, bag, chair, table; Can I have..., please? + there is/are + this/that; must / mustn't
weeks.act: Show-and-tell plus 2 questions from the class
weeks.hw: write 4 sentences about classroom objects using and/but

skills.L: Listen to There is/There are descriptions of classrooms
skills.S: Describe our classroom and agree class rules together
skills.R: Read classroom descriptions and find the differences
skills.W: Write There is / There are classroom sentences

lp.wu: Flashcard Race: Divide class into 2 teams. Hold up flashcards of classroom objects (pen, pencil, book, bag, chair, table). First team to shout the correct word in English gets a point. Teacher says 'What is this?' and children respond 'It's a pen!'
wuAlt: Object Hunt: Hide small classroom objects around the room. Children find one, bring it to the front, and say 'I found a pencil!'
Simon Says: Play Simon Says with classroom actions, e.g., 'Simon says touch a chair!'
lp.pres: Use a big poster of a classroom. Point to objects and model 'This is a pen. That is a table.' Then ask 'What is this?' to elicit responses. Introduce 'Can I have a pen, please?' with a puppet. Check understanding by asking 'What do you say to ask nicely?'
presAlt: Realia Bag: Put objects in a bag. Children guess by asking 'Is it a book?' Teacher responds 'Yes, it is!' or 'No, it isn't!'
Story Time: Read a short story about a messy classroom, e.g., 'There is a pen on the table. There are books on the chair.'
lp.prac: Classroom Bingo: Give each child a bingo grid with 6 classroom objects. Teacher calls out 'Can I have a pencil, please?' Children cover the matching picture. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins. Support by pointing to the flashcard when calling.
pracAlt: Pair Dialogue: Children practice 'Can I have a pen, please?' and 'Here you are.' with a partner. Teacher models first with a strong student.
Classroom Rules Poster: In groups, children draw a classroom object and write a rule, e.g., 'We must put books on the table.'
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes a classroom, e.g., 'There is a blue chair. There are two pencils on the table.' Children draw what they hear. Check by comparing drawings.
lp.re: Stand Up, Sit Down: Teacher holds up an object. If it's a 'must' object (e.g., book), children stand up. If it's a 'mustn't' object (e.g., pen on the floor), they sit down. Teacher says 'We must use books!' and 'We mustn't throw pens!'
lp.prod: Show-and-Tell Project: Each child brings 1 classroom object to the front. They say 'This is my bag. I must put it on the chair.' The class asks 2 questions, e.g., 'What color is it?' and 'Where do you put it?'
lp.rw: Find the Differences: In pairs, children get two similar classroom pictures with 3 differences. They take turns saying 'There is a pen on the table in picture 1, but there isn't in picture 2.' Then they write 2 sentences about their own classroom.
lp.st: Story: Read 'The Messy Desk' story about a child who must organize their things. End with the Goodbye Song: 'Goodbye, goodbye, see you next time! High-five, high-five, have a nice day!' Children line up for high-fives and get stickers.
g: Teams race to bring a classroom object to the teacher and say 'Can I have a pen, please?'
Children sit in a circle. Each child adds an object, e.g., 'I have a pen and a pencil.'
Children act out a classroom rule (e.g., 'mustn't run') for others to guess.
Teacher calls out objects, children cover them on their bingo cards.
Teacher removes an object from a table, children guess 'The pen is missing!
diff: Fast finishers: Write a short dialogue between two students asking for classroom objects.
Support learners: Use sentence starters like 'This is a ____.' and 'Can I have a ____, please?'
hw: Draw your classroom and write 4 sentences using 'and' and 'but', e.g., 'There is a blue book and a red pen. There isn't a chair, but there is a table.'
Make a poster of 3 classroom rules using 'must' and 'mustn't'.
Ask your family for 3 classroom objects in English using 'Can I have...?'
lp.tip: Use the American Space Oujda context by comparing classroom objects in Morocco vs. America (e.g., 'In America, students use laptops. In Morocco, we use books.').

weeks.obj: Retell a short Halloween story in the past; follow a simple Halloween story and say 4 themed words
weeks.lang: pumpkin, witch, ghost, candy; simple story frames + past simple (was/went/saw); story words first, then
weeks.act:
Write and perform a 4-line rhyme about Halloween
Flag craft + "I am from Morocco" chant; national symbols matching game.
weeks.hw:
prepare 2 facts about Halloween to tell the class
Teach someone at home the independence chant.

skills.L: Listen to a Halloween story told in the past
skills.S: Retell the story with was / went / saw
skills.R: Read the story text and order the events
skills.W: Write 3 past sentences about the story

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'Pass the Pumpkin' - children sit in a circle, pass a toy pumpkin while chanting 'Trick or treat?', stop the music, child holding pumpkin says 'I see a [color pumpkin]'.
wuAlt: Alternative warm-up 1: 'Halloween Charades' - children act out pumpkin, witch, ghost, candy for others to guess.
Alternative warm-up 2: 'Count the Candies' - show flashcards of candy, children count 'One candy, two candies...'.
lp.pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of pumpkin, witch, ghost, candy; model and drill pronunciation. Present a short story about a witch using 'The witch was happy. She went to the house. She saw a ghost.'; check understanding with 'Who was happy? Where did she go?'
presAlt: Alternative presentation 1: Use a picture book with Halloween images to introduce vocabulary and story frames.
Alternative presentation 2: Use a puppet to act out the story with 'was/went/saw' sentences.
lp.prac: Guided practice: 'Story Order' - children work in pairs to match picture cards to the story sentences; support with sentence starters 'The witch...' and 'She...'.
pracAlt: Alternative practice 1: 'Fill-in-the-Blank' - complete sentences with was/went/saw using word cards.
Alternative practice 2: 'Roleplay the Story' - children act out the story with simple props.
lp.ls: Listening slot: Children listen to a recorded Halloween story and order 4 picture cards; check by having them retell the story using 'was/went/saw'.
lp.re: Reactivation game: 'Simon Says' with Halloween actions - 'Simon says be a ghost!', 'Simon says pretend to eat candy!' to bring back vocabulary and energy.
lp.prod: Production task: 'Halloween Rhyme Time' - groups write a 4-line rhyme about Halloween using the target words, then perform it to the class with actions.
lp.rw: Reading and writing slot: Children read a short Halloween text and circle the words pumpkin, witch, ghost, candy; then write 3 sentences about the story using past simple.
lp.st: Story/song + goodbye: Sing 'The Halloween Song' (tune: 'Twinkle Twinkle') with actions; end with the goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Children pass a pumpkin while music plays, stop and child says a Halloween word.
Teams race to put on witch's hats and say 'I am a witch!'.
Match ghost picture cards to word cards.
Count candy flashcards and say 'I see [number] candies.'
Freeze when story stops, child says what happened next.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a 5-line rhyme with extra Halloween words.
Support / weaker learners: Use word banks with pictures to write sentences.
hw: Homework option 1: Draw a Halloween picture and write 2 sentences about it using past simple.
Homework option 2: Teach a family member the 'I am from Morocco' chant and perform it.
Homework option 3: Prepare 2 facts about Halloween to tell the class.
lp.tip: Use the American Space Oujda's cultural context to link Halloween to Moroccan storytelling traditions, making the theme relatable and engaging.

weeks.obj: Spell and read ch, sh, th words; recognize and say the sounds of letters A-F with 1 word each
weeks.lang: letter-sound links A-F; a is for apple... + digraphs ch, sh, th; thumb, teeth
weeks.act:
Pair dictation, then check with a code
Gratitude turkey craft: one feather = one "I am thankful for..." sentence.
weeks.hw:
read the phonics page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words
Say 3 "I am thankful for..." sentences at home.

skills.L: Listen for the th sound (thumb, teeth) in the phonics song
skills.S: Spell and say ch, sh, th words in relay teams
skills.R: Read digraph words and sort them ch/sh/th
skills.W: Write digraph words; complete the sorting table

lp.wu: Letter Sound Relay: Students line up in two teams. Teacher calls out a letter (A-F), one student from each team runs to the board, writes the letter, and says its sound and word (e.g., 'A is for apple!'). First team with correct letter, sound, and word gets a point.
wuAlt: Flashcard Jump: Students jump when they see the flashcard for the letter sound called out, shouting the sound and word.
Alphabet Bingo: Teacher calls out letter sounds, students cover the corresponding letter on their bingo cards.
lp.pres: Teacher shows Thanksgiving-themed flashcards (apple, bread, cheese, drum, egg, fish) for letters A-F. Models each letter-sound link: 'A is for apple, /æ/.' Students repeat. Introduces digraphs 'ch', 'sh', 'th' with picture cards (cheese, fish, thumb), modeling the sounds and words. Checks understanding by asking 'What sound does this make?' for each digraph.
presAlt: Story Time: Teacher reads a short Thanksgiving story with target words, pausing to emphasize sounds. Students repeat the words.
Mystery Bag: Students reach into a bag to find an object starting with A-F or containing ch/sh/th, say the word, and identify the sound.
lp.prac: Pair Dictation: Students work in pairs. One student says a word (e.g., 'thumb'), the other writes it. They check their spelling using a code on the board (A=apple, B=bread, etc.). Teacher circulates to support pronunciation and spelling.
pracAlt: Digraph Sort: Students sort picture cards into three boxes labeled 'ch', 'sh', 'th' as a group activity.
Word Relay: Teams race to write ch/sh/th words on the board when the teacher shows a picture.
lp.ls: Phonics Song: Students listen to a Thanksgiving phonics song focusing on ch/sh/th sounds. They stand up when they hear the target sounds and point to the correct digraph flashcard on the wall.
lp.re: Sound Jump: After the break, students jump on numbered spots on the floor. Teacher calls out a word (e.g., 'cheese'), students jump on the number corresponding to the sound (1=ch, 2=sh, 3=th).
lp.prod: Gratitude Turkey Craft: Each student makes a paper turkey. For each feather, they write one sentence: 'I am thankful for...' using target words (e.g., 'I am thankful for cheese.'). They present their turkey to the class.
lp.rw: Digraph Word Search: Students find and circle 3 ch/sh/th words in a simple word search puzzle. Then, they copy the words into their notebooks, writing each word three times.
lp.st: Thanksgiving Story: Teacher reads a short story about a thankful turkey, emphasizing target sounds. Students repeat key words. Goodbye routine: Sing 'Goodbye Song', update sticker chart, and line up for high-fives.
g: Students cover letters on their bingo cards when the teacher calls out a sound.
Teams race to match picture cards to the correct digraph on the board.
Students take turns saying a thankful sentence with a target word.
Students hop on squares labeled with ch/sh/th words, saying the sound as they land.
Students pass a turkey plush while saying a thankful sentence; stop when music plays.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a short thankful story using 5 target words.
Support: Use word banks with pictures for the turkey craft.
hw: Read the phonics page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words.
Say 3 'I am thankful for...' sentences at home to your family.
Draw a picture of your favorite Thanksgiving food and label it with its sound.
lp.tip: Use Moroccan context by linking gratitude to local traditions like sharing with neighbors during Ramadan or celebrating the Green March.

weeks.obj: Read a short rhyme and find long-vowel words; match letters G-M to their sounds and first-letter pictures
weeks.lang: letter-sound links G-M + long vowels review; rhyme families
weeks.act: Mini-project: make a poster about phonics and present it
weeks.hw: draw a comic strip about phonics with speech bubbles

skills.L: Listen to a short rhyme and clap the rhymes
skills.S: Read the rhyme aloud with the long-vowel words
skills.R: Read the rhyme and find the long-vowel words (Reading tasks)
skills.W: Write rhyming word families; complete the rhyme

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'Phonics Hopscotch'—draw a grid with G-M letters on the floor, kids hop to the letter called out by the teacher and say its sound, e.g., 'G! /g/ /g/ /g/'
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Letter Sound Bingo'—kids cover G-M flashcards as teacher calls out sounds
Alternative 2: 'I Spy with My Little Eye'—teacher says 'I spy something that starts with /g/', kids guess
lp.pres: Presentation: Show flashcards for G-M with pictures (e.g., 'G' for 'goat', 'M' for 'moon'), model the sounds clearly, drill choral repetition, check by holding up a card and asking 'What sound? What word?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a story about a 'Giant' and a 'Mouse' to introduce G and M sounds
Alternative 2: Realia show-and-tell with objects like a 'grape' (G) and a 'muffin' (M)
lp.prac: Guided practice: 'Phonics Match-Up'—kids match G-M letter cards to picture cards in pairs, teacher monitors and helps with pronunciation
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Sound Sorting'—sort G-M objects into 'long vowel' and 'short vowel' baskets
Alternative 2: 'Letter Relay'—teams race to place G-M letters in order on the board
lp.ls: Listening slot: Play a rhyme with long vowels (e.g., 'The goat on the boat with the coat'), kids clap when they hear a long-vowel word, then list them on the board
lp.re: Reactivation game: 'Phonics Freeze'—kids walk around as teacher plays music, stops and calls a sound (e.g., '/m/'), kids freeze and make the sound with their mouth
lp.prod: Production task: Mini-project 'My Phonics Poster'—groups draw a poster with G-M letters, pictures, and 2-3 long-vowel words, then present to the class, e.g., 'This is G for goat, /g/ /g/ /g/'
lp.rw: Reading and writing slot: Kids trace and copy G-M letters and a short rhyme with long vowels (e.g., 'The moon is high in the sky'), then circle the long-vowel words
lp.st: Story / song + goodbye: Sing 'The Phonics Song' for G-M, then end with the Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line
g: Match letter cards with picture cards face down, take turns flipping two to find a pair
Jump on the correct letter flashcard when teacher says a word
Say a word from the rhyme and kids say a rhyming word
Chain words starting with G-M sounds, e.g., 'goat, moon, muffin'
Act out a G-M word for others to guess
diff: Fast finishers: Write a sentence with 3 G-M words, e.g., 'The big goat ate a muffin'
Support: Trace letters with dotted lines and use picture prompts for matching
hw: Homework 1: Draw a comic strip with 3 frames showing G-M words in speech bubbles, e.g., 'I see a goat! /g/ /g/'
Homework 2: Find 5 objects at home starting with G-M and list them
Homework 3: Write a short rhyme with 2 long-vowel words like 'moon and spoon'
lp.tip: Use Moroccan cultural references like 'Green March' or 'Independence Day' in examples to boost engagement, e.g., 'The flag of Morocco is green' for the /g/ sound.

weeks.obj: Describe each person in my family tree; name 5 family members and say This is my...
weeks.lang: mother, father, sister, brother, baby; This is my... + possessives; He is X years old. She has got...
weeks.act: Roleplay with props: a situation about my family, in pairs
weeks.hw: interview a family member about my family and note 2 answers

skills.L: Listen to family descriptions with ages and jobs
skills.S: Describe each person in my family tree
skills.R: Read a family profile text and complete the tree
skills.W: Write a family-tree profile (3 sentences)

lp.wu: Family Chain: Students stand in a circle, one starts by saying 'This is my mother', the next says 'This is my mother, this is my father', continuing until someone forgets. They sit down, last one standing wins.
wuAlt: Flashcard Speed: Show family flashcards quickly, students shout the English word. Wrong answer = sit down.
Draw & Guess: One student draws a family member (e.g., brother), others guess 'Is this your brother?'
lp.pres: Use a large family tree poster with photos of a Moroccan family (include mother, father, sister, brother, baby). Model sentences: 'This is my mother. She is 35. She has got long hair.' Point to each person, ask 'Who is this?' and elicit answers. Check with thumbs up/down if they understand.
presAlt: Bring in a real family photo album (yours or a colleague's), describe each person using the target language.
Use a short animated story about a family, pause to introduce vocabulary and model sentences.
lp.prac: Family Tree Match: In pairs, students get cut-out family member pictures and labels. They match pictures to labels (mother, father, etc.) and say 'This is my...'. Monitor and correct pronunciation. Support by pre-teaching pronunciation with phonics drills (e.g., 'bro-ther' /'brʌðər/).
pracAlt: Bingo: Students draw a 3x3 grid and write 5 family words. Teacher calls out words, first to complete shouts 'Bingo!' and says the sentences.
Chain Drill: Teacher says 'This is my mother', student 1 repeats and adds 'This is my father', student 2 repeats both and adds 'This is my sister', etc.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Students get a blank family tree. Teacher describes a family: 'This is my father. He is 40. This is my mother. She has got glasses.' Students draw and label. Check by having them hold up their trees and compare in pairs.
lp.re: Family Charades: One student acts out a family member (e.g., rocking a baby for 'baby'), others guess 'Is this your brother?' or 'Is this your mother?'. Fast and physical to re-energize.
lp.prod: Family Roleplay: In pairs, students get props (toy phone, baby doll). One calls the other, introduces their family: 'Hello! This is my sister. She is 8. This is my baby. He is 1.' They take turns. Present to the class for stickers.
lp.rw: Read and Complete: Students read a short text about a family (e.g., 'My name is Fatima. This is my father. He is a teacher. This is my mother. She is a doctor.'). They complete a simple family tree diagram with names and ages.
lp.st: Story: Read 'The Very Busy Family' by Pat Hutchins, focusing on family actions. Sing 'If You're Happy and You Know It' with family actions (clap your hands for 'father', stomp your feet for 'mother'). End with Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Place family flashcards face down. Students turn two over, say 'This is my mother' if they match.
Teacher describes a family member (e.g., 'He is tall. He is my father.'), students guess who it is.
One student draws a family member, others guess 'Is this your sister?'
Students walk around asking 'How old is your mother?' and tally answers on a chart.
In teams, race to label a large family tree poster with the correct words.
Students listen to descriptions and mark the correct family member on their bingo card.
Students act out family members for others to guess.
Students take turns adding a family member to a sentence chain.
Students match family member pictures to words in a timed race.
Teacher asks questions like 'Who is the baby?', students answer with 'This is my baby.'
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write 3 extra sentences about their family (e.g., 'My father likes football').
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank with family words and sentence starters to describe their tree.
hw: Interview your family member: Ask 'How old are you?' and 'What is your job?'. Write 2 answers in your notebook.
Draw your family tree and label 5 members in English.
Write 3 sentences about your family: 'This is my... He/She is... years old.'
lp.tip: Use local family structures (e.g., including grandparents) to make the theme relatable. Praise effort with stickers to build confidence, as Moroccan learners may be shy to speak.

weeks.obj: Compare two toys with bigger than; name 5 toys and ask for them: Can I have the..., please?
weeks.lang: ball, doll, car, teddy, puzzle; I have got a... + comparatives: bigger, smaller, more expensive than
weeks.act: Quiz show in teams about toys
weeks.hw: find a toys worksheet in the library folder and bring it done

skills.L: Listen to toy comparisons (bigger than)
skills.S: Compare two toys with comparatives
skills.R: Read toy comparisons and match to picture pairs
skills.W: Write ___ is bigger / smaller than ___ sentences

lp.wu: Toy Charades: Students take turns miming a toy (ball, doll, car, teddy, puzzle) while classmates guess, saying 'Is it a...?' The mimer responds 'Yes, it is!' or 'No, it isn't!'
wuAlt: Toy Memory Game: Students match picture cards of toys, saying 'I have got a...' when they find a pair
Toy Toss: Students toss a soft ball and name a toy before catching it, saying 'I like the...'
lp.pres: Show flashcards of two toys (e.g., big ball, small ball) and model 'The ball is bigger than the ball.' Use real toys (teddy and car) to demonstrate 'The teddy is smaller than the car.' Ask students to repeat and point to the bigger/smaller toy.
presAlt: Toy Comparison Story: Draw a simple story of a boy with a big teddy and a girl with a small doll, narrating 'The teddy is bigger than the doll.'
Toy Sorting Line: Students line up toy flashcards from smallest to biggest, saying 'The car is smaller than the ball.'
lp.prac: Toy Comparison Worksheet: Students look at picture pairs (e.g., big puzzle, small puzzle) and write 'The puzzle is bigger than the puzzle.' in pairs, with teacher monitoring for accuracy.
pracAlt: Toy Comparison Board Game: Students roll a dice and move, landing on a toy to compare with the teacher's example, saying 'The car is bigger than the teddy.'
Toy Comparison Chain: Students sit in a circle and each adds a toy comparison, e.g., 'The ball is bigger than the doll. The doll is smaller than the car.'
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes toy comparisons (e.g., 'Draw a big ball and a small car. The ball is bigger than the car.') and students draw, then compare with a partner.
lp.re: Toy Relay Race: Teams race to grab two toys from a box, run back, and say 'The [toy] is bigger than the [toy]!' before tagging the next player.
lp.prod: Toy Shop Roleplay: Students work in pairs, one as shopkeeper, one as customer. Customer asks 'Can I have the [toy], please?' and shopkeeper responds 'Here you are. It's bigger than the [other toy].'
lp.rw: Read and Match: Students read short sentences like 'The doll is smaller than the car.' and match them to picture pairs on a worksheet, then write one similar sentence.
lp.st: Goodbye Song: Sing 'The Wheels on the Bus' with toy-themed lyrics ('The teddy on the bus goes hug and hug, hug and hug...'), followed by sticker chart rewards and a high-five line.
g: Students mark pictures of toys on their bingo card when the teacher calls out 'Bigger than the ball!'
Students flip over toy cards to find matching pairs, saying 'I have got a...' when they find one
Students toss a ball and name a toy bigger/smaller than the one they catch, saying 'The car is bigger than the teddy!'
Teams race to line up toy flashcards from smallest to biggest, saying 'The puzzle is smaller than the ball!'
Students take turns being shopkeeper and customer, asking 'Can I have the..., please?' and comparing toys
diff: Fast finishers: Draw their own toy comparison and write 3 sentences, e.g., 'My ball is bigger than my doll.'
Support: Use word banks with 'bigger', 'smaller', and toy names to help write sentences
hw: Find a toy worksheet in the library folder and complete it
Draw two toys at home and write 'The [toy] is bigger than the [toy].'
Ask family about their favorite toys and write one sentence comparing them
lp.tip: Use real toys or colorful flashcards to make comparisons tangible—Moroccan learners respond well to hands-on activities with familiar objects.

weeks.obj: Say which animal is the biggest and fastest; name 6 farm animals and make their sounds in English
weeks.lang: cow, horse, sheep, duck, chicken, pig; It is a... + superlatives: the biggest, the fastest
weeks.act:
Story chain: add a sentence about farm animals in turns
Party week: Christmas vocab stations, carols with actions, "Santa Says".
weeks.hw:
write 4 sentences about farm animals using and/but
Teach the carol to someone at home.

skills.L: Listen to superlative animal facts (the biggest, fastest)
skills.S: Say which animal is the biggest or fastest and why
skills.R: Read an animal fact sheet and find the superlatives
skills.W: Write 3 superlative animal facts

lp.wu: Animal Charades: Students take turns acting out farm animals (cow, horse, sheep, duck, chicken, pig) while others guess. The actor says the sound (e.g., 'Moo!') if stuck. Teacher models first.
wuAlt: Flashcard Speed: Show farm animal flashcards quickly; students shout the name and sound. Award points for speed and accuracy.
Simon Says Animals: Teacher says 'Simon says be a cow'—students act it out. Drop 'Simon says' to catch mistakes.
lp.pres: Use a big story poster showing a farm. Point to each animal and say 'It is a cow. The cow is the biggest.' Repeat for all 6 animals, adding 'the fastest' where relevant (e.g., 'The horse is the fastest'). Students repeat each sentence chorally.
presAlt: Mystery Box: Put toy animals in a box; students feel one and guess 'It is a...' using adjectives. Teacher reveals and models superlatives.
Video Clip: Show a short clip of farm animals; pause to ask 'What is it? Is it the biggest?'.
lp.prac: Superlatives Relay: Two lines of students race to match animal flashcards to superlative cards ('the biggest', 'the fastest'). Teams say the full sentence together when they match.
pracAlt: Find Your Partner: Give half the students animal cards, half superlative cards; they walk around and find their match, then say the sentence.
Board Game: Roll a dice to move on a farm path; land on a space and say 'The [animal] is the [superlative]'.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes animals with superlatives (e.g., 'Draw the biggest animal on the farm'). Students draw and hold up their pictures to check.
lp.re: Santa Says: After break, play 'Santa Says' with farm actions (e.g., 'Santa says hop like a rabbit'). Fast-paced to refocus energy.
lp.prod: Farm Animal Survey: Students walk around asking classmates 'What is your favourite farm animal?' and 'Why is it the best?'. They tally votes and present findings to the group.
lp.rw: Mini-Poster Creation: Students draw 3 farm animals and write a sentence for each using 'It is a...' and a superlative (e.g., 'The sheep is the fluffiest').
lp.st: Read 'The Christmas Farm' story (short, with animal illustrations). Sing 'Jingle Bells' with actions (shake bells for 'jingle'). End with 'Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.'
g: Students mark pictures of animals called out by the teacher.
First to shout 'The horse is the fastest!' wins a point.
Play animal sounds; students hold up the correct flashcard.
Do actions for 'Jingle Bells' while singing.
Follow commands only if preceded by 'Santa says'.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 4-sentence story about a Christmas adventure on the farm.
Support learners: Use word banks with animal names and superlatives for their poster.
hw: Write 4 sentences about farm animals using 'and' or 'but' (e.g., 'The cow is big but the duck is small').
Teach the 'Jingle Bells' actions to a family member and draw a picture of you doing it.
Make flashcards for 3 new farm animals and their sounds.
lp.tip: Use gestures for superlatives (arms wide for 'biggest', fast arm for 'fastest') to reinforce meaning visually, especially for kinesthetic learners.

weeks.obj: Present 3 animal facts to the class; name 4 wild animals; answer What is it? in a guessing game
weeks.lang: lion, elephant, monkey, snake; It is big/small... + has got / lives / can for facts; project talk
weeks.act:
Survey and simple bar graph about wild animals and
"My wish for 2027" craft + Happy New Year song; months-of-the-year line-up game.
weeks.hw:
prepare 2 facts about wild animals and to tell the class
Write your wish on the class poster template.

skills.L: Listen to a model animal presentation
skills.S: Present 3 animal facts to the class
skills.R: Read the fact cards and build my presentation
skills.W: Write my 3 animal facts as cue cards

lp.wu: Play 'Mime the Animal': Teacher mimes a wild animal, students guess 'Is it a lion?' or 'Is it an elephant?' using target vocabulary. Students take turns miming.
wuAlt: Play 'Animal Charades': Students draw an animal flashcard and act it out for the class to guess.
Play 'Flashcard Race': Two teams race to slap the correct animal flashcard when the teacher says the name.
lp.pres: Show flashcards of lion, elephant, monkey, snake. Model sentences: 'A lion is big. It has got a mane. It lives in Africa.' Drill pronunciation. Check understanding by asking 'What has a mane?' and 'Where does a snake live?'
presAlt: Tell a short story about a trip to the zoo using the target animals and facts.
Use a video clip of animals and pause to elicit facts from students.
lp.prac: Play 'Guess the Animal': Teacher describes an animal ('It is big and grey. It has a trunk.'), students guess the animal. Students then describe animals in pairs using 'It is... It has got... It lives...'
pracAlt: Complete a 'My Animal Fact' worksheet by filling in blanks with size, body part, and location.
Play 'Animal Bingo' with fact clues instead of names.
lp.ls: Listen to a short audio recording of a child presenting their animal facts. Students listen and fill in a simple chart with the animal name and one fact they heard.
lp.re: Play 'Months Line-Up': Students get a month card and line up in order from January to December. Teacher asks 'What month comes after March?' to review the year.
lp.prod: Survey and Graph Activity: Students ask 3 classmates 'What is your favorite wild animal?' and tally results. As a group, they draw a simple bar graph on the board to show the most popular animal.
lp.rw: Create 'My Wish for 2027' Craft: Students write one sentence 'I wish...' on a star-shaped paper (e.g., 'I wish I can see a lion.') and decorate it. They stick it on a class New Year poster.
lp.st: Sing 'Happy New Year' song with actions. Read a short picture story about animals celebrating the New Year. End with the goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students match animal flashcards to fact cards, reading the facts aloud.
One student thinks of an animal, others ask 'Is it big? Can it fly?' to guess.
Students ask classmates about favorite animals and draw a bar graph.
Students write a wish for 2027 on a star and decorate it.
Students line up in order from January to December.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a second, more complex fact about their animal using 'It can...'
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence frame 'It is... It has got...' to write their facts.
hw: Prepare 2 facts about a wild animal to tell the class next week.
Write your wish on the class poster template.
Draw a picture of your favorite wild animal and label it.
lp.tip: Use the animal theme to connect with local Moroccan wildlife like the Barbary macaque or desert fox to make the lesson more relatable and culturally relevant.

weeks.obj: Read and act a short Christmas play script; follow the Christmas story frames; join 2 carols; review S1 topics
weeks.lang: Christmas vocabulary; review week 1-13 + script reading; stage directions
weeks.act: Show-and-tell plus 2 questions from the class
weeks.hw: read the christmas page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words

skills.L: Listen to the Christmas play audio
skills.S: Read and act the play script in groups
skills.R: Read the script and highlight the stage directions
skills.W: Write the programme: cast and scenes

lp.wu: Christmas Pictionary: Students draw Christmas words (tree, star, gift) from a hat while others guess. Props: whiteboard markers, hat, word cards. Students say 'It's a...' when guessing.
wuAlt: Christmas Charades: Students act out words like 'sing' or 'decorate' without speaking. Props: no props needed. Students mime actions and others guess.
Christmas Memory Chain: Each student adds a Christmas word to a chain, e.g., 'I see a tree, I see a star...' Props: no props needed. Students repeat the chain with each addition.
lp.pres: Show Christmas flashcards (tree, star, gift, bell, carol) and model sentences: 'It's a Christmas tree.' 'I can sing a carol.' Check understanding by asking 'What is this?' and 'Can you...?'
presAlt: Use a Christmas storybook with pictures, pointing to items and saying their names. Props: storybook. Students repeat after the teacher.
Bring realia: a small tree, a bell, a gift box. Students touch and name items. Props: realia. Teacher asks 'What is this?' and students answer.
lp.prac: Christmas Bingo: Students have bingo cards with pictures. Teacher calls words, students mark them. Props: bingo cards, markers. Teacher says 'Find the star.' and students respond by marking it.
pracAlt: Christmas Word Sort: Students sort flashcards into 'Christmas' and 'Not Christmas' piles. Props: flashcards, two boxes. Students say 'This is Christmas.' or 'This is not Christmas.'
Christmas Roleplay Pairs: Students ask and answer 'What do you see?' using flashcards. Props: flashcards. Students say 'I see a gift.' and 'What do you see?'
lp.ls: Listen to a Christmas play audio. Students follow along with their scripts and highlight stage directions. Props: audio player, scripts. Students raise hands when they hear a direction like 'Santa enters'.
lp.re: Christmas Freeze Dance: Play music, students dance when music stops, they freeze like a Christmas item. Props: music player. Students say 'I'm a tree!' when frozen.
lp.prod: Group Play Practice: Students read and act the Christmas play in groups, using stage directions. Props: scripts, simple props (paper stars). Students perform a short scene for the class.
lp.rw: Write a Christmas Programme: Students fill in cast names and scenes for the play. Props: programme templates, pencils. Students write 'Scene 1: Santa enters' and 'Cast: Ali, Sara'.
lp.st: Sing 'Jingle Bells' with actions, then read a short Christmas story. End with the goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line. Props: storybook, stickers.
g: Students draw words from a hat while others guess.
Students act out words like 'sing' or 'decorate' without speaking.
Each student adds a Christmas word to a chain, e.g., 'I see a tree, I see a star...'
Students mark pictures on bingo cards as teacher calls words.
Students dance and freeze like Christmas items when music stops.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write 3 sentences about their ideal Christmas party.
Support / weaker learners: Use word banks to fill in the programme template.
hw: Read the Christmas page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words.
Draw a picture of your favorite Christmas item and label it in English.
Ask a family member about their Christmas traditions and write 2 sentences.
lp.tip: Use Moroccan Christmas traditions (like sharing sweets) to connect the theme locally, making the lesson more relatable and engaging for students.

weeks.obj: Show what I know in games and a written quiz; show learning through game-based observation tasks
weeks.lang: all S1 outcomes; game-based assessment + semester 1 review
weeks.res: Tests (teacher-chosen games); observation checklist; Reading tasks
weeks.act: Mixed-skills revision circuit in teams
weeks.hw: revise your notes for the assessment week

skills.L: Listening quiz with longer instructions (Tests)
skills.S: Paired picture description plus games observation
skills.R: Read-and-answer quiz across S1 topics
skills.W: Short written quiz with guided sentences

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'Flashcard Race' - Teacher shows flashcards of S1 vocab (animals, food, family), teams take turns shouting the word in English. Props: Flashcards, timer. Children stand in lines, race to say the word first. Teacher says 'Ready, set, go!'
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Simon Says' with S1 verbs (jump, run, draw) - Teacher says 'Simon says jump!' children jump.
Alternative 2: 'Number Bingo' - Teacher calls numbers 1-20, children cross off on bingo sheets.
lp.pres: Presentation: 'Story Time' - Teacher reads a short story about a Moroccan family celebrating Eid. Props: Story flashcards (Eid, couscous, gifts). Model sentences: 'They were happy.' 'He gave a present.' Check understanding: 'Who was happy?' 'What did he give?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: 'Realia Show' - Show Moroccan objects (tagine, mint tea), say 'This is a tagine.' 'It is blue.'
Alternative 2: 'Picture Talk' - Show a picture of a Green March celebration, ask 'What do you see?'
lp.prac: Guided Practice: 'Find the Pair' - Children match picture cards with word cards (S1 nouns). In pairs, they take turns saying 'This is a...' and 'It is a...'. Support: Teacher models first match, helps with pronunciation.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Sentence Building' - Children use word cards to make sentences like 'I have a cat.'
Alternative 2: 'Roleplay Cards' - Pairs practice dialogues like 'What is this?' 'It is a book.'
lp.ls: Listening Slot: 'Instruction Quiz' - Teacher reads 3-step instructions (e.g., 'Stand up, touch your nose, sit down'). Children do the actions. Checks comprehension by observing if they follow correctly.
lp.re: Reactivation Game: 'Musical Statues' - Play Moroccan music, children dance when music stops, freeze. Teacher calls out an S1 word (e.g., 'animal'), children must act like that animal.
lp.prod: Production Task: 'My Mini-Poster' - Children draw a picture of their favorite S1 topic (family, food, pets) and write 2-3 sentences (e.g., 'This is my family. We are happy. I have a cat.'). Present to the class.
lp.rw: Reading and Writing Slot: 'Read and Answer' - Children read a short paragraph about a Moroccan festival (e.g., 'Independence Day is in November. People celebrate.'). Then answer 3 questions (e.g., 'When is it?') in simple sentences.
lp.st: Story / Song + Goodbye: 'Goodbye Song' (to the tune of 'Twinkle Twinkle') - 'Goodbye friends, goodbye friends, see you next time, goodbye friends.' Props: Sticker chart. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teams race to shout the word on the flashcard.
Match picture cards with word cards.
Dance and freeze when music stops, act out a word.
Draw and write about a topic to present.
Read a short text and answer questions.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 extra sentences about their mini-poster.
Support: Use sentence starters like 'This is...' for the writing task.
hw: Homework 1: Draw a picture of your home and label 5 things in English.
Homework 2: Write 5 sentences about your favorite food.
Homework 3: Ask your family 3 questions in English and write the answers.
lp.tip: Use the sticker chart to motivate kids during assessment week—stickers for effort, not just correct answers. Connect tasks to local culture (Eid, Green March) to make learning relevant.
checklist: I can say 10+ S1 words correctly.
I can follow 3-step instructions in English.
I can write 2-3 connected sentences.
I can describe a picture in English.
I can answer simple questions about a story.
I can play a game using S1 language.
I can present my mini-poster to the class.

weeks.obj: Give health advice with should; name 8 body parts and touch them on command
weeks.lang: head, shoulders, knees, arms, hands, feet, eyes, ears + should / shouldn't; headache, stomachache
weeks.act: Pair dictation, then check with a code
weeks.hw: interview a family member about my body and note 2 answers

skills.L: Listen to health problems and match the advice
skills.S: Give advice with should / shouldn't in roleplays
skills.R: Read health advice texts and match to problems
skills.W: Write 3 pieces of advice with should

lp.wu: Simon Says: Teacher calls out body parts with 'Simon says touch your...' or 'Simon says touch my...'. Students must touch the correct part on themselves or the teacher. If they move without 'Simon says', they sit down. Last student standing wins.
wuAlt: Body Part Bingo: Students draw 6 body parts on a grid. Teacher calls out words, students mark them. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Flashcard Race: Two lines of students. Teacher shows a body part flashcard, first student to touch the correct part on themselves gets a point for their team.
lp.pres: Teacher uses a large 'Mr. Potato Head' doll or a drawing on the board. Students name each part as it's added (head, shoulders, knees, etc.). Teacher models: 'You have a head. You have shoulders.' Then introduces health problems: 'I have a headache. You should rest.' Teacher asks: 'If I have a headache, what should I do?' to check comprehension.
presAlt: Storytime: Teacher reads a simple story about a character with a stomachache. Students point to the character's stomach. Teacher models: 'He has a stomachache. He shouldn't eat too much.'
Realia: Teacher brings a bandage and a thermometer. Students guess the body part (knee for bandage, head for thermometer). Teacher models: 'If you have a fever, you should see a doctor.'
lp.prac: Pair Dictation: Student A has a picture of a body with a problem (e.g., red knee). Student B has a picture of advice (e.g., a bandage). Student A describes the problem: 'I have a sore knee.' Student B writes it down. Then they check with a code (e.g., A=problem, B=advice). Teacher circulates to help with spelling and sentence structure.
pracAlt: Matching Game: Students have cards with body problems on one side and advice on the other. They work in pairs to match them correctly, saying the full sentences: 'A headache? You should drink water.'

Roleplay Cards: Students pick a card with a problem (e.g., 'My stomach hurts') and a card with an advice role (e.g., 'You are a doctor'). They practice the dialogue: 'What's wrong?' 'I have a stomachache.' 'You should lie down.'
lp.ls: Students listen to 3 short dialogues between a child and a parent about a health problem. They match each dialogue to a picture of the problem (e.g., Dialogue 1 matches a picture of a child holding their head). Teacher plays the audio twice, then checks answers as a class.
lp.re: Head, Shoulders, Knees, and Toes Remix: After the break, students stand in a circle. Teacher sings the song but replaces 'eyes' and 'ears' with 'headache' and 'stomachache'. Students must touch their head when they sing 'headache' and their stomach when they sing 'stomachache'.
lp.prod: Health Advice Posters: In groups of 3, students create a mini-poster with 3 health problems and 3 pieces of advice using 'should/shouldn't'. They draw simple pictures (e.g., a sun for 'You should go outside'). Each group presents their poster to the class, saying: 'If you have a headache, you should rest.'
lp.rw: Students read 3 short health advice sentences (e.g., 'If you have a cold, you should drink tea.'). They match each sentence to a picture of the problem (e.g., a picture of a child with a runny nose). Then, they write 2 original advice sentences in their notebooks: 'If I have a stomachache, I should...'
lp.st: Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line. Teacher leads a call-and-response song: 'Goodbye, goodbye, see you next time! Wave your hands and say goodbye!' Students get a sticker for the day and line up for a high-five with the teacher.
g: Teacher calls out 'Simon says touch your...' or 'Simon says touch my...'. Students must touch the correct part.
Students draw 6 body parts on a grid. Teacher calls out words, students mark them. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Two lines of students. Teacher shows a body part flashcard, first student to touch the correct part on themselves gets a point.
Students match problem cards (e.g., 'sore knee') to advice cards (e.g., 'put a bandage') and say the full sentence.
Students pick a problem card and an advice role card (e.g., 'doctor') and practice the dialogue.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a dialogue between a doctor and a patient with 4 turns each, using 'should/shouldn't'.
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank with body parts and 'should/shouldn't' to complete sentence starters like 'If I have a ___, I should ___.'
hw: Interview a family member: Ask 'What do you do when you have a headache?' and write down their answer in English.
Draw a picture of yourself with a health problem (e.g., a cold) and write one piece of advice for yourself.
Create a 'My Body' poster with 8 labeled body parts and one health tip.
lp.tip: Use the local context of the American Space Oujda by connecting health advice to common Moroccan home remedies, like 'If you have a stomachache, you should drink mint tea,' to make the language more relevant and memorable.

weeks.obj: Describe actions with how: quickly, slowly; understand and produce 8 action verbs with TPR
weeks.lang: clap, jump, run, walk, swim, fly, eat, sleep + adverbs of manner; action verbs review
weeks.act: Mini-project: make a poster about actions and movement and present it
weeks.hw: find a actions and movement worksheet in the library folder and bring it done

skills.L: Listen to actions with how + adverbs and act them
skills.S: Describe actions: jump quickly, walk slowly
skills.R: Read action + adverb sentences and match to mimes
skills.W: Write adverb sentences about 4 actions

lp.wu: Simon Says: Students stand, teacher calls out actions with adverbs (e.g., 'Simon says jump quickly!'), students perform the action. If 'Simon says' is omitted, students freeze. Teacher says 'Simon says clap slowly' and students clap slowly.
wuAlt: Action Charades: Teacher mimes an action (e.g., swimming fast), students guess 'You swim quickly!', or 'Action Race: Two students race to the board to circle the correct verb card when called (e.g., 'Run!').
lp.pres: Teacher uses flashcards showing actions (run, jump, etc.) and adverbs (quickly, slowly). Model sentences: 'The boy runs quickly' with a fast running mime, 'The girl walks slowly' with a slow walking mime. Ask students: 'Is he running fast or slow?' to check understanding.
presAlt: TPR Story: Teacher tells a simple story about a superhero, using TPR for actions ('He flies quickly to save the cat!'), or 'Adverb Charades: Teacher mimes an action and students guess the adverb ('You eat slowly!').
lp.prac: Adverb Bingo: Students get bingo cards with action+adverb phrases (e.g., 'jump quickly'). Teacher calls out actions with adverbs, students mark the phrase. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins. Support: Write phrases on the board.
pracAlt: Action Relay: Teams line up, teacher whispers an action+adverb (e.g., 'swim slowly') to the first student, they mime it to the next, who guesses the phrase. Or 'Match the Cards': Students match action flashcards to adverb flashcards (e.g., 'run' + 'quickly').
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher reads sentences like 'The bird flies quickly' and 'The turtle walks slowly', students draw the action in a box. Check drawings to see if they matched the adverb.
lp.re: Action Freeze Dance: Play music, students dance freely. When music stops, teacher calls out an action+adverb (e.g., 'sleep slowly'), students freeze in that pose. Fast-paced and fun.
lp.prod: Mini-Poster Project: In groups, students create a poster with 4 actions and adverbs (e.g., 'The lion runs quickly'). They draw pictures and write sentences. Then, each group presents their poster to the class, saying 'Look! He jumps quickly!'
lp.rw: Read and Match: Students read short sentences (e.g., 'She eats slowly') and match them to the correct picture from a worksheet. Then, they write 2 new sentences about actions they like (e.g., 'I walk quickly to school').
lp.st: Story: Read 'The Busy Bee' story, where the bee flies quickly, walks slowly, etc. Then, sing the 'Action Song' with gestures. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teacher calls out actions with adverbs, students perform only if 'Simon says' is included.
Teams mime action+adverb phrases, next student guesses the phrase.
Students mark action+adverb phrases on bingo cards when called.
Students freeze in action+adverb poses when music stops.
Students match action flashcards to adverb flashcards.
diff: Fast finishers: Draw a 5th action on their poster and write a sentence.
Support: Use sentence starters like 'He ____ quickly' to fill in the verb.
hw: Find an actions worksheet in the library folder and complete it.
Draw 4 actions at home and write the adverb (e.g., 'My cat sleeps slowly').
Ask a family member to do an action, then describe it (e.g., 'You eat quickly!').
lp.tip: Use TPR consistently to reinforce kinesthetic learning, as it helps Moroccan kids retain vocabulary better. Link actions to local contexts, like 'walk quickly to the souk' or 'fly slowly like a desert bird'.

weeks.obj: Do a fruit-market roleplay with money; name 6 fruits; answer Do you like...? with yes/no
weeks.lang: apple, banana, orange, grapes, strawberry, lemon + How much is/are...? numbers + money
weeks.act: Roleplay with props: a situation about fruit, in pairs
weeks.hw: write 4 sentences about fruit using and/but

skills.L: Listen to market dialogues with prices
skills.S: Fruit-market roleplay with money and How much...?
skills.R: Read price lists and check the totals
skills.W: Write my market shopping list with prices

lp.wu: Fruit Relay Race: Students line up in teams. Teacher calls a fruit (e.g., 'apple!'), first student runs to the table, picks up the correct flashcard, and runs back. Team with the most correct flashcards wins.
wuAlt: Fruit Bingo: Teacher calls out fruits, students cross them off their bingo cards. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Fruit Charades: Student mimes a fruit, others guess 'Is it a...?'
lp.pres: Teacher brings a basket of real fruit (apple, banana, orange, grapes, strawberry, lemon). Holds each up, says 'This is an apple,' students repeat. Then models 'How much is the apple? It's 5 dirhams.' Students repeat. Checks understanding by asking 'Show me the apple.'
presAlt: Fruit Story: Teacher tells a short story about buying fruit at the souk, using target language. Students point to the fruits as they're mentioned.
Fruit Market Video: Show a short clip of a fruit market, pause, ask 'What fruit is that? How much is it?'
lp.prac: Fruit Shop Roleplay: In pairs, one student is the shopkeeper with price cards, the other is the customer. They practice 'How much is the...?' 'It's... dirhams.' 'Do you like...?' 'Yes, I do/No, I don't.' Teacher circulates, models if needed.
pracAlt: Fruit Memory Game: Students match picture cards with word cards, saying the word and price when they find a match.
Fruit Dice Game: Roll a dice, say the fruit and a price (e.g., 'Grapes! 6 dirhams!').
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher reads a shopping list ('I want an apple, 3 bananas, and some grapes.'). Students draw the fruit and write the total price. Teacher checks drawings and totals.
lp.re: Fruit Freeze Dance: Play music, students dance with fruit flashcards. When music stops, teacher calls a fruit, students holding it must freeze and say 'I like...!'
lp.prod: Fruit Market Project: In groups of 3, students create a mini fruit market. One is shopkeeper, one is customer, one is the 'price checker'. They use play money and price lists. Each group presents their market to the class.
lp.rw: Read and Match: Students read a simple price list ('Apple: 5 dirhams, Banana: 3 dirhams') and match it to the correct picture of a fruit shop. Then they write 2 sentences: 'I like apples but I don't like lemons.'
lp.st: Read 'The Hungry Caterpillar' story, stopping to name the fruits. Sing 'Do You Like Bananas?' song. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students toss a ball and say a fruit and price before catching it.
Student draws a fruit, others guess 'Is it a...?'
Move around the board, land on a fruit, say the price.
Match picture to word, saying the fruit name.
Ask classmates 'Do you like...?' and tally the answers.
diff: Fast finishers: Design their own fruit shop poster with prices and 3 sentences about what they like.
Support: Use word banks with fruit names and prices for the roleplay.
hw: Write 4 sentences about fruit using 'and' and 'but' (e.g., 'I like apples and bananas, but I don't like lemons.')
Draw a picture of your favorite fruit and write its price in dirhams.
Ask your family 'Do you like...?' for 3 fruits and write down their answers.
lp.tip: Use real fruit to engage tactile learners and connect to local souk culture. For the roleplay, use Moroccan dirhams to make it culturally relevant and practical.

weeks.theme: Food 2: I like / I don't like
weeks.obj: Say what I like and explain why; talk about food likes and dislikes in simple sentences
weeks.lang: I like... / I do not like...; yum! yuck! + I like... because...; Do you like...? review
weeks.act:
Quiz show in teams about food
Ramadan routines vocab (suhoor, iftar, mosque); days-of-the-week fasting chart craft.
weeks.hw:
prepare 2 facts about food to tell the class
Draw your iftar table and label 5 foods in English.

skills.L: Listen to like/because opinions about food
skills.S: Say what I like and explain why
skills.R: Read food opinions and agree or disagree
skills.W: Write I like ___ because ___ sentences

lp.wu: Food Charades: Teacher shows flashcards of food (dates, harira, msemen, orange juice), students mime and say 'I like/don't like' the food. Winner gets a sticker.
wuAlt: Food Bingo: Students mark 'like' or 'don't like' on a grid as teacher calls out foods.
Quick Quiz: Students stand if they like the food, sit if they don't (dates, milk, couscous).
lp.pres: Teacher holds up suhoor/iftar flashcards, models 'I like dates for suhoor because they are sweet.' and 'I don't like milk for iftar because it is cold.' Students repeat in pairs. Teacher asks 'Do you like...?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Picture Story: Show a comic of a child eating suhoor/iftar, elicit 'I like/don't like' sentences.
Realia: Pass around a date, ask 'Do you like this?' and teach 'yum!/yuck!'
lp.prac: Team Quiz Show: Teams take turns answering 'Do you like...?' for Ramadan foods. Correct answers get points. Teacher monitors for 'because' sentences.
pracAlt: Food Survey: Students walk around asking 'Do you like...?' and tally results on a worksheet.
Matching Game: Match food pictures to 'I like/don't like' cards.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes an iftar table ('I like msemen and tea. I don't like lentils.'), students draw and label 5 foods. Check drawings for accuracy.
lp.re: Stand Up/Sit Down: Teacher says 'I like harira!', students stand. 'I don't like soup!', students sit. Fast-paced to re-energize.
lp.prod: Iftar Table Craft: Students draw their ideal iftar table, label 5 foods, and write 'I like ___ because ___' for 2 foods. Present to group with 'This is my iftar. I like...'.
lp.rw: Days-of-the-Week Fasting Chart: Students copy the days of the week, draw a sun for fasting days, and write 'I fast on Monday' for 2 days. Teacher checks spelling.
