lp.st: Goodbye Song: 'If You're Happy and You Know It' with verses 'If you like dates, clap your hands!' End with sticker chart and high-five line.
g: Students mime food and class guesses 'Do you like...?'
Teams answer 'Do you like...?' for Ramadan foods.
Students react to 'I like/don't like' statements.
Students ask 'Do you like...?' and tally results.
Draw and label foods, present to class.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 'I like/don't like' sentences about Ramadan.
Support learners: Trace food words and use sentence starters.
hw: Prepare 2 facts about food to tell the class (e.g., 'Dates are sweet.')
Draw your iftar table and label 5 foods in English.
Ask your family 'Do you like...?' for 3 foods and write the answers.
lp.tip: Use local Ramadan foods (harira, msemen, dates) to build cultural connection and relevance for Moroccan learners.

weeks.obj: Describe a person from head to toe; name 6 clothing items; say I am wearing...
weeks.lang: t-shirt, trousers, dress, shoes, hat, jacket + is wearing + has got; descriptions in detail
weeks.act: Story chain: add a sentence about clothes in turns
weeks.hw: read the clothes page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words

skills.L: Listen to head-to-toe descriptions and draw the person
skills.S: Describe a person from head to toe (guess who)
skills.R: Read descriptions and match to the photos
skills.W: Write a 3-sentence person description

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'Guess the Item' — Teacher holds up flashcards of clothes one by one; students shout the English word; first to say correctly gets a point.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Simon Says' with clothes commands like 'Simon says touch your shoes'.
Alternative 2: 'Clothes Bingo' — students draw 6 items from the list and cross them off as the teacher names them.
lp.pres: Presentation: Show a story of a child getting dressed; use flashcards to introduce t-shirt, trousers, dress, shoes, hat, jacket; model 'She is wearing a red dress' and 'He has got a blue hat'; check understanding by asking 'What is he wearing?' and 'Has she got a hat?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a realia bag with actual clothes items; students pull one out and say the word.
Alternative 2: Show a short video of someone dressing up; pause to name each item.
lp.prac: Guided practice: 'Describe and Draw' — Teacher describes a person (e.g., 'She is wearing a yellow hat and green shoes'); students draw in pairs; walk around to help with spelling and pronunciation.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Matching Pairs' — students match clothing words to pictures on flashcards.
Alternative 2: 'Sentence Race' — teams race to write sentences like 'He is wearing a jacket' on the whiteboard.
lp.ls: Listening slot: 'Listen and Draw' — Teacher describes a person (e.g., 'He has got a black jacket and brown shoes'); students draw on a worksheet; compare drawings in pairs to check comprehension.
lp.re: Reactivation game: 'Fashion Show' — students walk down a 'catwalk' while saying what they are wearing (e.g., 'I am wearing a blue t-shirt and jeans'); others guess who it is.
lp.prod: Production task: 'Guess Who?' — Students work in groups; one student describes a classmate (e.g., 'She is wearing a pink dress and a hat'); others guess who it is; present the best descriptions to the class.
lp.rw: Reading and writing slot: 'Read and Match' — Students read short descriptions (e.g., 'He is wearing a blue jacket and trousers') and match them to photos; then write 3 sentences about their own outfit.
lp.st: Story / song + goodbye: Sing 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' with clothing variations; read a short story about a child choosing clothes for a festival; end with Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teams race to dress a paper doll with flashcards.
Students close eyes; teacher removes one clothing item; they guess what's missing.
Students draw clothing items for others to guess.
Teacher says 'I spy something you wear on your feet'; students guess 'shoes'.
Students take turns describing what the teacher is wearing.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a 5-sentence description of a Moroccan festival outfit.
Support / weaker learners: Use word banks with pictures to help write sentences.
hw: Homework option 1: Read the clothes page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words.
Homework option 2: Draw a picture of yourself and write 3 sentences about what you are wearing.
Homework option 3: Interview a family member about their clothes and write 2 sentences.
lp.tip: Use local context like the Green March or Independence Day to make descriptions relevant (e.g., 'He is wearing a green jacket for the Green March').

weeks.obj: Present a mini weather forecast; recognize 4 weather words and report today's weather
weeks.lang: sunny, rainy, windy, cloudy; What is the weather like? + It will be...; seasons and months review
weeks.act: Survey and simple bar graph about weather and seasons
weeks.hw: draw a comic strip about weather and seasons with speech bubbles

skills.L: Listen to a mini weather forecast
skills.S: Present a mini weather forecast with It will be...
skills.R: Read the forecast maps and complete the chart
skills.W: Write tomorrow's forecast (2 sentences)

lp.wu: Weather Charades: Teacher acts out sunny, rainy, windy, cloudy; children guess and shout the word. Props: none. Children say 'It is sunny!' when correct.
wuAlt: Weather Bingo: Teacher calls weather words; children mark the flashcard on their bingo card. Props: bingo cards, weather flashcards.
Weather Pictionary: Teacher draws weather words; children guess and say the word. Props: whiteboard, markers.
lp.pres: Teacher shows flashcards of sunny, rainy, windy, cloudy while modeling 'What is the weather like? It is sunny.' Then uses a toy globe to point to different seasons, reviewing months. Children repeat chorally. Teacher asks 'What is the weather like in summer?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Weather Story: Teacher tells a short story about a boy who experiences all four weather types, using flashcards to illustrate. Props: weather flashcards, boy puppet.
Weather Video: Teacher plays a short animated video of a weather forecast, pausing to ask 'What is the weather like?' Props: tablet, projector.
lp.prac: Weather Drill: Children work in pairs. One child holds a flashcard, the other asks 'What is the weather like?' and the other answers 'It is sunny.' Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation. Props: weather flashcards.
pracAlt: Weather Memory Game: Children flip over weather flashcards to find matching pairs. When they find a pair, they say 'It is sunny.' Props: weather flashcards.
Weather Board Game: Children roll a die and move to a square with a weather word. They must say 'It is [weather word].' Props: board game, dice, weather flashcards.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes a simple weather forecast (e.g., 'It will be sunny in Rabat, rainy in Casablanca'). Children draw the weather on a map of Morocco. Props: worksheet with map of Morocco, crayons.
lp.re: Weather Relay: Two lines of children race to the board to draw a weather word (sunny, rainy, windy, cloudy) called by the teacher. Props: whiteboard, markers.
lp.prod: Weather Survey: Children ask 5 classmates 'What is your favorite season?' and record answers on a simple bar graph. Then they present their findings: 'Mohammed likes summer because it is sunny.' Props: survey worksheet, crayons.
lp.rw: Read and Write: Children read a short paragraph about a boy's favorite season and weather. Then they write 2 sentences about their own favorite season and weather. Props: worksheet with paragraph, pencils.
lp.st: Weather Song: Sing 'What's the Weather Like Today?' with actions. Props: none. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teacher calls weather words; children mark the flashcard on their bingo card.
Children act out weather words; others guess and say the word.
Children race to draw a weather word on the board.
Children flip over flashcards to find matching pairs and say the word.
Children ask classmates about favorite seasons and graph the results.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Draw a weather map of Morocco with 4 different cities and write a forecast for each.
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank to fill in the blanks in the reading paragraph.
hw: Draw a comic strip with 4 panels showing different weather and seasons with speech bubbles.
Write 3 sentences about the weather today in Oujda and what you will wear.
Ask your family about their favorite season and draw a picture of it.
lp.tip: Use local context (e.g., 'It is sunny in Oujda today') to make the language relevant. Celebrate Islamic holidays like Eid with a 'Eid weather' activity to connect with learners' culture.

weeks.obj: Write pet-care instructions with imperatives; say I have got a (pet) and ask And you?
weeks.lang: cat, dog, bird, fish; I have got... Have you got...? + imperatives + Feed/Don't feed; care card
weeks.act: Show-and-tell plus 2 questions from the class
weeks.hw: interview a family member about pets and I have got and note 2 answers

skills.L: Listen to pet-care instructions
skills.S: Dictate pet-care rules to a partner
skills.R: Read pet-care instructions and order them
skills.W: Write pet-care instructions with imperatives

lp.wu: Pet Charades: Students take turns acting out pet actions (e.g., barking like a dog, meowing like a cat) while others guess. Teacher asks 'What pet is it?' and students respond 'It's a dog/cat/bird/fish.'
wuAlt: Pet Flashcard Race: Two teams race to match pet flashcards to their names on the board.
Pet Sound Bingo: Teacher calls out pet names, students cover the matching animal picture on their bingo sheet.
lp.pres: Teacher shows a stuffed dog and says 'I have got a dog.' Then asks a student 'And you?' to elicit 'I have got a...' Teacher uses flashcards to model 'I have got a cat/dog/bird/fish.' To check understanding, teacher holds up a fish and asks 'Have you got a fish?' Students respond 'Yes, I have' or 'No, I haven't.'
presAlt: Pet Family Photo: Teacher brings in a family photo with pets and says 'I have got a dog and a cat.' Students point and repeat.
Pet Survey Demo: Teacher surveys 3 students with 'Have you got a pet?' and writes answers on the board.
lp.prac: Find Your Pet Partner: Each student gets a pet flashcard. They walk around asking 'Have you got a...?' When they find a match (e.g., two dogs), they high-five and sit down. Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation of 'got' and question intonation.
pracAlt: Pet Memory Game: Students match pet flashcards to 'I have got a...' sentence cards in pairs.
Pet Circle Drill: Students stand in a circle, pass a pet toy, and say 'I have got a...' then pass to the next student who adds a new pet.
lp.ls: Teacher reads a short story about a boy who has a fish. Students listen and raise their hand when they hear the word 'fish.' After, students draw the fish in their notebook to show comprehension.
lp.re: Pet Freeze Dance: Teacher plays music, students dance. When music stops, teacher calls out a pet (e.g., 'bird!'), students freeze and flap their wings like a bird. Last student to freeze is out.
lp.prod: Pet Care Card Project: In groups, students create a care card for a pet (dog, cat, bird, or fish). They write 2-3 imperatives like 'Feed it twice a day' and 'Don't give it chocolate.' Groups present their cards to the class.
lp.rw: Reading and Writing: Students read a short paragraph about 'My Cat' and circle all the imperatives (e.g., 'Brush it', 'Play with it'). Then, they write 2 sentences about how to care for their own pet using 'Feed' or 'Don't feed.'
lp.st: Teacher reads the story 'The Lost Parrot' about a boy looking for his pet bird. After, students sing the goodbye song 'If You're Happy and You Know It' with actions like 'clap your hands' and 'stomp your feet.'
g: Students mark off pets on their bingo sheet as the teacher calls them out.
Teacher says 'Simon says feed the dog' and students pretend to feed a toy dog.
Students act out pet actions for others to guess.
Students ask 'Have you got a...?' to find a matching pet partner.
Students match care instruction cards to the correct pet picture.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a 4-sentence paragraph about their dream pet.
Support / weaker learners: Trace over pre-written imperatives like 'Feed the dog' and draw a picture.
hw: Interview a family member: 'Have you got a pet?' and write down 2 answers.
Draw a picture of your family's pet and write 1 care instruction.
Make a pet care card for a friend's pet with 2 rules.
lp.tip: Use the Green March (Moroccan holiday) to connect by discussing pets in families—many Moroccan families have cats or birds, making the theme relatable and culturally relevant.

weeks.obj: Read U-Z words and sort them by sound; link letters N-T to sounds and build 3-letter words
weeks.lang: letter-sound links N-T; word building: cat, pen... + blends and word families; sorting
weeks.act:
Write and perform a 4-line rhyme about phonics
Eid greetings roleplay "Eid Mubarak!"; gift-and-cookie counting game.
weeks.hw:
find a phonics worksheet in the library folder and bring it done
Write the Eid greeting card we started in class.

skills.L: Phonics listening; sort the words by sound
skills.S: Say and sort U-Z words by sound in teams
skills.R: Read U-Z word cards and sort into sound families
skills.W: Write the sorted word lists

lp.wu: Phonics Relay Race: Students line up in two teams. Teacher shows a flashcard (e.g., 'sun'), first student runs to the board, writes the first letter ('s'), runs back, tags next student who writes 'u', then next writes 'n'. First team to spell correctly wins. They shout: 'S-U-N! Sun!'
wuAlt: Sound Sorting Race: Students grab U-Z flashcards from a pile and sort them into 'short vowel' and 'long vowel' baskets on their table, naming each letter sound as they place it.
Phonics I Spy: Teacher says 'I spy with my little eye something beginning with /p/', students guess words like 'pen' or 'pencil'.
lp.pres: Teacher holds up letter N flashcard: 'This is letter N. It says /n/. Like in 'nose'.' Students repeat '/n/'. Then shows T: 'This is T. It says /t/. Like in 'tiger'.' Students repeat '/t/'. Teacher models blending: 'N + T = NT. Like in 'ant'.' Checks with thumbs up/down: 'Is this /nt/?' for 'net' and 'cat'.
presAlt: Storytime: Teacher reads a short story about 'Noon the Tiger' who finds a 'net' and a 'nut', emphasizing the /n/ and /t/ sounds. Students repeat the words after each page.
Phonics Hopscotch: Draw a hopscotch board with N-T letters. Students hop and say the sound: 'N! /n/! T! /t!' when they land on a letter.
lp.prac: Word Building Pairs: Students get letter cards (n, t, a, e, p). Teacher says 'cat', students find c, a, t and build it. Then 'pen', 'net'. Teacher circulates, helping with blending. Game: 'Phonics Bingo'—Teacher calls words, students mark them on their bingo card with U-Z words.
pracAlt: Sound Families Sort: Students work in groups. They have a set of U-Z word cards (e.g., 'sun', 'tap', 'net', 'pen'). They sort them into 'short a' (cat, pen) and 'short e' (net, tent) families, saying the words as they sort.
Blend Challenge: Teacher writes blends on the board (nt, st, nd). Students race to add a vowel to make a real word (e.g., nt + a = ant).
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes a picture using target sounds: 'Draw a net. Draw a tent. Draw a pen in the tent.' Students draw and hold up their pictures. Teacher checks if they included all items with /n/ and /t/ sounds.
lp.re: Eid Freeze Dance: Play Arabic music. Students dance. When music stops, teacher calls 'Eid Mubarak!', students freeze and say it back. Restart. After break, this reactivates the Eid theme quickly.
lp.prod: Eid Greeting Roleplay: Students practice in pairs. One is a guest, one is a host. Guest: 'Eid Mubarak! I brought cookies.' Host: 'Eid Mubarak! Thank you! How many cookies?' They count 1-5 cookies using numbers. Then switch roles.
lp.rw: Eid Card Writing: Students finish the Eid card started in class. They write: 'Eid Mubarak!' inside, draw a gift, and write '1 gift' or '2 cookies' using the target words. They trace the sentence if needed.
lp.st: Story: 'The Eid Phonics Party'—a short story about friends sharing gifts with words like 'net', 'tent', 'pen'. Song: 'Eid Mubarak' song with actions (wave, hug). Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students shoot a ball into a basket. If they make it, they must say a U-Z word with /n/ or /t/ sound correctly to get a point.
Students sit in a circle. Teacher gives out cookie cards (1-5). They pass a cookie and say 'Eid Mubarak! One cookie!' when they pass it.
Students match word cards (e.g., 'cat', 'pen') to the correct family picture (cat family, pen family) on the table.
Students sit in a circle. They pass a 'gift' (box) and say 'Eid Mubarak! I have a gift.' When music stops, the one holding it opens it and says 'It's a pen!' or 'It's a net!'
Students hop on letter flashcards (N, T, U, Z). When they land, they must say a word with that sound (e.g., 'N! Net!')
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a 4-line rhyme about phonics, e.g., 'N is for net, T is for tent, Pen and pen, They all went!'
Support / weaker learners: Use letter tracing worksheets for N and T, and build words with magnetic letters.
hw: Find a phonics worksheet in the library folder and bring it done next class.
Write the Eid greeting card we started in class for a family member.
Ask your family 3 words with /n/ or /t/ sounds (e.g., 'What is in the kitchen?') and write them down.
lp.tip: Use the Eid theme to make phonics meaningful—connect letters to gifts, cookies, and greetings. Moroccan learners will engage more with familiar cultural contexts.

weeks.obj: Use a picture dictionary to find U-Z words; complete the alphabet with sounds U-Z; sing the alphabet song
weeks.lang: letter-sound links U-Z; alphabetical order + dictionary skills: A-Z order, guide words
weeks.act: Pair dictation, then check with a code
weeks.hw: write 4 sentences about phonics using and/but

skills.L: Listen to dictionary-skills instructions
skills.S: Use a picture dictionary in pair tasks
skills.R: Find U-Z words in the picture dictionary (Comprehension)
skills.W: Write my dictionary page entries A-Z

lp.wu: Alphabet Relay: Divide class into 2 teams. One student runs to the board, writes a letter U-Z, next student writes the next, etc. First team to write all letters wins. They cheer 'U-V-W, we are the best!'
wuAlt: Letter Sound Jump: Teacher calls 'Jump for U!' kids jump and say /uː/. Fast-paced review.
Alphabet Chain: Each student says one letter + sound, e.g., 'U is for umbrella, /uː/'.
lp.pres: Show flashcards U-Z with pictures. Drill sounds: 'U is for umbrella, /uː/'. Model dictionary use: 'Look at guide words: Umbrella-zebra. Find umbrella!' Students point to the page.
presAlt: Storytime: Read a short story with U-Z words, e.g., 'The unicorn saw a xylophone.' Kids repeat the words.
Alphabet Poster: Add U-Z letters to a class poster, each student draws one word.
lp.prac: Pair Dictation: Student A says a U-Z word, Student B writes the letter. Swap. Check with a code: Teacher shows flashcards, kids say the sound and letter.
pracAlt: Alphabet Order Race: Give mixed U-Z cards. Pairs sort them fastest. Say 'U comes before V!'
Find the Word: Teacher calls 'Find umbrella!' Kids point in their picture dictionaries.
lp.ls: Listen and Circle: Play audio of U-Z words. Kids circle the correct word in their picture dictionaries. Check answers as a class.
lp.re: Alphabet Dance: Play the alphabet song. Kids dance and freeze when the music stops. Teacher calls a letter, e.g., 'Freeze on V!'
lp.prod: My Dictionary Page: Each student creates a page for 2 letters U-Z. Draw 3 pictures, write the words. Present to their group: 'This is V for violin.'
lp.rw: Trace and Write: Students trace U-Z letters in their notebooks. Write 2 sentences: 'U is for umbrella. V is for violin.'
lp.st: Sing the Alphabet Song: Full class with actions. End with goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teams race to write U-Z letters on the board.
Teacher calls a letter, kids jump and say the sound.
Kids point to U-Z words in their picture dictionaries.
Teacher describes a U-Z word, kids find it.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a sentence for each U-Z letter, e.g., 'U is for umbrella, it is blue.'
Support: Trace letters with dotted lines, use alphabet posters for reference.
hw: Write 4 sentences about phonics using and/but, e.g., 'U is for umbrella and V is for violin.'
Draw 5 U-Z words and label them.
Sing the alphabet song to your family.
lp.tip: Use the American Space Oujda's picture dictionaries with local images (e.g., 'zebra' in a Moroccan context) to boost engagement and cultural relevance.

weeks.obj: Compare Easter in two countries; review colors, numbers, animals through seasonal games
weeks.lang: review weeks 16-24 language + Easter words; compare with but/and
weeks.act: Mixed-skills revision circuit in teams
weeks.hw: revise your notes for the assessment week

skills.L: Listen to Easter customs in two countries
skills.S: Compare Easter in two countries with and / but
skills.R: Read two short custom texts and compare
skills.W: Write 2 comparison sentences: Easter here / there

lp.wu: Easter Egg Hunt Race: Hide 20 numbered plastic eggs around the classroom. Kids race in pairs to find and count them aloud: 'One egg, two eggs, three eggs!'
wuAlt: Spring Bingo: Call out colors/animals (e.g., 'blue bird'), kids mark their cards and shout 'Bingo!'
Simon Says Spring: 'Simon says hop like a bunny!' or 'Simon says paint a red egg!'
lp.pres: Show flashcards of Easter in Morocco vs. USA (e.g., 'Morocco: couscous, USA: ham'). Model sentences: 'In Morocco, we paint eggs. In the USA, they hunt eggs.' Check with thumbs-up/down.
presAlt: Use a Venn diagram on the board with two circles: 'Morocco' and 'USA', kids add sticky notes
Read a short dialogue: 'Do you eat chocolate eggs?' 'Yes, and we paint them!'
lp.prac: Pair Comparison Drill: Kids get picture cards (e.g., 'lambs', 'chocolate') and make sentences: 'In Morocco, we have lambs. In the USA, they have chocolate.' Support with sentence frames.
pracAlt: Easter Memory Game: Flip cards to match pairs, then compare: 'The bunny is here, but the egg is there'
Team Relay: Run to grab a flashcard and race to say a comparison sentence
lp.ls: Listen to two short audio clips (Moroccan vs. Easter customs). Kids tick a chart: 'Paint eggs? Yes/No' and 'Eat lamb? Yes/No'.
lp.re: Bunny Hop Relay: Kids hop like bunnies to the board, write a color/number word, and hop back. Team with most words wins.
lp.prod: Mini-Poster Project: In groups, draw two scenes (Easter in Morocco vs. USA) and write 2 sentences: 'Here, we... There, they...' Present to the class.
lp.rw: Read two short texts (5 lines each) about Easter customs. Kids circle differences with colored pencils and write one comparison sentence: 'In Morocco, we... but in the USA, they...'
lp.st: Read 'The Easter Bunny's Big Day' story, then sing 'Five Little Bunnies' with actions. End with goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Kids throw soft eggs and count catches: 'One, two, three!'
Call out a color, kids grab the matching flashcard
Act out animals (e.g., 'lamb') for teammates to guess
Teams race to write a comparison sentence on the board
Spot 5 differences between two Easter pictures
diff: Fast finishers: Draw a new Easter tradition and write 3 sentences
Support: Use word banks with 'and/but' and picture prompts
hw: Make a list of 3 Easter/spring words and draw them
Interview family: 'Do you like Easter? Why?' and write 2 sentences
Play a spring word game with a sibling (e.g., 'I spy with my little eye...')
lp.tip: Use the Moroccan context to build confidence—compare Easter with local celebrations like Aid al-Fitr to show respect for their culture while teaching comparisons.

weeks.obj: Describe my dream house room by room; name 4 rooms and say where simple things are
weeks.lang: house, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom; Where is mummy? She is in the... + there is/are + big/small adjectives
weeks.act: Roleplay with props: a situation about my house, in pairs
weeks.hw: read the my house page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words

skills.L: Listen to dream-house descriptions
skills.S: Describe my dream house room by room
skills.R: Read house descriptions and match to floor plans
skills.W: Write my dream-house description (3 sentences)

lp.wu: Flashcard Race: Show room flashcards (kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, living room) one by one; students shout the room name and make a sentence like 'It's big!'
wuAlt: Simon Says: Play Simon Says with prepositions, e.g., 'Simon says stand in the bedroom'
Miming Game: Students mime activities (e.g., cooking) and others guess the room
lp.pres: Use a big house poster; point to each room and model 'This is the kitchen. It is big. Where is the fridge? It is in the kitchen.'; ask students to repeat and point to objects in the poster
presAlt: Story Time: Read a short story about a family in their house, highlighting room names and prepositions
Realia Tour: Bring toy furniture; place items in 'rooms' on a mat and ask 'Where is the bed?'
lp.prac: House Map Pairs: Give each pair a blank house map with rooms; one student places furniture flashcards, the other asks 'Where is the table?' and answers 'It is in the kitchen.'
pracAlt: Bingo Game: Students draw a house grid and write room names; call out 'Find the bathroom!' and mark off
Flashcard Swap: Students pass room flashcards and say 'I have the kitchen. It is small.'
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Play an audio describing a dream house (e.g., 'There is a big bedroom and a small bathroom'); students draw the rooms and objects as they hear them
lp.re: Room Relay: Divide students into teams; run to the board, write a room name, and run back; first team to write 4 rooms wins
lp.prod: Dream House Roleplay: In pairs, one student describes their dream house using 'There is/are + big/small', the other draws it; present to the class
lp.rw: Read and Match: Students read short descriptions (e.g., 'I sleep here. It is small.') and match them to room pictures; then write 3 sentences about their own house
lp.st: Story: Read 'The Magic House' story about a house with different rooms; end with the Goodbye Song, sticker chart, and high-five line
g: Teacher hides toy furniture; students ask 'Where is the bed?' and hunt for it
Students mime room activities (e.g., brushing teeth) and others guess
Students assemble a house puzzle and name each room
Call out 'Jump in the bedroom!' and students hop to the correct flashcard
One student describes a room, others draw it
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 sentences about their dream house with adjectives
Support: Use sentence starters like 'There is a ____ in the ____.'
hw: Read the 'My House' page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words
Draw your dream house and label 2 rooms
Ask your family about their house and write 2 sentences
lp.tip: Use Moroccan home elements (e.g., riad, courtyard) to connect the theme to students' lives; praise effort, not accuracy, to build confidence

weeks.obj: Give directions from one piece of furniture to another; describe where things are using in, on, under
weeks.lang: table, chair, bed, box; in, on, under + prepositions of movement: into, out of
weeks.act: Quiz show in teams about furniture
weeks.hw: draw a comic strip about furniture with speech bubbles

skills.L: Listen to directions between pieces of furniture and move the toy
skills.S: Give directions from one piece of furniture to another
skills.R: Read direction sentences and follow the route
skills.W: Write directions with into, out of, under

lp.wu: Furniture Relay: Students race to touch named furniture flashcards. Teacher says 'Touch the table!', students run and touch the table flashcard on the wall. Last to touch sits down.
wuAlt: Simon Says: Teacher says 'Simon says put your pen under the chair!', students follow. If no Simon Says, they freeze.
Find My Spot: Teacher calls out furniture, students quickly move to stand near the real object in class.
lp.pres: Teacher uses a big 'My Bedroom' poster. Points to a teddy bear on the bed and says 'The teddy is on the bed'. Then moves it under the bed and says 'Now the teddy is under the bed'. Uses a box to show 'in the box'. Models sentences: 'The cat is in the box. The cat is on the box. The cat is under the box'. Asks students 'Where is the cat?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Storytime: Teacher reads a short story about a mouse hiding in, on, and under furniture. Uses gestures for prepositions.
Realia Hunt: Teacher hides a small toy in, on, under classroom furniture. Students ask 'Is it in the box?' and teacher answers 'Yes, it is' or 'No, it isn't'.
lp.prac: Furniture Bingo: Students get bingo grids with furniture pictures. Teacher calls out sentences like 'The book is on the table'. Students cover the picture if it matches. Teacher walks around to help with pronunciation and sentence structure.
pracAlt: Preposition Pairs: Students work in pairs. One student places an object (e.g., a pencil) in, on, under a piece of furniture. The other student says a sentence like 'The pencil is under the chair'.
Drawing Dictation: Teacher dictates sentences like 'Draw a ball on the bed. Draw a cat under the table'. Students draw and compare.
lp.ls: Listen and Move: Teacher gives directions like 'Walk to the chair. Put your pencil under the chair'. Students follow the instructions with their bodies and a pencil. Teacher checks if they are in the correct spot.
lp.re: Furniture Freeze Dance: Play Moroccan pop music. When music stops, teacher shouts a preposition, e.g., 'Under!'. Students must quickly find something to get under. Last one to freeze is out.
lp.prod: Furniture Treasure Hunt: In teams, students hide a small toy somewhere in the classroom. They write 3 clues on a piece of paper using 'in', 'on', 'under', e.g., 'It is under the big table'. Another team follows the clues to find the treasure. Teams present their clues.
lp.rw: Comic Strip Creation: Students draw a simple comic with 3-4 boxes showing a character moving furniture or hiding things. In each box, they write a speech bubble or a caption using 'in', 'on', 'under', e.g., 'The book is on the bed'.
lp.st: Teacher sings 'The Preposition Song' (to the tune of 'Twinkle Twinkle') with gestures. Then reads a short story about a boy looking for his lost toy under the bed, on the table, and in the box. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teams answer questions like 'Where is the ball? (show picture)' for points.
One student hides an object, others ask 'Is it in the box?' until they find it.
Draw a hopscotch with 'in', 'on', 'under'. Students say the word as they land on it.
Students act out a preposition (e.g., hiding under a chair) for others to guess.
Students compare two similar room pictures and spot differences using 'in', 'on', 'under'.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a short story (3-4 sentences) about a lost toy using all three prepositions.
Support / weaker learners: Cut and paste pictures of furniture and objects, then label them with 'in', 'on', 'under'.
hw: Draw your bedroom and write 3 sentences about where things are (e.g., 'My teddy is on the bed').
Create a 'Find My Toy' poster with 3 clues using in, on, under for a friend to solve.
Write a short dialogue between two friends looking for a lost cat using prepositions.
lp.tip: Use real classroom furniture to make prepositions tangible. For cultural relevance, relate the lesson to Moroccan homes by showing pictures of traditional furniture.

weeks.obj: Tell the time and describe my day; sequence 5 morning actions with English words
weeks.lang: wake up, wash, brush my teeth, eat, go to school + o'clock/half past; daily routine adverbs
weeks.res: Flashcards/Daily Routine; Music/Songs (brush my teeth); Comprehension
weeks.act: Story chain: add a sentence about morning routines in turns
weeks.hw: interview a family member about morning routines and note 2 answers

skills.L: Listen to times and daily events
skills.S: Tell the time and describe my day in order
skills.R: Read o'clock / half-past sentences and match the clocks
skills.W: Write my day timeline with times

lp.wu: Flashcard Race: Students line up in two teams. Teacher shows a flashcard of a morning routine action (e.g., 'brush teeth'), first student to shout the English word and mime it gets a point for their team.
wuAlt: Morning Charades: One student mimes a morning action (e.g., 'wake up'), others guess the English word.
Quick Review Bingo: Each student draws a 3x3 grid with words like 'wash', 'eat', 'go to school'. Teacher calls out actions, students cross them off first to shout 'Bingo!'
lp.pres: Teacher uses a big storybook with pictures of a child's morning routine. 'Look! Sam wakes up at 7 o'clock. He washes his face. He brushes his teeth.' Teacher points to a clock and says '7 o'clock'. Students repeat chorally. Teacher asks 'What time does Sam wake up?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Realia Demo: Teacher brings a toothbrush, soap, and a toy clock. 'I wake up at 6 o'clock. I wash my face. I brush my teeth.' Students repeat actions and sentences.
Video Clip: Show a short, silent video of a morning routine. Teacher narrates: 'He wakes up. He eats breakfast. He goes to school.'
lp.prac: Clock Matching Game: In pairs, students have a set of clock faces (o'clock/half past) and sentence cards ('I eat at 8 o'clock'). They match the clocks to the sentences. Teacher circulates to help with pronunciation and time vocabulary.
pracAlt: Sentence Dominoes: Students have dominoes with a time on one half and a morning action on the other (e.g., '7:00' | 'wake up'). They take turns connecting them to make a logical sequence.
Routine Relay: Two lines of students. Teacher whispers a sentence like 'I brush my teeth' to the first student. They whisper it down the line. Last student runs to the board and writes/draws it.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher reads a short story: 'I wake up at 7 o'clock. I eat breakfast at 7:30. I go to school at 8 o'clock.' Students draw the three events in order on a piece of paper with three empty clock faces. Teacher checks drawings for correct sequence.
lp.re: Action Race: After the break, students stand. Teacher calls out a time (e.g., '8 o'clock!') and an action (e.g., 'go to school!'). Students must mime the action and say the sentence 'I go to school at 8 o'clock!' The fastest group gets a point.
lp.prod: My Morning Timeline Project: In groups of three, students draw and write a 4-step timeline of their own morning routine using sentence starters like 'I wake up at ___. I eat at ___.' Each group presents their timeline to the class, pointing and reading their sentences.
lp.rw: Read and Match: Students read a short paragraph: 'My name is Fatima. I wake up at 6:30. I eat cereal. I go to school at 7:45.' They then match the paragraph to the correct set of three clock faces (6:30, 7:00, 7:45) by drawing a line.
lp.st: Teacher tells a simple story using a felt board: 'The Lazy Lion's Morning'. The lion wakes up late, rushes, and forgets to brush his teeth. The story uses target vocabulary. End with the 'Goodbye Song' (e.g., 'See You Later Alligator'), updating the sticker chart, and a high-five line as students exit.
g: Students have bingo cards with clock faces. Teacher calls out times ('half past seven'), students cover the matching clock.

One student is 'Mr. Wolf', back to the class. Class chants 'What's the time, Mr. Wolf?' He answers a time (e.g., '8 o'clock') and class takes that many steps. If he says 'dinnertime!', he chases them.
Two teams race to put a set of picture cards in the correct morning order (wake up, wash, eat, go to school).
Students play in pairs. A grid has times in the boxes. Student A says a sentence ('I eat at 8 o'clock') to claim a box with '8 o'clock'.
Students turn over cards with morning actions and times. They must match a picture of 'brushing teeth' with a card saying '7:30'.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a 5-sentence paragraph about their sibling's morning routine using 'He/She' and times.
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank with pictures to fill in the blanks in sentences like 'I ___ at 7 o'clock.' (wake up/wash/eat).
hw: Interview a family member about their morning routine and write down 2 answers in English (e.g., 'My dad wakes up at 5:30 AM.', 'My mom drinks tea for breakfast').
Draw a picture of your family eating breakfast and write one sentence about it (e.g., 'We eat at 7:30 AM').
Make a paper clock and show the time you usually go to school.
lp.tip: Use the local context of Ramadan to discuss morning routines before dawn (Suhoor), connecting the lesson to students' lives and making the language more meaningful.

weeks.obj: Run a review quiz show for the class; show confidence across the year's topics in station games
weeks.lang: all year outcomes + semester 2 review quiz
weeks.act:
Mixed-skills revision circuit in teams
Recycle-sort game in English; plant-a-seed craft with "First... then..." instructions.
weeks.hw:
revise your notes for the assessment week
Find 3 things at home to recycle and name them in English.

skills.L: Quiz-show listening station
skills.S: Run a review quiz show for the class
skills.R: Review reading station - match and answer
skills.W: Write 2 quiz questions for another team

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'Recycle Relay' — children line up in teams, race to a bin with mixed paper/plastic items, shout the English name (e.g., 'bottle!', 'box!'), and run back. Teacher times each team for 60 seconds.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Recycle Pictionary' — draw a recyclable item, teammates guess the English word.
Alternative 2: 'Recycle Bingo' — teacher calls items, children cross them off their bingo cards.
lp.pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of recyclable items (paper, plastic, glass) and non-recyclable (food, plastic bags). Model sentences: 'This is paper. We can recycle paper.' Ask: 'Can we recycle this?' Children respond 'Yes, we can' or 'No, we can't'.
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a short story about a character sorting trash into bins.
Alternative 2: Bring real recyclable items (e.g., bottles, cans) for children to touch and name.
lp.prac: Guided practice: 'Recycle Sort Game' — children work in teams to sort picture cards into 'recycle' or 'don't recycle' bins. Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation. Teams earn points for correct sorts.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Recycle Memory' — match pairs of recyclable items with their English names.
Alternative 2: 'Recycle Charades' — act out recycling actions, teammates guess the verb (e.g., 'cut', 'fold').
lp.ls: Listening slot: 'Earth Day Quiz' — children listen to teacher ask questions about recycling (e.g., 'What can we recycle?'). They raise hands to answer. Teacher checks comprehension by asking follow-ups: 'Why can't we recycle plastic bags?'
lp.re: Reactivation game: 'Recycle Tag' — children run around the room. Teacher shouts a recyclable item; tagged children freeze and say its English name. Last child unfreezes them.
lp.prod: Production task: 'Plant-a-Seed Craft' — children follow 'First... then...' instructions to plant seeds in cups (e.g., 'First, put soil in the cup. Then, put a seed in the soil. Next, add water.'). They present their cups to the class using the target language.
lp.rw: Reading and writing slot: 'Recycling Poster' — children read a short paragraph about Earth Day (e.g., 'We can help Earth. Recycle paper, plastic, and glass.'). Then, they write 2 sentences about what they recycle at home (e.g., 'I recycle bottles. I recycle boxes.').
lp.st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Sing 'Reduce, Reuse, Recycle' song with actions. End with 'Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line'.
g: Teams take turns answering review questions for points.
Race to sort items into bins and name them.
Follow 'First... then...' instructions to plant seeds.
Draw recyclable items for teammates to guess.
Cross off items called by the teacher.
diff: Fast finishers: Design a 'Recycling Hero' badge with 3 English words.
Support: Use sentence starters for writing (e.g., 'I recycle...').
hw: Homework 1: Find 3 things at home to recycle and name them in English.
Homework 2: Draw a picture of you recycling and write 1 sentence.
Homework 3: Ask your family 1 recycling question in English.
lp.tip: Use local examples (e.g., Moroccan plastic recycling bins) to make the theme relatable. Praise effort over accuracy to build confidence.
checklist: I can name 5 recyclable items in English.
I can sort items into 'recycle' and 'don't recycle'.
I can follow 'First... then...' instructions.
I can write 2 sentences about recycling.
I can answer quiz questions about Earth Day.
I can present my plant-a-seed craft to the class.
I can play a recycling game with my team.

weeks.obj: Present my best work and get my certificate; complete game-based final assessment; celebrate the year
weeks.lang: all year outcomes + full-year presentation; I can... statements
weeks.act:
Mixed-skills revision circuit in teams
Jobs guessing game (What does a ... do?); thank-you cards for workers we know.
weeks.hw:
revise your notes for the assessment week
Draw one job you love and write 3 sentences about it.

skills.L: Final listening game tasks (Tests)
skills.S: Present my best work and a short speaking chat
skills.R: Reading comprehension check sheet
skills.W: I can... statements writing; certificate page

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'I Spy' with jobs flashcards. Teacher holds up a job flashcard (e.g., 'teacher') and says 'I spy someone who helps students learn.' Students guess 'Is it a teacher?' Teacher responds 'Yes, it is! What does a teacher do?' Students say 'A teacher teaches.'
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Jobs Charades' - students act out a job and others guess 'Is he a doctor?' 'Does she drive a bus?'
Alternative 2: 'Jobs Pictionary' - students draw a job and others guess 'Is it a cook?'
lp.pres: Presentation: Show 5 job flashcards (doctor, teacher, farmer, builder, cook). Model 'What does a doctor do?' 'A doctor helps sick people.' Ask 'What does a farmer do?' Students respond 'A farmer grows food.' Check understanding with 'Who helps sick people?' 'Who grows food?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a short story about a boy who wants to be a firefighter. Ask 'What does a firefighter do?'
Alternative 2: Bring in toy props (stethoscope, book, seeds, hammer, spoon) and ask 'What does this person do?'
lp.prac: Guided practice: 'Jobs Guessing Game' in teams. Team A describes a job without naming it (e.g., 'They wear a uniform. They drive a big red truck. They help people.') Team B guesses 'Is it a firefighter?' Teacher monitors and helps with sentence starters 'They... ' 'They can... '
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Match the Job to the Tool' - students match flashcards (doctor-stethoscope, builder-hammer) and say 'A doctor uses a stethoscope.'
Alternative 2: 'Jobs Bingo' - students listen to descriptions and mark the job on their bingo card
lp.ls: Listening slot: 'Jobs Listening Test' - students listen to 5 short audio clips (e.g., 'I work in a hospital. I help people feel better.') and write the job (doctor, teacher, etc.) on a worksheet. Teacher plays clips twice and checks answers.
lp.re: Reactivation game: 'Jobs Relay Race' - two lines of students. Teacher shows a job flashcard, first student runs to the board, writes the job, runs back, tags next student. Team with all jobs written first wins.
lp.prod: Production task: 'My Best Work Presentation' - students show their favorite project from the year (e.g., a poster, a story) and say 'This is my poster. I drew a teacher. She teaches students. I like this work.' Then they ask friends 'What is your best work?'
lp.rw: Reading and writing slot: 'I Can... Statements' - students complete a certificate page by writing 5 sentences like 'I can read a short story.' 'I can write 3 sentences about my job.' Then they draw a picture of their favorite job.
lp.st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Sing 'The People in Your Neighborhood' song (Sesame Street). Teacher says 'Today we celebrate Labour Day! Thank you to all workers.' Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students act out a job and others guess 'Is it a doctor?'
Students draw a job and others guess 'Is it a cook?'
Students race to write jobs on the board
Students write their skills and get a sticker
Students make cards for workers they know
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 sentences about a job they want to do in the future
Support: Trace the job names and draw a picture with teacher help
hw: Homework 1: Draw one job you love and write 3 sentences about it (e.g., 'I love being a teacher. I teach students. I help them learn.')
Homework 2: Ask your family about their jobs and write them down
Homework 3: Review your notes for the final assessment week
lp.tip: Use Labour Day to connect to local Moroccan workers (e.g., farmers, builders) and discuss how they help the community. This makes the lesson culturally relevant and meaningful.
checklist: I can say 5 jobs in English
I can ask 'What does a ... do?'
I can answer 'A ... ... '
I can present my best work
I can write 3 sentences about a job
I can read a short text about jobs
I can complete the I Can... certificate

levels.desc: For children aged 9–11 who can produce full sentences and short dialogues. The year pushes into A1+–A2 with story-based and project-based learning, short roleplays, reading short paragraphs, writing two to three connected sentences, and a first introduction to the simple past, possessives, and comparatives — aligned with Cambridge Movers/Flyers.

levels.label: Teens · Beginners

weeks.theme: Welcome and getting to know you
weeks.obj: introduce themselves, ask 5 get-to-know-you questions, and complete a partner profile
weeks.lang: be (am/is/are); Wh- questions (what, where, how old); possessive adjectives
weeks.act: Human bingo; name toss with questions; partner profile poster; class rules negotiation
weeks.hw: write a 5-sentence profile of your partner

skills.L: Listen to partner profiles and complete the grid
skills.S: Ask and answer 5 get-to-know-you questions
skills.R: Read sample profiles and underline the question words (Worksheets)
skills.W: Complete a partner-profile card in full sentences

lp.wu: Human Bingo: Students walk around with a bingo grid containing prompts like 'likes football', 'has a brother', 'lives near school'. They ask 'Do you like football?' and mark 'BINGO' when they find someone who says 'Yes, I do'.
wuAlt: Name Toss: Students stand in a circle and toss a soft ball, saying their name and one hobby, e.g., 'I'm Ali and I like football'.
Two Truths and a Lie: Students write three statements about themselves, two true and one false, and others guess the lie.
lp.pres: Teacher introduces 'be' verbs with flashcards showing people with names, ages, and hometowns. Model sentences: 'I am 14', 'She is from Oujda', 'They are students'. Check understanding by asking 'How old are you?' and 'Where are you from?' to students.
presAlt: Realia Introduction: Teacher shows personal items (a book, a photo, a key) and says 'This is my book. I am a teacher. It is blue'.
Animated GIFs: Display GIFs of teens with captions like 'He is 13', 'They are friends' to illustrate 'be' + adjectives.
lp.prac: Pair drill: Students practice 'What's your name?', 'How old are you?', 'Where are you from?' with a partner. Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation. Then, play 'Find Someone Who...' with a worksheet where students write names next to prompts like 'is 13', 'likes pizza'.
pracAlt: Question Chain: Students sit in a circle and take turns asking the person next to them a question, e.g., 'What's your name?', and that person answers and asks the next student.
Flashcard Match: Match name cards with age/hometown cards, e.g., 'Lina' + 'is 14' + 'is from Berkane'.
lp.ls: Teacher reads three short profiles of Moroccan teens aloud. Students listen and fill in a grid with names, ages, and hometowns. Check answers as a class, e.g., 'Is Amina 13 or 14?'
lp.re: Stand Up, Sit Down: Teacher says a sentence like 'If you are 13, stand up' or 'If you like football, sit down'. Students move quickly to practice 'be' + adjectives.
lp.prod: Partner Profile Poster: Students work in pairs to create a poster with their partner's name, age, hometown, and hobbies. They use full sentences like 'He is 14', 'She lives in Oujda', 'He likes football'. Present posters to the class.
lp.rw: Read three sample profiles and underline the question words (What, Where, How old). Then, write 3 questions about a new profile using the underlined words, e.g., 'What's his name?', 'Where is she from?'
lp.st: Sing 'Hello, Hello' with actions (wave, clap, stomp). Close with: 'Today we learned to introduce ourselves. Thank you, class!'
g: Students ask 'Do you like football?' to fill their grid.
Students toss a ball and say name + hobby.
Students write names next to prompts like 'is 13'.
Students move based on 'be' + adjective sentences.
Students ask and answer questions in a circle.
diff: Fast finishers: Add a hobby and a favorite color to their partner's profile.
Support: Use sentence starters like 'He is ___', 'She lives in ___' on the worksheet.
hw: Write a 5-sentence profile of your partner.
Draw a picture of your partner and label 3 things (e.g., 'football', 'book').
Record a 30-second video introducing your partner.
lp.tip: Use local references (e.g., 'Are you from Oujda?') to make the language relevant. Pair stronger and weaker learners to boost confidence.

weeks.obj: describe 4 family members or friends with simple details
weeks.lang: possessive 's; have got; adjectives (tall, kind, funny)
weeks.act: Family tree project; guess who descriptions; adjective matching relay
weeks.hw: family tree + 3 description sentences

skills.L: Listen to family descriptions and identify who is who
skills.S: Describe 4 family members with have got + adjectives
skills.R: Read short family profiles and match the details (Lesson Plans/Family)
skills.W: Write 3 sentences about my family or friend

lp.wu: Family Charades: Teacher acts out a family member (e.g., cooking, playing football) and students shout the word in English. Students then take turns in pairs acting out a family member while their partner guesses.
wuAlt: Family Bingo: Teacher calls out family words (mother, father, sister, brother) and students cross them off their bingo cards. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Family Chain: Students sit in a circle. Student 1 says 'I have a mother.' Student 2 says 'Student 1 has a mother. I have a father.' and so on, building a chain.
lp.pres: Teacher shows flashcards of family members (mother, father, sister, brother). Teacher models: 'This is my mother. She is kind.' Students repeat. Teacher introduces possessive 's: 'This is my mother. She is my father's wife.' Teacher checks understanding by asking: 'Who is kind?' and 'Whose wife is she?'
presAlt: Family Photo Story: Teacher brings a real photo of her family and tells a short story using the target language: 'This is my sister. She is tall and funny. She has got a dog.' Students ask questions.
Puppet Show: Teacher uses puppets to act out a family scene. Puppet 1 says 'I am tall. I am kind.' Puppet 2 says 'He is my brother. He has got a blue shirt.'
lp.prac: Adjective Matching Relay: Students line up in two teams. At the front, there are two sets of cards: family member pictures and adjective cards (tall, kind, funny). The first student runs to match a family member with an adjective (e.g., 'My father is tall.'), runs back, and tags the next student. The first team to match all cards wins.
pracAlt: Find Your Partner: Each student gets a card with either a family member or an adjective. They walk around asking 'Who has got...?' or 'What are you?' to find their match and form a complete sentence.
Sentence Building Race: In pairs, students get jumbled sentence cards (e.g., 'my / brother / is / funny'). They race to arrange them correctly and read the sentence aloud.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes a family member: 'This is my sister. She is tall. She has got long hair. She is kind.' Students draw the person. Teacher then shows a picture to check. This checks comprehension of listening for details.
lp.re: Stand Up If...: Teacher says 'Stand up if you have got a brother.' 'Stand up if your mother is kind.' Students stand up or sit down. This reactivates the language physically after the break.
lp.prod: Guess Who?: In pairs, Student A thinks of a family member. Student B asks questions: 'Is he tall? Is she funny? Has he got a car?' Student A answers: 'Yes, he is. No, she isn't. Yes, he has.' Student B guesses who it is. This encourages freer use of the language.
lp.rw: Read and Match: Students read 3 short family profiles (e.g., 'My name is Amina. I have a brother. His name is Karim. He is tall and funny.'). They match each profile to a picture. Then, they write 3 sentences about their own family using 'have got' and adjectives.
lp.st: Teacher sings a simple family song like 'The Family in the House' with gestures. Then, the teacher says: 'Today we learned to describe family members. Thank you for your hard work. See you next week!'
g: Students act out a family member (e.g., cooking, playing football) and their partner guesses the word.
Teams race to match family member pictures with adjective cards to make sentences.
Students with family member and adjective cards find their match to form a sentence.
Students ask yes/no questions to guess which family member their partner is thinking of.
Teacher gives clues about family members and students stand up if it applies to them.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a description of a famous Moroccan celebrity or athlete.
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence frame: 'My _______ is _______ and _______. He/She has got _______.'
hw: Draw your family tree and write 3 sentences: 'My _______ is _______. He/She has got _______. He/She is _______.'
Interview a family member in Arabic and write 3 simple facts in English about them.
Write a short paragraph (3-4 sentences) about your best friend using 'have got' and adjectives.
lp.tip: Use realia like family photos to make the lesson personal and relatable. For Moroccan learners, connect the theme to local family values, like respect for elders, which are universal but can be highlighted in English.

weeks.obj: describe their school day using present simple I/you/we/they
weeks.lang: present simple; time expressions (at 7 o'clock, in the morning)
weeks.act: Routine survey mingle; daily timeline drawing; verb drill tennis
weeks.hw: write your real school day in 6 sentences

skills.L: Listen to a student's day and order the events
skills.S: Describe my school day with present simple + time
skills.R: Read a routine text and find the time expressions
skills.W: Write my daily routine paragraph (4 sentences)

lp.wu: Routine Charades: Teacher mimes waking up, eating breakfast, going to school. Students shout the verbs (wake up, eat, go). Teacher writes them on the board.
wuAlt: Verb Tennis: Teacher says 'wake up', student says 'eat breakfast', teacher says 'go to school', student says 'study English'.
Quick Survey: Teacher asks 'What time do you wake up?' to 3 students, writes answers on the board.
lp.pres: Teacher shows flashcards of a school day (7:00 wake up, 8:00 go to school, 10:00 have a break, 1:00 eat lunch, 4:00 go home). Models 'I wake up at 7 o'clock' and 'You wake up at 7 o'clock'. Checks understanding by asking 'What time do you wake up?' to a student.
presAlt: Storytime: Teacher tells a simple story about 'Ali's School Day' using the flashcards and gestures.
Realia: Teacher shows a real alarm clock and says 'I wake up at 7 o'clock'.
lp.prac: Verb Drill Tennis: Students stand in two lines. Teacher says 'I wake up at...', student in the other line says 'You wake up at...'. Continue with 'go to school', 'have a break', 'eat lunch', 'go home'.
pracAlt: Routine Survey Mingle: Students walk around asking 'What time do you...?' for 3 routines, write answers on a grid.
Daily Timeline Drawing: Students draw a timeline of their school day and label times with 'at...'.
lp.ls: Listen and Order: Teacher reads a short script about 'Leila's School Day' (e.g., 'I wake up at 7. I go to school at 8. I have a break at 10. I eat lunch at 1. I go home at 4.'). Students cut and paste 5 picture cards in the correct order.
lp.re: Routine Relay: Two lines of students. Teacher says a routine (e.g., 'wake up'), first student runs to the board, writes the verb, runs back. Next student does the next one. Fastest team wins.
lp.prod: My School Day Presentation: Students work in pairs. They draw 4 pictures of their school day and write a sentence for each (e.g., 'I wake up at 7 o'clock. I go to school at 8 o'clock. I eat lunch at 1 o'clock. I go home at 4 o'clock.'). They present to the class.
lp.rw: Read and Find: Students read a short text about 'Youssef's Day' (e.g., 'Youssef wakes up at 7 o'clock. He goes to school at 8 o'clock. He has a break at 10 o'clock. He eats lunch at 1 o'clock. He goes home at 4 o'clock.'). They underline all the time expressions (at 7 o'clock, etc.).
lp.st: Song: Sing 'What Time Do You...?' to the tune of 'Frère Jacques'. End with the routine: 'Today we learned to talk about our school day. Thank you, class!'
g: Students volley present simple sentences back and forth in pairs.
Students ask 'What time do you...?' to classmates and write answers.
Students draw a timeline of their school day with time expressions.
Students listen to a script and order picture cards of a daily routine.
Teams race to write present simple verbs on the board.
Students draw and present their daily routine in 4 sentences.
Students read a text and underline time expressions.
Students sing a song about daily routines.
Recap: 'Today we can describe our school day. Thank you, class!'
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a 6-sentence paragraph about their ideal school day.
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence frame: 'I ______ at ______ o'clock.' for 4 routines.
hw: Write your real school day in 6 sentences (e.g., 'I wake up at 6:30. I eat breakfast at 7:00. I go to school at 7:30. I have a break at 10:00. I eat lunch at 1:00. I go home at 4:00.')
Draw a picture of your school day and label 3 activities with time expressions.
Ask a family member about their daily routine and write 3 sentences about it.
lp.tip: Use gestures for all verbs to support visual and kinesthetic learners. For the American Space Oujda context, connect the topic to local school schedules (e.g., 'In Morocco, we have a long lunch break at 1 o'clock').

weeks.obj: compare school subjects and say what they like and why
weeks.lang: school subjects; like/don't like + noun; because
weeks.act:
Subject popularity graph in teams; school debate mini (favorites); interview a classmate
Spooky story chain: each pair writes one paragraph, read aloud with lights off; Halloween taboo.
weeks.hw:
Participation quiz ( Kahoot-style on paper)
Write the ending of the class spooky story (6-8 lines).

skills.L: Listen to subject opinions (like / don't like + because)
skills.S: Compare subjects and say what I like and why
skills.R: Read a school-life text and answer 3 questions
skills.W: Write my subject review with because

lp.wu: Subject Charades: Teacher writes 5 school subjects on the board (Math, Art, Science, PE, English). Students take turns miming the subject while others guess, saying 'You like [subject]!' or 'It's [subject]!'
wuAlt: Subject Bingo: Teacher calls out subjects, students cross them on a 3x3 grid with pictures. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Subject Speed Chat: Students walk around and ask 'What subject is this?' pointing to a flashcard, then reply 'I like it!' or 'I don't like it!'
lp.pres: Teacher shows flashcards of school subjects, models 'I like Math because it's fun' and 'I don't like Science because it's difficult'. Students repeat chorally. Teacher asks 'Do you like Math?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Subject Survey: Teacher walks around asking 'Do you like Art?', students respond with thumbs up/down. Teacher tallies on the board, modeling 'Three students like Art.'
Mini-Story: Teacher tells a short story about a student who likes PE but doesn't like History, using gestures for 'like' and 'don't like'.
lp.prac: Subject Popularity Graph: Teams of 3 receive a graph with subjects on the x-axis. They ask classmates 'Do you like [subject]?', tally responses, and draw bars. Teams report 'Most students like Art!'
pracAlt: Subject Debate Mini: Teams debate 'Math is better than Art'. Each student says 'I like [subject] because...' with one reason. Teacher times 1-minute turns.
Find Someone Who...: Students walk around with a grid, asking 'Do you like Science?', writing names of those who say 'Yes'.
lp.ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher describes a student's favorite subject: 'He likes Art because he can draw pictures.' Students draw the subject and reason, then compare in pairs.
lp.re: Subject Jump: Teacher calls out a subject (e.g., 'PE!'), students jump if they like it, crouch if they don't. Teacher asks 'Why?' after each round.
lp.prod: Interview a Classmate: Students pair up, ask 'What's your favorite subject? Why?', then report back to the class: 'Fatima likes History because it's interesting.'
lp.rw: Read a short text about a student's week, answer 3 questions: 'What subject does he like? Why? What subject doesn't he like?' Students write answers in full sentences.
lp.st: Spooky Story Chain: Pairs write one paragraph about a haunted school, using 'I like/don't like [subject]' (e.g., 'I don't like History because the ghosts talk!'). Read aloud with lights off. End with 'Today we learned to say what subjects we like and why. Thank you, class!'
g: Students describe a subject without saying its name or 3 taboo words (e.g., for Math: 'numbers, plus, calculator').
Match subject flashcards with 'like/don't like' cards, saying sentences like 'I like Art!'.
Two teams race to write 5 subjects they like on the board, saying 'I like [subject]!' for each.
Teacher says a subject, students spell it. If correct, they say 'I like [subject]!'.
Teacher posts subjects in corners, students go to their favorite and say 'I like [subject] because...'
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 more reasons why they like/dislike a subject.
Support: Use sentence frames 'I like [subject] because it's...' with word bank (fun, easy, interesting).
hw: Write 6 sentences about your favorite subject (e.g., 'I like English. It's fun. I don't like Math. It's difficult.')
Draw your ideal classroom with your favorite subjects, label 3 items.
Interview a family member about their school subjects, write 2 sentences.
lp.tip: Use Moroccan school examples (e.g., 'I like Arabic because it's my language') to build cultural relevance. Keep sentences short and repeat 'because' often for reinforcement.

weeks.obj: talk about hobbies using like + -ing and adverbs of frequency
weeks.lang: like/love/hate + -ing; always, sometimes, never
weeks.act:
Find someone who... mingle; hobby poster pairs; frequency line-up game
Project: Green March timeline posters, presented in the past simple.
weeks.hw:
5 sentences about your free time
Write 5 past-simple sentences about the Green March.

skills.L: Listen to free-time habits with frequency adverbs
skills.S: Talk about hobbies with like + -ing and adverbs
skills.R: Read hobby profiles and match them to people
skills.W: Write my free-time habits (3 sentences)

lp.wu: Hobby Charades: Teacher writes 5 hobbies on the board (e.g., play football, listen to music, read books, watch TV, cook). Students take turns acting out a hobby while others guess, saying 'He/She likes...' or 'He/She is playing...'.
wuAlt: Hobby Pictionary: Students draw a hobby on the board for others to guess, using 'He/She is...'.
Find My Match: Teacher gives each student a hobby picture; they mingle to find another student with the same picture and say 'I like...'.
lp.pres: Teacher shows flashcards of hobbies and models sentences: 'I like playing football. I love listening to music. I hate watching TV.' Then introduces adverbs: 'I always play football on Fridays. I sometimes listen to music. I never watch TV.' Checks understanding with thumbs up/down: 'Do you like swimming?'
presAlt: Hobby Survey: Teacher asks 3 students about their hobbies, writing their answers on the board to model the structure.
Green March Video: Shows a short clip of the Green March, pauses, and asks 'Did they like walking? Did they always walk?' to connect to past simple.
lp.prac: Find Someone Who...: Students get a grid with hobbies (e.g., play football, read books). They mingle asking 'Do you like...?' and write names. Teacher monitors for correct use of like + -ing and adverbs.
pracAlt: Hobby Poster Pairs: Students draw 3 hobbies in pairs and label them with 'I like/love/hate + -ing'.
Frequency Line-Up: Teacher gives cards with adverbs (always, sometimes, never); students line up from most to least frequent and say a sentence with their card.
lp.ls: Listen to 3 teens talking about their free time. Students tick the hobbies they hear and circle the adverbs (always, sometimes, never). Teacher plays audio twice, then checks answers as a class.
lp.re: Hobby Relay: Two lines of students. Teacher calls a hobby (e.g., 'play football'), first student runs to the board, writes 'I like playing football', runs back, tags next. Team with correct sentences wins.
lp.prod: Green March Timeline Poster: In pairs, students create a poster with 3 pictures of the Green March (e.g., walking, singing, waving flags). They write 3 past simple sentences: 'They walked to the city. They sang songs. They waved flags.' Then present to the class.
lp.rw: Read 3 short hobby profiles (e.g., 'I am Amina. I like reading books. I never play sports.'). Students match each profile to a picture. Then write 3 sentences about their own free time using 'I like/love/hate + -ing' and an adverb.
lp.st: Sing 'What Do You Like to Do?' song with actions. Then close with: 'Today we talked about hobbies using like + -ing and adverbs. Thank you, class! Goodbye!'
g: Students get a bingo grid with hobbies; teacher calls out 'I like playing football' and students mark the square.
Students act out hobbies for others to guess using 'He/She likes...'.
Students mingle asking 'Do you like...?' and write names on a grid.
Students line up with adverb cards from 'always' to 'never' and say a sentence.
Pairs create a poster with past simple sentences about the Green March.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 more sentences about the Green March using different verbs.
Support learners: Use sentence starters like 'I like...' and 'I sometimes...' on their poster.
hw: Write 5 sentences about your free time using 'I like/love/hate + -ing' and an adverb.
Write 5 past-simple sentences about the Green March (e.g., 'They walked. They sang.').
Draw a picture of your favorite hobby and write 2 sentences about it.
lp.tip: Use the Green March theme to connect to local culture and build pride, while practicing past simple. Teens respond well to real-world topics like national history.

weeks.obj: say what they can and can't do; hold a short can-can't interview
weeks.lang: can/can't for ability; adverbs (well, fast)
weeks.act: Class olympics quiz; talent show circle; can-can't guessing game with teams
weeks.hw: Note: short written check next week

skills.L: Listen to can/can't mini-interviews
skills.S: Hold a can-can't interview with a partner
skills.R: Read ability profiles and complete the grid (Worksheets)
skills.W: Write 3 can / can't sentences about me

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'Stand if You Can' game. Teacher calls out sports (e.g., 'Run!'), students stand if they can do it. Teacher models: 'I can run.' Students repeat. Teacher calls 'Swim!', students sit if they can't. Teacher models: 'I can't swim.'
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Simon Says' with can/cant commands (e.g., 'Simon says: You can jump!')
Alternative 2: Quick survey: 'Ask 3 classmates: Can you play football?'. Tally results on board.
lp.pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of sports (football, swim, run). Teacher models: 'I can play football.' Point to self. Then shows a sport they can't do (e.g., ice skate). Models: 'I can't ice skate.' Students repeat sentences chorally. Check: 'Can I play football?' (Yes!) 'Can I ice skate?' (No!)
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a story about a character who can/can't do sports. Draw stick figures on board.
Alternative 2: Bring in a real football. Teacher demonstrates 'I can kick the ball.' Then tries to juggle and says 'I can't juggle.'
lp.prac: Guided practice: 'Can-Can't Relay' in teams. Teams race to write sentences on board: 'I can swim.' 'I can't play tennis.' Teacher monitors for accuracy. Support: Give sentence starters on board.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Matching Pairs' worksheet. Match sports to can/cant sentences.
Alternative 2: 'Chain Drill'. Student 1: 'I can run.' Student 2: 'He can run. I can swim.'
lp.ls: Listening slot: Students listen to 3 short interviews (audio recording) about sports. They complete a grid: 'Name / Can do / Can't do'. Check answers as class.
lp.re: Reactivation game: 'Freeze Dance'. Play music, students dance. When music stops, teacher calls: 'Freeze! Can you jump?' Students jump if they can. If not, freeze.
lp.prod: Production task: 'Talent Show Circle'. Students stand in a circle. Each student says: 'My name is [name]. I can [skill]. I can't [skill].' (e.g., 'I can sing. I can't dance.')
lp.rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read 3 short ability profiles (e.g., 'Fatima: She can cook. She can't swim.'). They complete a grid with names and skills. Then write 3 sentences about themselves: 'I can... I can't...'
lp.st: Story / song + goodbye: Sing 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' with can/cant twist (e.g., 'Can you touch your nose?'). Close with: 'Today we learned to say what we can and can't do. Thank you, class!'
g: Teams answer quiz questions: 'Who can swim? A) Ali B) Sara'
One student acts a sport, others guess: 'Can you play football?'
Student mimes a sport, others guess: 'Can you run?'
Students walk around asking: 'Can you play basketball?' and write names
Students write 9 abilities in grid. Teacher calls: 'Can you swim?' Students mark if they can.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 can/cant sentences about a famous athlete.
Support: Use picture prompts for writing sentences (e.g., a picture of a football for 'I can play football.')
hw: Option 1: Interview a family member: 'Can you cook? Can you drive?' Write 3 sentences.
Option 2: Draw 3 things you can do and 3 you can't. Label them in English.
Option 3: Complete the worksheet: 'My Sports Skills'.
lp.tip: Use local sports like football and athletics to make it relevant. Encourage peer correction gently during the talent show to build confidence.

weeks.obj: understand a short Halloween text and exchange themed vocabulary
weeks.lang: Halloween vocabulary; there is/there are (spooky room descriptions)
weeks.act:
Spooky room description pairs; Halloween word games; short reading with questions
Project: 18 November 1955 - timeline cards and a mini museum walk with captions.
weeks.hw:
Optional: bring a themed word to teach
Write a short paragraph: what independence means to me.

skills.L: Listen to a spooky description and draw the room
skills.S: Exchange Halloween vocabulary in themed games
skills.R: Read a short Halloween text and answer the questions (Reading tasks)
skills.W: Write 3 there is / there are spooky sentences

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'Two Truths and a Lie' - Students write three sentences about Halloween: two true (e.g., 'I like pumpkin pie'), one false (e.g., 'I am a vampire'). In pairs, they guess the lie.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Halloween Pictionary' - Teacher draws Halloween words, students guess.
Alternative 2: 'Word Association' - Teacher says 'Halloween', students say related words.
lp.pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of Halloween items (bat, witch, pumpkin, ghost). Model sentences: 'There is a bat.' 'There are two ghosts.' Check understanding by asking 'What is in the picture?' and having students repeat.
presAlt: Alternative 1: 'Spooky Story' - Tell a short story using target vocabulary, e.g., 'In the room, there is a big pumpkin and a black cat.'
Alternative 2: 'Realia Hunt' - Hide small Halloween toys in the classroom, students find them and say 'There is a...'
lp.prac: Guided practice: 'Spooky Room Description Pairs' - Student A describes a picture with 'there is/there are' (e.g., 'There is a spider on the wall. There are three candles.'). Student B draws. Swap roles.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Memory Game' - Students take turns adding to a spooky room description (e.g., 'There is a ghost.' 'There is a ghost and a spider.')
Alternative 2: 'Find the Differences' - Students compare two similar spooky room pictures and say 'There is a... in picture 1 but not in picture 2.'
lp.ls: Listening slot: Students listen to a description of a spooky room (e.g., 'There is a black cat. There are three bats. There is a big pumpkin.'). They draw what they hear. Teacher checks drawings for comprehension.
lp.re: Reactivation game: 'Halloween Charades' - Students act out Halloween words (witch, ghost, spider) while others guess. After the break, this brings the vocabulary back physically.
lp.prod: Production task: 'Spooky Room Project' - In pairs, students design a spooky room on paper. They write three sentences using 'there is/there are' to describe it. They present their room to the class.
lp.rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read a short text about Halloween (e.g., 'Halloween is on October 31st. People wear costumes. There are pumpkins and ghosts.'). They answer 2-3 simple questions (e.g., 'What date is Halloween?'). Then, they write three 'there is/there are' sentences about their own spooky room.
lp.st: Story / song + goodbye: Sing 'Five Little Pumpkins' song. Close with 'Today we learned Halloween vocabulary and how to describe a spooky room with there is/there are. Thank you, class!'
g: Students mark Halloween words on their bingo cards as the teacher calls them.
In teams, race to write as many Halloween words as possible in 2 minutes.
Students add one sentence to a collaborative spooky story.
Students draw Halloween words for their team to guess.
Teacher hides flashcards, students find and say 'There is a...'
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a longer description of a spooky room with five sentences.
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank with Halloween vocabulary to write their sentences.
hw: Homework option 1: Write a short paragraph: 'What independence means to me.'
Homework option 2: Bring one Halloween-themed word to teach the class next week.
Homework option 3: Draw a spooky room and label the items in English.
lp.tip: Use the local context of Independence Day (18 November 1955) to connect Halloween's spooky fun with themes of history and national identity, making the lesson culturally relevant for Moroccan learners.

weeks.obj: categorize food vocabulary and ask about quantities
weeks.lang: countable/uncountable; some/any; How much/How many
weeks.act:
Food categories team race; shopping list game; some/any worksheet relay
Compare Thanksgiving with harvest customs here; gratitude survey with graphs.
weeks.hw:
Short written check (10 items)
Interview 3 people: one thing they are thankful for; report back.

skills.L: Listen to a shopping dialogue and spot some / any
skills.S: Categorize food and ask How much / How many
skills.R: Read a food text and find the countables (Lesson Plans/Food)
skills.W: Write my shopping list with some / any

lp.wu: Warm-up: 'Food Categories Race'. Teacher writes 4 columns on the board: Fruit, Vegetables, Drinks, Other. Students in teams take turns running to the board and writing one food word per category. Fastest team with correct words wins.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'I Spy with My Little Eye' - Teacher says 'I spy something you eat for breakfast', students guess using 'Is it...?'
Alternative 2: 'Mime the Food' - Students mime a food/drink, others guess 'Are you eating/drinking...?'
lp.pres: Presentation: Show flashcards of Thanksgiving foods (turkey, pumpkin pie, potatoes, cranberry sauce). Model: 'How many potatoes?' 'Some potatoes.' 'How much cranberry sauce?' 'Some cranberry sauce.' Elicit countable/uncountable. Check with thumbs up/down: 'Is potato countable?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use realia (apple, bread, milk) to demonstrate countable/uncountable.
Alternative 2: Draw a simple market scene on the board and ask 'How much...? How many...?'
lp.prac: Guided practice: 'Shopping List Relay'. Teams get a list with gaps (e.g., '___ apples, ___ milk'). One student runs to the board, writes 'some' or 'any', then next student adds the word. Teacher monitors for accuracy.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Fill in the Blanks' worksheet with pictures of food, students write 'some/any'.
Alternative 2: 'Pair Drill' - Student A asks 'How many...?', Student B answers 'Some.../Any...?'
lp.ls: Listening slot: Play a short dialogue between two friends planning a Thanksgiving meal. Students listen and circle 'some' or 'any' on their worksheet (e.g., 'Do we have ___ potatoes?').
lp.re: Reactivation game: 'Stand Up If You Like...'. Teacher calls out foods (e.g., 'Stand up if you like pizza!'), students stand and say 'I like some pizza!' or 'I don't like any pizza!'
lp.prod: Production task: 'Thanksgiving vs. Moroccan Harvest Survey'. Students in pairs interview 3 classmates: 'What food do you eat for Eid al-Adha? How much...? How many...?' They graph results and present to the class.
lp.rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read a short text about a typical Thanksgiving meal. They underline all countable nouns. Then, they write 3 sentences about their family's meal using 'some/any'.
lp.st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Sing 'Thanksgiving Food Song' (tune: 'Frère Jacques'). Close with: 'Today we learned to ask about quantities with How much/How many and some/any. Thank you, class!'
g: Teams write food words in columns: Fruit, Vegetables, Drinks, Other.
Teams fill gaps with 'some/any' and food words on the board.
Students stand and say 'I like some...' when a food is called.
Interview classmates about Eid al-Adha food and graph results.
Students sort picture cards into countable/uncountable piles.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 more sentences about their ideal Thanksgiving meal.
Support: Use a word bank with 'some/any' and food words for the writing task.
hw: Homework 1: Complete a 10-item worksheet on countable/uncountable nouns.
Homework 2: Interview 3 people: 'What are you thankful for?' and report back.
Homework 3: Write a short paragraph about your family's favorite food using 'some/any'.
lp.tip: Teach 'some/any' through visual aids (full/empty containers) to make the abstract concept concrete for beginners. Connect to Moroccan harvest customs to build cultural relevance.

weeks.obj: order food and drink politely in a roleplay
weeks.lang: Would you like...? I'd like...; Can I have...?
weeks.res: Listening (graded cafe dialogues mp3); Lesson Plans/Food
weeks.act: Cafe roleplay with menus made in class; waiter rotation; dialogue listening gap-fill
weeks.hw: write your ideal menu

skills.L: Listening folder: cafe dialogues - order and confirm
skills.S: Cafe roleplay: order, ask and pay politely
skills.R: Read a cafe menu and match dishes to sections
skills.W: Write my own cafe dialogue (6 lines)
